#### Multi-variable Assessment

```{r variable-assessment, results='asis', fig.show='hold', out.width='32%'}
selected_assessment_vars <- c(
    "Developmental_Stage",
    "Scientific_Name",
    "Cultivar",
    "study_alias",
    "Author"
)

selected_assessment_vars <- intersect(selected_assessment_vars, colnames(sample_data(ps_beta_genus)))

safe_file_label <- function(x) {
    x <- iconv(x, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
    x <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x)
    x <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", x)
    tolower(x)
}

clean_group_values <- function(x) {
    x <- iconv(as.character(x), from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "")
    x[x == "" | is.na(x)] <- NA_character_
    x
}

named_variable_palette <- function(levels, context = "alpha_diversity") {
    levels <- sort(unique(levels))
    pal <- get_palette(length(levels), "wildagain", context)
    if (length(pal) < length(levels)) {
        pal <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(POISON_FROG_GRADIENT)(length(levels))
    }
    names(pal) <- levels
    pal
}

prepare_variable_samples <- function(ps, variable, min_group_n = 3) {
    meta_df <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
    meta_df$sample_id <- rownames(meta_df)
    meta_df$group <- clean_group_values(meta_df[[variable]])
    meta_df <- meta_df[!is.na(meta_df$group), , drop = FALSE]

    group_counts <- meta_df |>
        dplyr::count(group, name = "n") |>
        dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n), group)

    keep_groups <- group_counts$group[group_counts$n >= min_group_n]
    meta_keep <- meta_df[meta_df$group %in% keep_groups, , drop = FALSE]

    list(
        metadata = meta_keep,
        group_counts = group_counts,
        kept_groups = keep_groups,
        status = if (length(keep_groups) >= 2 && nrow(meta_keep) >= 4) "ready" else "skipped_sparse"
    )
}

plot_variable_alpha <- function(alpha_df, variable, output_dir) {
    safe_var <- safe_file_label(variable)
    n_groups <- dplyr::n_distinct(alpha_df$group)
    pal <- named_variable_palette(alpha_df$group, "alpha_diversity")
    plot_width <- max(8, min(16, n_groups * 0.45 + 5))

    p_obs <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes(x = group, y = Observed, fill = group)) +
        geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA) +
        geom_jitter(aes(color = group), width = 0.15, size = 1.2, alpha = 0.95) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
        scale_color_manual(values = pal) +
        labs(x = variable, y = "Observed ASV Richness",
             title = paste("Observed ASV Richness by", variable)) +
        theme_pipeline_classic() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")

    p_sh <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes(x = group, y = Shannon, fill = group)) +
        geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA) +
        geom_jitter(aes(color = group), width = 0.15, size = 1.2, alpha = 0.95) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
        scale_color_manual(values = pal) +
        labs(x = variable, y = "Shannon Diversity Index",
             title = paste("Shannon Diversity by", variable)) +
        theme_pipeline_classic() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")

    if ("Developmental_Stage" %in% colnames(alpha_df) && variable != "Developmental_Stage") {
        p_obs <- p_obs + facet_wrap(~Developmental_Stage, scales = "free_x")
        p_sh <- p_sh + facet_wrap(~Developmental_Stage, scales = "free_x")
    }

    ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("alpha_observed_by_", safe_var, ".tiff")),
           p_obs, width = plot_width, height = 5.2, dpi = 300)
    ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("alpha_shannon_by_", safe_var, ".tiff")),
           p_sh, width = plot_width, height = 5.2, dpi = 300)
}

plot_variable_pcoa <- function(dist_sub, meta_sub, variable, output_dir) {
    safe_var <- safe_file_label(variable)
    pcoa_result <- cmdscale(dist_sub, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
    var_explained <- round(pcoa_result$eig / sum(pcoa_result$eig) * 100, 2)
    pcoa_df <- data.frame(
        sample_id = rownames(pcoa_result$points),
        PCoA1 = pcoa_result$points[, 1],
        PCoA2 = pcoa_result$points[, 2],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ) |>
        dplyr::left_join(
            meta_sub[, intersect(c("sample_id", "group", "Developmental_Stage"), colnames(meta_sub)), drop = FALSE],
            by = "sample_id"
        )

    n_groups <- dplyr::n_distinct(pcoa_df$group)
    pal <- named_variable_palette(pcoa_df$group, "beta_diversity")

    p <- ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = group)) +
        geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.95) +
        scale_color_manual(values = pal) +
        labs(
            x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_explained[1], "%)"),
            y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_explained[2], "%)"),
            color = variable,
            title = paste("Genus-level Bray-Curtis community clustering by", variable)
        ) +
        theme_pipeline_classic() +
        theme(legend.position = "right") +
        guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

    pcoa_uses_stage_facets <- "Developmental_Stage" %in% colnames(pcoa_df)
    if (pcoa_uses_stage_facets) {
        p <- p + facet_wrap(~Developmental_Stage, nrow = 1)
    }

    pcoa_kind <- if (pcoa_uses_stage_facets) "wide" else "standard"
    save_nature_figure(file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_bray_genus_by_", safe_var, ".tiff")),
                       p, kind = pcoa_kind)
    readr::write_csv(pcoa_df, file.path(output_dir, paste0("pcoa_bray_genus_by_", safe_var, ".csv")))
}

subset_stage_for_pcoa <- function(meta_df, stages = c("Seeds", "Seedlings")) {
    stage_col <- "Developmental_Stage"
    if (!stage_col %in% colnames(meta_df)) {
        return(meta_df)
    }

    meta_df |>
        dplyr::filter(.data[[stage_col]] %in% stages) |>
        dplyr::mutate(
            Developmental_Stage = factor(.data[[stage_col]], levels = stages)
        )
}

subset_phyloseq_to_stages <- function(ps_obj, stages = c("Seeds", "Seedlings")) {
    stage_col <- "Developmental_Stage"
    if (!stage_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps_obj))) {
        return(ps_obj)
    }

    ps_sub <- subset_samples(ps_obj, Developmental_Stage %in% c("Seeds", "Seedlings"))
    prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
}

drop_invalid_distance_samples <- function(dist_obj, meta_df) {
    dist_mat <- as.matrix(dist_obj)
    keep_ids <- intersect(rownames(dist_mat), meta_df$sample_id)
    dist_mat <- dist_mat[keep_ids, keep_ids, drop = FALSE]
    meta_df <- meta_df[match(keep_ids, meta_df$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]

    if (nrow(dist_mat) == 0 || nrow(meta_df) == 0) {
        return(list(dist = as.dist(matrix(numeric(0), nrow = 0, ncol = 0)), meta = meta_df))
    }

    bad_rows <- apply(dist_mat, 1, function(x) any(!is.finite(x)))
    bad_groups <- is.na(meta_df$group)
    keep <- !(bad_rows | bad_groups)
    dist_mat <- dist_mat[keep, keep, drop = FALSE]
    meta_df <- meta_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]

    list(dist = as.dist(dist_mat), meta = meta_df)
}

assess_metadata_variable <- function(ps_alpha, variable,
                                     beta_stats_dist, pcoa_bray_dist,
                                     figures_dir, diversity_dir, tables_dir,
                                     min_group_n = 3) {
    use_stage_subset <- variable != "Developmental_Stage"
    ps_alpha_use <- if (use_stage_subset) subset_phyloseq_to_stages(ps_alpha) else ps_alpha

    prepared <- prepare_variable_samples(ps_alpha_use, variable, min_group_n = min_group_n)
    counts_tbl <- prepared$group_counts |>
        dplyr::mutate(variable = variable, kept = group %in% prepared$kept_groups, .before = 1)

    if (prepared$status != "ready") {
        return(list(
            status = prepared$status,
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = tibble::tibble(),
            beta = tibble::tibble()
        ))
    }

    meta_sub <- prepared$metadata
    sample_ids <- meta_sub$sample_id

    rich <- phyloseq::estimate_richness(ps_alpha_use, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon"))
    alpha_df <- data.frame(sample_id = rownames(rich), rich, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::inner_join(
            meta_sub[, intersect(c("sample_id", "group", "Developmental_Stage"), colnames(meta_sub)), drop = FALSE],
            by = "sample_id"
        )

    alpha_tests <- tibble::tibble(
        variable = variable,
        metric = c("Observed", "Shannon"),
        test = "Kruskal-Wallis",
        statistic = c(
            unname(kruskal.test(Observed ~ group, data = alpha_df)$statistic),
            unname(kruskal.test(Shannon ~ group, data = alpha_df)$statistic)
        ),
        p_value = c(
            kruskal.test(Observed ~ group, data = alpha_df)$p.value,
            kruskal.test(Shannon ~ group, data = alpha_df)$p.value
        ),
        n_samples = nrow(alpha_df),
        n_groups = dplyr::n_distinct(alpha_df$group)
    )

    plot_variable_alpha(alpha_df, variable, figures_dir)

    beta_sample_ids <- intersect(sample_ids, labels(beta_stats_dist))
    if (length(beta_sample_ids) < 4) {
        return(list(
            status = "skipped_sparse",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = tibble::tibble()
        ))
    }

    dist_matrix <- as.matrix(beta_stats_dist)
    beta_meta <- data.frame(
        group = factor(meta_sub$group[match(beta_sample_ids, meta_sub$sample_id)]),
        sample_id = beta_sample_ids,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    beta_clean <- drop_invalid_distance_samples(
        as.dist(dist_matrix[beta_sample_ids, beta_sample_ids, drop = FALSE]),
        beta_meta
    )
    dist_sub <- beta_clean$dist
    beta_meta <- beta_clean$meta

    if (nrow(beta_meta) < 4 || dplyr::n_distinct(beta_meta$group) < 2) {
        return(list(
            status = "skipped_sparse",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = tibble::tibble()
        ))
    }

    n_perm <- config$analysis$permutations
    if (is.null(n_perm)) n_perm <- 999
    set.seed(123)
    permanova_result <- vegan::adonis2(
        dist_sub ~ group,
        data = beta_meta,
        permutations = n_perm,
        parallel = parallel_config$n_threads
    )

    set.seed(123)
    disp_result <- vegan::betadisper(dist_sub, beta_meta$group)
    disp_test <- vegan::permutest(
        disp_result,
        permutations = n_perm,
        parallel = parallel_config$n_threads
    )

    beta_tests <- tibble::tibble(
        variable = variable,
        method = c("PERMANOVA", "PERMDISP"),
        distance = "bray_asv",
        statistic = c(
            unname(as.data.frame(permanova_result)[1, "F"]),
            unname(disp_test$tab[1, "F"])
        ),
        r2 = c(unname(as.data.frame(permanova_result)[1, "R2"]), NA_real_),
        p_value = c(
            unname(as.data.frame(permanova_result)[1, "Pr(>F)"]),
            unname(disp_test$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"])
        ),
        n_samples = length(beta_sample_ids),
        n_groups = dplyr::n_distinct(beta_meta$group)
    )

    pcoa_meta_sub <- subset_stage_for_pcoa(meta_sub)
    pcoa_sample_ids <- intersect(pcoa_meta_sub$sample_id, labels(pcoa_bray_dist))

    if (length(pcoa_sample_ids) < 4 || dplyr::n_distinct(pcoa_meta_sub$group) < 2) {
        return(list(
            status = "completed_no_pcoa",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = beta_tests
        ))
    }

    pcoa_dist_matrix <- as.matrix(pcoa_bray_dist)
    pcoa_meta_sub <- pcoa_meta_sub[match(pcoa_sample_ids, pcoa_meta_sub$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
    pcoa_clean <- drop_invalid_distance_samples(
        as.dist(pcoa_dist_matrix[pcoa_sample_ids, pcoa_sample_ids, drop = FALSE]),
        pcoa_meta_sub
    )
    pcoa_dist_sub <- pcoa_clean$dist
    pcoa_meta_sub <- pcoa_clean$meta

    if (nrow(pcoa_meta_sub) < 4 || dplyr::n_distinct(pcoa_meta_sub$group) < 2) {
        return(list(
            status = "completed_no_pcoa",
            counts = counts_tbl,
            alpha = alpha_tests,
            beta = beta_tests
        ))
    }

    plot_variable_pcoa(pcoa_dist_sub, pcoa_meta_sub, variable, diversity_dir)

    list(
        status = "completed",
        counts = counts_tbl,
        alpha = alpha_tests,
        beta = beta_tests
    )
}
```

#### UMAP Representation (wild-again utils/UMAP approach)

```{r umap}
compute_umap <- function(ps, group_col = NULL, output_dir) {
    if (!requireNamespace("umap", quietly = TRUE)) {
        cat("UMAP package not installed, skipping\n")
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_umap"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        # Transform count data
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) {
            otu <- t(otu)
        }

        # Apply CLR transformation
        otu_clr <- microbiome::transform(otu, "clr")

        # Remove NA columns (if any)
        otu_clr <- otu_clr[, colSums(is.na(otu_clr)) == 0]

        # Run UMAP
        umap_result <- umap::umap(otu_clr, n_components = 2)

        # Create data frame
        umap_df <- data.frame(
            Sample = rownames(otu_clr),
            UMAP1 = umap_result$layout[, 1],
            UMAP2 = umap_result$layout[, 2],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

        # Add metadata
        if (!is.null(group_col) && group_col %in% colnames(sample_data(ps))) {
            meta_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ps))
            umap_df <- merge(umap_df, meta_df, by.x = "Sample", by.y = "row.names", all.x = TRUE)
        }

        # Plot
        p <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = .data[[group_col]])) +
            geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.95) +
            labs(
                x = "UMAP1",
                y = "UMAP2",
                color = group_col,
                title = "UMAP Ordination (CLR-transformed)"
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "right") +
            guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1))

        # Save
        save_nature_figure(file.path(output_dir, "umap.tiff"), p, kind = "standard")
        write.csv(umap_df, file.path(output_dir, "umap_data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

        list(status = "completed", n_samples = nrow(umap_df))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("UMAP error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    cat("Computing UMAP...\n")
    umap_result <- compute_umap(ps_beta, group_col, figures_dir)
    cat("  UMAP:", umap_result$status, "\n")
}
```

### Differential Abundance Analysis (DESeq2)

```{r deseq2}
run_deseq2 <- function(ps, group_col, g1, g2, output_path) {
    if (!requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly = TRUE)) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_missing_deseq2"))
    }
    
    tryCatch({
        sd <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        if (!(group_col %in% colnames(sd))) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_no_group_column"))
        }
        
        keep <- sd[[group_col]] %in% c(g1, g2)
        if (sum(keep) < 4) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_too_few_samples"))
        }
        
        ps_sub <- prune_samples(keep, ps)
        # Samples with zero total counts give NA size factors and abort
        # estimateSizeFactors(type = "poscounts") with
        # "all(!is.na(value)) is not TRUE". Three such samples survive filtering here
        # - the same three for which Shannon is undefined (n = 1883, not 1886).
        n_before <- nsamples(ps_sub)
        ps_sub <- prune_samples(sample_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
        n_dropped <- n_before - nsamples(ps_sub)
        if (n_dropped > 0) {
            cat("  dropped", n_dropped, "zero-count sample(s) before DESeq2\n")
        }
        ps_sub <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_sub) > 0, ps_sub)
        
        sample_data(ps_sub)[[group_col]] <- factor(
            sample_data(ps_sub)[[group_col]],
            levels = c(g2, g1)
        )
        
        # DESeq2 wants countData as features x samples. A phyloseq otu_table may be
        # stored either way, so transpose only when taxa are NOT already the rows -
        # an unconditional t() here silently failed every run with
        # "ncol(countData) == nrow(colData) is not TRUE" and left
        # differential_abundance/ empty.
        otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_sub), "matrix")
        if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_sub)) otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

        dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
            countData = otu_mat,
            colData = data.frame(sample_data(ps_sub)),
            design = as.formula(paste("~", group_col))
        )
        dds <- DESeq2::estimateSizeFactors(dds, type = "poscounts")
        dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
        
        res <- DESeq2::results(dds, contrast = c(group_col, g1, g2))
        res_df <- as.data.frame(res)
        res_df$feature_id <- rownames(res_df)
        res_df <- res_df[order(res_df$padj), ]
        
        write.csv(res_df, output_path, row.names = FALSE)
        list(
            status = "completed",
            n_features = nrow(res_df),
            n_significant = sum(res_df$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
    }, error = function(e) {
        # cat() not message(): the YAML sets `message: false`, so message() output is
        # discarded and a failure here shows only as status "failed" with no reason.
        cat("  DESeq2 error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

da_groups <- config$differential_abundance$groups
group_col <- config$analysis$primary_group

if (!is.null(da_groups) && length(da_groups) == 2) {
    cat("Running DESeq2 (", da_groups[1], "vs", da_groups[2], ")...\n")
    deseq2_result <- run_deseq2(
        ps, group_col, da_groups[1], da_groups[2],
        file.path(da_dir, "deseq2_results.csv")
    )
    cat("  DESeq2:", deseq2_result$status, "\n")
    if (deseq2_result$status == "completed") {
        cat("  Features:", deseq2_result$n_features, "\n")
        cat("  Significant (padj < 0.05):", deseq2_result$n_significant, "\n")
    }
} else {
    cat("No differential abundance groups specified, skipping DESeq2\n")
    deseq2_result <- list(status = "skipped_no_groups")
}
```

### Volcano Plot (DESeq2 Results)

```{r volcano-plot}
plot_volcano <- function(ps, deseq2_result, da_dir, figures_dir) {
    if (is.null(deseq2_result) || deseq2_result$status != "completed") {
        return(list(status = "skipped_no_deseq2"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        res_path <- file.path(da_dir, "deseq2_results.csv")
        if (!file.exists(res_path)) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_no_results_file"))
        }

        res_df <- readr::read_csv(res_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

        # Add genus labels from taxonomy
        tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        res_df <- res_df |>
            dplyr::mutate(
                genus = dplyr::if_else(
                    feature_id %in% rownames(tax_df),
                    tax_df[feature_id, "Genus"],
                    feature_id
                ),
                genus = dplyr::if_else(is.na(genus) | genus == "", feature_id, genus)
            )

        # Classify direction
        res_df <- res_df |>
            dplyr::mutate(
                direction = dplyr::case_when(
                    is.na(padj) ~ "NS",
                    padj >= 0.05 ~ "NS",
                    log2FoldChange > 1 ~ "Up",
                    log2FoldChange < -1 ~ "Down",
                    .default = "NS"
                ),
                direction = factor(direction, levels = c("Up", "Down", "NS"))
            )

        direction_colors <- c("Up" = "#ce232a", "Down" = "#447099", "NS" = "grey70")

        # Top significant taxa for labelling
        top_sig <- res_df |>
            dplyr::filter(direction != "NS") |>
            dplyr::arrange(padj) |>
            head(15)

        p <- ggplot(res_df, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = direction)) +
            geom_point(alpha = 0.95, size = 1.5) +
            geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
            geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
            scale_color_manual(values = direction_colors) +
            ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
                data = top_sig,
                aes(label = genus),
                size = 3, max.overlaps = 20, show.legend = FALSE
            ) +
            labs(
                x = "log2 Fold Change",
                y = "-log10(adjusted p-value)",
                color = "Direction",
                title = "Volcano Plot (DESeq2)"
            ) +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom")

        save_nature_figure(file.path(figures_dir, "volcano_deseq2.tiff"),
                           p, kind = "standard")

        n_up <- sum(res_df$direction == "Up", na.rm = TRUE)
        n_down <- sum(res_df$direction == "Down", na.rm = TRUE)
        cat("  Volcano plot: Up =", n_up, ", Down =", n_down, "\n")

        list(status = "completed", n_up = n_up, n_down = n_down)
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Volcano plot error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Generating volcano plot...\n")
volcano_result <- plot_volcano(ps, deseq2_result, da_dir, figures_dir)
cat("  Volcano:", volcano_result$status, "\n")
```

### ANCOM-BC2 Differential Abundance

```{r ancombc}
run_ancombc2 <- function(ps, group_col, output_path) {
    if (!requireNamespace("microbiomeMarker", quietly = TRUE)) {
        return(list(status = "skipped_missing_package"))
    }

    tryCatch({
        sd <- data.frame(sample_data(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        if (!(group_col %in% colnames(sd))) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_no_group_column"))
        }

        groups <- unique(na.omit(sd[[group_col]]))
        if (length(groups) < 2) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_fewer_than_2_groups"))
        }

        # Run ANCOM-BC2
        ancom_result <- microbiomeMarker::run_ancombc2(
            ps,
            group = group_col,
            p_adj_cutoff = 0.05,
            pairwise = FALSE
        )

        # Extract results
        res_df <- as.data.frame(microbiomeMarker::marker_table(ancom_result))

        if (nrow(res_df) > 0) {
            # Add taxonomy labels
            tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
            res_df <- res_df |>
                dplyr::mutate(
                    genus = dplyr::if_else(
                        feature %in% rownames(tax_df),
                        tax_df[feature, "Genus"],
                        feature
                    ),
                    genus = dplyr::if_else(is.na(genus) | genus == "", feature, genus)
                )
        }

        readr::write_csv(res_df, output_path)

        list(
            status = "completed",
            n_features = nrow(res_df),
            n_significant = sum(res_df$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("ANCOM-BC2 error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Running ANCOM-BC2...\n")
if (!is.null(group_col)) {
    ancombc_result <- run_ancombc2(
        ps, group_col,
        file.path(da_dir, "ancombc2_results.csv")
    )
    cat("  ANCOM-BC2:", ancombc_result$status, "\n")
    if (ancombc_result$status == "completed") {
        cat("  Significant features:", ancombc_result$n_significant, "\n")
    }
} else {
    ancombc_result <- list(status = "skipped_no_group")
}
```

### Co-occurrence Network

```{r cooccurrence-network}
build_cooccurrence_network <- function(ps, group_col = NULL, top_n = 50,
                                        rho_threshold = 0.6, p_threshold = 0.05,
                                        figures_dir, tables_dir) {
    tryCatch({
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)

        # Relative abundance
        rel_abund <- sweep(otu, 1, rowSums(otu), "/")
        rel_abund[is.na(rel_abund)] <- 0

        # Select top N taxa by mean relative abundance
        mean_ra <- colMeans(rel_abund)
        top_idx <- order(mean_ra, decreasing = TRUE)[1:min(top_n, ncol(rel_abund))]
        top_matrix <- rel_abund[, top_idx, drop = FALSE]

        if (ncol(top_matrix) < 10) {
            return(list(status = "skipped_too_few_taxa"))
        }

        # Add genus labels
        tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        col_ids <- colnames(top_matrix)
        display_names <- col_ids
        if ("Genus" %in% colnames(tax_df)) {
            genus_labels <- tax_df[col_ids, "Genus"]
            genus_labels[is.na(genus_labels) | genus_labels == ""] <- col_ids[is.na(genus_labels) | genus_labels == ""]
            display_names <- genus_labels
        }

        # Pairwise Spearman correlations
        n_taxa <- ncol(top_matrix)
        edges <- list()
        for (i in seq_len(n_taxa - 1)) {
            for (j in (i + 1):n_taxa) {
                ct <- cor.test(top_matrix[, i], top_matrix[, j], method = "spearman",
                               exact = FALSE)
                edges[[length(edges) + 1]] <- data.frame(
                    taxon1 = display_names[i],
                    taxon2 = display_names[j],
                    taxon1_id = col_ids[i],
                    taxon2_id = col_ids[j],
                    rho = ct$estimate,
                    p_value = ct$p.value,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
                )
            }
        }

        edge_df <- purrr::list_rbind(edges)

        # BH correction
        edge_df$p_adj <- p.adjust(edge_df$p_value, method = "BH")

        # Filter significant edges
        sig_edges <- edge_df |>
            dplyr::filter(abs(rho) >= rho_threshold, p_adj < p_threshold)

        if (nrow(sig_edges) == 0) {
            cat("  No significant co-occurrence edges found\n")
            readr::write_csv(edge_df, file.path(tables_dir, "cooccurrence_edges.csv"))
            return(list(status = "completed_no_significant_edges", n_edges = 0))
        }

        # Build igraph network
        g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
            sig_edges[, c("taxon1", "taxon2")],
            directed = FALSE
        )
        igraph::E(g)$weight <- sig_edges$rho
        igraph::E(g)$color <- ifelse(sig_edges$rho > 0, "#ce232a", "#447099")
        igraph::E(g)$width <- abs(sig_edges$rho) * 3

        # Node properties
        igraph::V(g)$size <- igraph::degree(g) * 2 + 5
        igraph::V(g)$label.cex <- 0.7
        igraph::V(g)$color <- "#918bc0"
        igraph::V(g)$frame.color <- NA

        # Save plot
        tiff(file.path(figures_dir, "cooccurrence_network.tiff"),
            width = 10, height = 10, units = "in", res = 300)
        set.seed(123)
        plot(g,
             layout = igraph::layout_with_fr(g),
             main = paste0("Co-occurrence Network (|rho| >= ", rho_threshold,
                           ", n = ", igraph::ecount(g), " edges)"),
             vertex.label.color = "black",
             edge.curved = 0.1)
        legend("bottomleft",
               legend = c("Positive", "Negative"),
               col = c("#ce232a", "#447099"),
               lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.9)
        dev.off()

        # Save edge list
        readr::write_csv(sig_edges, file.path(tables_dir, "cooccurrence_edges.csv"))

        cat("  Network: ", igraph::vcount(g), " nodes, ",
            igraph::ecount(g), " edges\n")

        list(status = "completed",
             n_nodes = igraph::vcount(g),
             n_edges = igraph::ecount(g))
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Co-occurrence network error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Building co-occurrence network...\n")
cooccurrence_result <- build_cooccurrence_network(
    ps, group_col, top_n = 50,
    rho_threshold = 0.6, p_threshold = 0.05,
    figures_dir = figures_dir, tables_dir = tables_dir
)
cat("  Co-occurrence:", cooccurrence_result$status, "\n")
```

### Rarefaction Curves

```{r rarefaction}
rarefaction_curves <- function(ps, output_path, n_depths = 10) {
    tryCatch({
        otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
        if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)

        max_depth <- max(rowSums(otu))
        min_depth <- min(rowSums(otu))
        
        cat("  Sequencing depth range:", min_depth, "-", max_depth, "\n")
        
        # Use 10% of max depth as minimum, or 100, whichever is smaller
        start_depth <- max(10, min(min_depth, 100))
        depths <- unique(round(seq(start_depth, max_depth, length.out = n_depths)))

        results <- list()
        for (d in depths) {
            for (i in seq_len(nrow(otu))) {
                samp_counts <- otu[i, ]
                total <- sum(samp_counts)
                if (total < d) next

                rarefied <- rarefy(samp_counts, sample = d)
                results[[length(results) + 1]] <- data.frame(
                    sample_id = rownames(otu)[i],
                    depth = d,
                    expected_richness = as.numeric(rarefied),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
                )
            }
        }

        if (length(results) > 0) {
            rare_df <- purrr::list_rbind(results)
            write.csv(rare_df, output_path, row.names = FALSE)
            list(status = "completed", n_points = nrow(rare_df))
        } else {
            list(status = "skipped_no_data")
        }
    }, error = function(e) {
        message("Rarefaction error: ", conditionMessage(e))
        list(status = "failed", error = conditionMessage(e))
    })
}

cat("Computing rarefaction curves...\n")
rarefaction_result <- rarefaction_curves(
    ps, file.path(diversity_dir, "rarefaction_data.csv")
)
cat("  Rarefaction:", rarefaction_result$status, "\n")
```

### Performance Benchmark (run manually)

Times the two operations that dominate this pipeline's runtime on the current machine:
symmetric eigendecomposition (BLAS-bound; `betadisper` and PCoA) and `adonis2` at several
thread counts. It is **not run during a normal render** (`eval = FALSE`), because it
competes with the analysis for CPU. Run the chunk interactively when the machine is idle,
then set `analysis.threads` in `analysis_config.json` to the fastest row.

```{r performance-benchmark, eval = FALSE}
# Measure the two things that dominate this pipeline's runtime, so tuning decisions
# rest on numbers from this machine rather than on general advice.
#
#   Rscript tools/benchmark_performance.R [n_samples]
#
# Run it when nothing else heavy is running - a concurrent render will skew every
# timing here. Default n is 1886, the sample count of the real filtered object.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(vegan)
})

n <- 1886L   # sample count of the filtered object

si <- sessionInfo()
cat("== environment ==\n")
cat("  R         :", R.version.string, "\n")
cat("  platform  :", R.version$platform, "\n")
cat("  BLAS      :", basename(si$BLAS), "\n")
cat("  LAPACK    :", basename(si$LAPACK), "\n")
cat("  physical  :", system("sysctl -n hw.physicalcpu", intern = TRUE), "cores\n")
cat("  logical   :", system("sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu", intern = TRUE), "cores\n")
cat("  detectCores(logical=TRUE):", parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE), "\n\n")

# ── 1. BLAS-bound work ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# betadisper does a full PCoA internally and cmdscale eigendecomposes the whole
# distance matrix, so symmetric eigen at this size is a direct proxy for a large
# slice of the pipeline's cost. The reference libRblas is single-threaded;
# libRblas.vecLib.dylib (Apple Accelerate) is multithreaded and ships with R.
cat("== 1. symmetric eigendecomposition,", n, "x", n, "==\n")
set.seed(1)
m <- crossprod(matrix(rnorm(n * 200), nrow = 200))
t_eigen <- system.time(eigen(m, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE))[["elapsed"]]
cat(sprintf("  eigen(): %.1f s\n", t_eigen))
cat(sprintf("  matrix multiply %dx%d: %.1f s\n\n", n, n,
            system.time(m %*% m)[["elapsed"]]))

# ── 2. Permutation tests at varying thread counts ─────────────────────────────
# adonis2 and permutest take `parallel =`. More threads is not automatically
# faster: the 8 logical cores here are 4 physical cores with hyperthreading, and
# these permutations are memory-bandwidth bound.
cat("== 2. adonis2, 999 permutations, by thread count ==\n")
set.seed(1)
comm <- matrix(rpois(n * 100, 3), nrow = n)
grp <- factor(sample(c("Seeds", "Seedlings"), n, replace = TRUE))
d <- vegdist(comm, method = "bray")
df <- data.frame(group = grp)

for (th in unique(c(1L, 2L, 4L, parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE) - 1L))) {
    set.seed(123)
    el <- system.time(
        vegan::adonis2(d ~ group, data = df, permutations = 999, parallel = th)
    )[["elapsed"]]
    cat(sprintf("  parallel = %-2d : %6.1f s\n", th, el))
}

cat("\n== how to act on this ==\n")
cat("  * If BLAS is libRblas.0.dylib, switch to Apple Accelerate and re-run:\n")
cat("      cd /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib\n")
cat("      ln -sf libRblas.vecLib.dylib libRblas.dylib\n")
cat("    Revert with: ln -sf libRblas.0.dylib libRblas.dylib\n")
cat("  * Set analysis.threads in analysis_config.json to whichever row above wins.\n")
```


# Part 2 — All analysis figures

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## About this part
Every analysis figure, from `figures_all.qmd`. It reads the persisted outputs Part 1 just wrote rather than recomputing them, and wraps each figure in `fig_section()` so a missing input records a skip instead of aborting the render. Writes `tables/figure_manifest.csv`.
:::


## What this document is

Every figure in the project is generated here, and only here. It reads the
**persisted outputs** of the analysis pipeline rather than recomputing them, so it
renders in seconds and never touches the 609 MB count table:

| Input | Supplies |
| --- | --- |
| `setup/ps_clean.rds` | filtered phyloseq object (1,886 x 2,000) — alpha diversity, composition |
| `setup/ps0.rds` | pre-filter object — QC library sizes |
| `cache/{bray,jaccard}_distance.rds` | beta-diversity distances |
| `diversity/pcoa_*.csv` | ordination coordinates, metadata already joined |
| `diversity/rarefaction_data.csv`, `diversity/umap_data.csv` | rarefaction and UMAP |
| `tables/*.csv` | composition, indicator taxa, co-occurrence, correlations |
| `validation/supplementary/*.csv` | manuscript Fig 1–4 tables of record |

Run the pipeline first if any input is missing:

```
python3 microbiome_analysis.py --config analysis_config.json
quarto render phyloseq_analysis.qmd -P config:analysis_config.json
```

Every figure is wrapped in `fig_section()`, which reports a **skip** and carries on
when an input is absent — the same degrade-don't-fail rule the Python pipeline uses
for a missing `Rscript`. Nothing here recomputes statistics; `permanova_*`,
`permdisp_*` and the audit tables are read as the values of record.

```{r fx-setup}

    normalizePath(file.path(base_dir, configured_path), mustWork = FALSE)
}
```

```{r fx-palettes}
# Palette and themes lifted from phyloseq_analysis.R / phyloseq_analysis.qmd so
# figures produced here are visually identical to the pipeline's.
# Same thick palette as Part 1; seeds navy / seedlings vermillion as in Figure 1.
NATURE_THICK     <- c("#3C5488", "#E64B35", "#00A087", "#E6A700", "#6A3D9A", "#4DBBD5", "#7E6148", "#1B7837", "#D95F02", "#2166AC", "#E7298A", "#66A61E", "#8C510A", "#01665E")
PRIMARY_PELLET   <- NATURE_THICK[1:4]
CORE_PELLET      <- c("Biomarker" = "#E64B35", "Core" = "#3C5488", "Flexible" = "#00A087")
STAGE_PELLET     <- c("Seeds" = "#3C5488", "Seedlings" = "#E64B35")
PIPELINE_BAR_FILL <- "#3C5488"
INK <- "#1f1f1f"

get_palette <- function(n) {
    if (n <= length(PRIMARY_PELLET)) return(PRIMARY_PELLET[seq_len(n)])
    # Extend with thick colours, not the pastel RColorBrewer "Set3".
    rep(NATURE_THICK, length.out = n)
}

theme_nature_base <- function(base_size = 8) {
    theme_classic(base_size = base_size) %+replace%
        theme(
            text = element_text(colour = "black"),
            axis.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size),
            axis.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size - 1),
            legend.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size - 1),
            legend.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = base_size),
            strip.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1, face = "bold"),
            strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white"),
            panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.35),
            panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, colour = "#d9d9d9"),
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = base_size + 1),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size - 1),
            plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4)
        )
}
theme_pipeline_classic  <- function(base_size = 8) theme_nature_base(base_size)
theme_pipeline_faceted  <- function(base_size = 8) theme_nature_base(base_size)
theme_set(theme_nature_base())

figure_size <- function(kind = c("standard", "wide", "square", "tall", "compact")) {
    switch(match.arg(kind),
        standard = list(width = 7.0, height = 5.1),
        wide     = list(width = 8.8, height = 5.1),
        square   = list(width = 6.6, height = 6.0),
        tall     = list(width = 6.9, height = 7.0),
        compact  = list(width = 6.4, height = 4.6))
}

save_nature_figure <- function(filename, plot, kind = "standard", dpi = 300, ...) {
    dims <- figure_size(kind)
    # LZW is lossless, so the figures are bit-identical in content but a fraction of
    # the size. Uncompressed 300 dpi TIFFs were running 13-15 MB each, 449 MB total.
    ggsave(filename, plot, width = dims$width, height = dims$height, dpi = dpi,
           compression = "lzw", ...)
    invisible(filename)
}

safe_file_label <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x))
```

```{r fx-fig-registry}
# Every figure registers here. A section that cannot run records a skip and its
# reason instead of aborting the render, so one missing input never costs the
# other 36 figures.
FIG_LOG <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
FIG_LOG$rows <- list()

record <- function(name, status, reason = NA_character_, file = NA_character_) {
    FIG_LOG$rows[[length(FIG_LOG$rows) + 1]] <- tibble(
        figure = name, status = status, reason = reason,
        file = if (is.na(file)) NA_character_ else basename(file))
    invisible(NULL)
}

#' Run a figure block, requiring `needs` to exist first.
fig_section <- function(name, needs = character(), expr) {
    missing <- needs[!file.exists(needs)]
    if (length(missing)) {
        reason <- paste("missing:", paste(basename(missing), collapse = ", "))
        message("SKIP ", name, " - ", reason)
        record(name, "skipped", reason)
        return(invisible(NULL))
    }
    out <- tryCatch(force(expr), error = function(e) {
        message("FAIL ", name, " - ", conditionMessage(e))
        record(name, "failed", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
    })
    if (!is.null(out)) {
        record(name, "written", NA_character_, if (is.character(out)) out[1] else NA_character_)
        message("OK   ", name)
    }
    invisible(out)
}

fig <- function(name) file.path(FIGS, paste0(name, ".tiff"))
```

```{r fx-load-core}
PS_CLEAN <- res("setup", "ps_clean.rds")
PS0      <- res("setup", "ps0.rds")

ps <- if (file.exists(PS_CLEAN)) readRDS(PS_CLEAN) else NULL
if (!is.null(ps)) {
    # as.data.frame() on a sample_data object keeps the phyloseq class, which dplyr
    # verbs reject ("no applicable method for 'mutate'"). Coerce to a plain tibble.
    meta <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
    meta$sample_id <- rownames(meta)
    meta <- as_tibble(meta)
    cat(sprintf("ps_clean: %d samples x %d taxa\n", nsamples(ps), ntaxa(ps)))
} else {
    meta <- NULL
    cat("ps_clean.rds absent - object-derived figures will be skipped\n")
}

# Alpha diversity recomputed from the filtered object: tables/alpha_diversity.csv
# carries no sample id, so it cannot be joined to metadata for by-variable panels.
alpha <- NULL
if (!is.null(ps)) {
    rich <- estimate_richness(ps, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson"))
    alpha <- tibble(sample_id = rownames(rich),
                    Observed = rich$Observed,
                    Shannon = rich$Shannon,
                    Simpson = rich$Simpson) |>
        left_join(meta, by = "sample_id")
    cat(sprintf("alpha diversity: %d samples\n", nrow(alpha)))
}
```

```{r fx-fig-rarefaction}
fig_section("rarefaction_curves", needs = res("diversity", "rarefaction_data.csv"), {
    rare <- read_csv(res("diversity", "rarefaction_data.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
    if (!is.null(meta)) {
        rare <- rare |> left_join(meta, by = "sample_id")
    }
    grp <- if (PRIMARY %in% names(rare)) PRIMARY else NULL
    p <- ggplot(rare, aes(x = depth, y = expected_richness, group = sample_id)) +
        {if (!is.null(grp)) geom_line(aes(colour = .data[[grp]]), alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.2)
         else geom_line(alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.2)} +
        {if (!is.null(grp)) scale_colour_manual(values = STAGE_PELLET)} +
        scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
        labs(x = "Sequencing depth (log scale)", y = "Expected ASV richness",
             colour = grp, title = "Rarefaction curves",
             subtitle = "Sensitivity analysis; primary results are non-rarefied") +
        theme_pipeline_classic()
    print(p)
    save_nature_figure(fig("rarefaction_curves"), p, "standard")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-alpha-by-variable}
# One panel pair per grouping variable, matching plot_variable_alpha() in the pipeline.
alpha_by_variable <- function(variable) {
    if (is.null(alpha) || !variable %in% names(alpha)) return(invisible(NULL))
    dat <- alpha |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[variable]])) |> mutate(group = as.factor(.data[[variable]]))
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(dat$group) < 2) return(invisible(NULL))
    pal <- get_palette(dplyr::n_distinct(dat$group))
    width <- max(7.0, min(12.0, 2.2 + 0.42 * dplyr::n_distinct(dat$group)))
    sv <- safe_file_label(variable)

    for (metric in c("Observed", "Shannon")) {
        nm <- sprintf("alpha_%s_by_%s", tolower(metric), sv)
        fig_section(nm, needs = PS_CLEAN, {
            p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = group, y = .data[[metric]], fill = group)) +
                geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA) +
                geom_jitter(aes(colour = group), width = 0.15, size = 1.0, alpha = 0.95) +
                scale_fill_manual(values = pal) + scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
                labs(x = variable,
                     y = if (metric == "Observed") "Observed ASV richness" else "Shannon diversity",
                     title = sprintf("%s by %s",
                                     if (metric == "Observed") "Observed ASV richness" else "Shannon diversity",
                                     variable)) +
                theme_pipeline_classic() +
                theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")
            if (PRIMARY %in% names(dat) && variable != PRIMARY) {
                p <- p + facet_wrap(vars(.data[[PRIMARY]]), scales = "free_x")
            }
            print(p)
            ggsave(fig(nm), p, width = width, height = 5.2, dpi = 300,
                   compression = "lzw")
            fig(nm)
        })
    }
}

for (v in unique(c(PRIMARY, SECONDARY, "Cultivar", "Author"))) alpha_by_variable(v)
```

## 4. Beta diversity

```{r fx-fig-pcoa}
# Ordination coordinates are persisted with metadata already joined, so each PCoA
# is a redraw of the pipeline's stored result, not a fresh decomposition.
pcoa_plot <- function(path, colour_var, title, legend_label = colour_var) {
    dat <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
    # By-variable exports carry the grouping column as `group`; the overall exports
    # carry the real variable names. Accept either.
    col <- if (colour_var %in% names(dat)) colour_var else if ("group" %in% names(dat)) "group" else NA
    if (is.na(col)) return(NULL)
    dat <- dat |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[col]]))
    pal <- get_palette(dplyr::n_distinct(dat[[col]]))
    ggplot(dat, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, colour = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_point(size = 1.3, alpha = 0.95) +
        stat_ellipse(level = 0.95, linewidth = 0.35) +
        scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
        labs(x = "PCoA 1", y = "PCoA 2", colour = legend_label, title = title) +
        theme_pipeline_classic() +
        theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"))
}
```

```{r fx-fig-cooccurrence}
fig_section("cooccurrence_network", needs = res("tables", "cooccurrence_edges.csv"), {
    stopifnot(requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE))
    edges <- read_csv(res("tables", "cooccurrence_edges.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
        dplyr::filter(p_adj < 0.05, abs(rho) > 0.6, taxon1_id != taxon2_id)
    g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
        edges |> dplyr::select(from = taxon1_id, to = taxon2_id, rho), directed = FALSE)
    set.seed(42)
    lay <- igraph::layout_with_fr(g)
    nodes <- tibble(id = igraph::V(g)$name, x = lay[, 1], y = lay[, 2],
                    degree = igraph::degree(g)) |>
        left_join(edges |> dplyr::select(id = taxon1_id, label = taxon1) |> distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE),
                  by = "id")
    el <- igraph::as_edgelist(g)
    seg <- tibble(
        x = nodes$x[match(el[, 1], nodes$id)], y = nodes$y[match(el[, 1], nodes$id)],
        xend = nodes$x[match(el[, 2], nodes$id)], yend = nodes$y[match(el[, 2], nodes$id)],
        rho = igraph::E(g)$rho)
    p <- ggplot() +
        geom_segment(data = seg, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend, alpha = abs(rho)),
                     colour = "#8C8C8C", linewidth = 0.25) +
        geom_point(data = nodes, aes(x = x, y = y, size = degree), colour = PRIMARY_PELLET[1],
                   alpha = 0.85) +
        geom_text_repel(data = nodes |> slice_max(degree, n = 18),
                        aes(x = x, y = y, label = label), size = 2, max.overlaps = 20) +
        scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.6, 4)) +
        scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.15, 0.7), guide = "none") +
        labs(title = "Genus co-occurrence network",
             subtitle = sprintf("%d edges at |rho| > 0.6 and adjusted p < 0.05", nrow(edges)),
             size = "Degree") +
        theme_void(base_size = 8) +
        theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 9),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7))
    print(p)
    save_nature_figure(fig("cooccurrence_network"), p, "square")
})
```

```{r fx-fig-correlation-heatmaps}
corr_heatmap <- function(path, facet_label, name) {
    fig_section(name, needs = path, {
        dat <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
            dplyr::filter(!is.na(spearman_rho))
        p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = genus, y = group_value, fill = spearman_rho)) +
            geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
            geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(p_adj < 0.05, "*", "")), size = 2.6, vjust = 0.75) +
            scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#3B6E9E", mid = "white", high = "#C0392B",
                                 midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
            labs(x = NULL, y = facet_label, fill = "Spearman rho",
                 title = sprintf("Top-5 genus vs stage correlation by %s", facet_label),
                 subtitle = "* adjusted p < 0.05") +
            theme_pipeline_classic() +
            theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
        print(p)
        save_nature_figure(fig(name), p, "wide")
    })
}

corr_heatmap(res("tables", "top5_genus_stage_correlation_by_family.csv"),
             "Plant family", "top5_genus_stage_correlation_heatmap_by_plant_family")
corr_heatmap(res("tables", "top5_genus_stage_correlation_by_cultivar.csv"),
```

## 7. Manuscript figures

Fig 1–4 are the audit's corrected figures. They are **not** recomputed here: the
values of record live in `validation/supplementary/`, and `manuscript_figures.qmd`
regenerates the panels against them. That notebook is kept separate on purpose —
see the independence note in `CLAUDE.md`. This section surfaces the manifest so one
document still accounts for every figure in the project.

```{r fx-manuscript-figs}
MF <- res("validation", "figures")
MFR <- res("validation", "figures_R")
man <- tibble(
    figure = c("fig1_composition", "fig2_alpha", "fig3_beta", "fig4_indicator"),
    python_original = file.path(MF, paste0(c("fig1_composition", "fig2_alpha",
                                             "fig3_beta", "fig4_indicator"), "_corrected.png")),
    r_regeneration = file.path(MFR, paste0(c("fig1_composition", "fig2_alpha",
                                             "fig3_beta", "fig4_indicator"), "_R.png"))) |>
    mutate(original_present = file.exists(python_original),
           regeneration_present = file.exists(r_regeneration)) |>
    dplyr::select(figure, original_present, regeneration_present)
knitr::kable(man, caption = "Manuscript figures — produced by manuscript_figures.qmd")
```

# Part 3 — Manuscript audit figures

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## About this part
Fig 1–4 of the manuscript, as corrected by the 2026-08-04 audit. Fig 1 and Fig 2a are
recomputed from the aligned raw inputs; Fig 2b/2c, 3 and 4 are read from the audit's
tables of record so the panels show published values rather than a fresh permutation
run. The `Validation` section at the end reconciles every recomputed quantity.

The recomputation behind those tables is `validation/verify_manuscript.py`, which
reimplements the statistics independently of Part 1 — that is deliberate, so agreement
between them is evidence rather than tautology. Do not refactor the two to share code.
:::

```{r ms-run-validation}
# Optionally regenerate the audit tables before drawing Fig 1-4. Guarded the same way
# the Python pipeline guards its R step: if the interpreter or script is missing, the
# existing tables are used and the render continues.
run_validation <- isTRUE(as.logical(if (exists("params")) params$run_validation else FALSE))
validation_script <- file.path(base_dir, "validation", "verify_manuscript.py")

if (run_validation) {
    python_bin <- Sys.which("python3")
    if (nzchar(python_bin) && file.exists(validation_script)) {
        message("running ", validation_script)
        status <- system2(python_bin, c(shQuote(validation_script),
                                        "--config", shQuote(config_path)))
        message("verify_manuscript.py exit status: ", status)
    } else {
        message("skipping validation run - python3 or verify_manuscript.py not found")
    }
} else {
    message("run_validation is FALSE - using the audit tables already on disk")
}
```


## What this document does

Regenerates the four corrected figures from the manuscript audit in R. Panels
are built from two kinds of input:

- **Recomputed from raw data** (`asv_sparse.npz`, `metadata_aligned.csv`,
  `taxonomy_aligned.csv`): the filtering cascade, phylum/genus composition
  (Fig 1) and per-sample Shannon (Fig 2a).
- **Read from the audit's result tables** (`TableS1`–`TableS3`, the PERMANOVA /
  PERMDISP files): effect sizes (Fig 2b, 2c), beta diversity (Fig 3) and
  indicator taxa (Fig 4). These are the tables of record, so the figures show
  the published values rather than a fresh permutation run.

The `Validation` section at the end compares every recomputed quantity against
the audit tables.

```{r ms-setup}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(patchwork)
library(Matrix)
library(ggtext)

library(jsonlite)

# Paths come from analysis_config.json, resolved relative to the config file --
# the same contract phyloseq_analysis.qmd and validation/verify_manuscript.py use.
resolve_path <- function(base_dir, configured_path) {
  if (startsWith(configured_path, "/")) {
    return(configured_path)
  }
  normalizePath(file.path(base_dir, configured_path), mustWork = FALSE)
}

config_path <- if (exists("params") && !is.null(params$config)) {
  params$config
} else {
  "analysis_config.json"
}
if (!file.exists(config_path)) {
  stop("Configuration file not found: ", config_path)
}
config <- fromJSON(config_path)
base_dir <- dirname(normalizePath(config_path))

# Everything this notebook reads and writes lives under <outputs.directory>/validation,
# produced by: python3 validation/verify_manuscript.py --config <config>
VALID <- file.path(resolve_path(base_dir, config$outputs$directory), "validation")
DATA  <- VALID                                       # aligned raw inputs
SUPP  <- file.path(VALID, "supplementary")           # audit tables of record
OUT   <- file.path(VALID, "figures_R")               # regenerated PNGs land here
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

MS_READY <- all(dir.exists(c(DATA, SUPP)))
if (!MS_READY) {
  message("Part 3 skipped - missing ", paste(c(DATA, SUPP)[!dir.exists(c(DATA, SUPP))],
                                             collapse = ", "),
          "\n  populate it with: python3 validation/verify_manuscript.py --config ",
          config_path, "\n  or re-render with -P run_validation:true")
}

# Palette matched to the Python originals.
RED   <- "#DC0000"   # seed-enriched / stage / recomputed-correct
BLUE  <- "#2166AC"   # seedling-enriched / other
PURPL <- "#6A3D9A"   # batch / provenance
GREY  <- "#6E6E6E"   # annotation text, as-published values
INK   <- "#1A1A1A"

theme_fig <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = rel(1.05), hjust = 0, colour = INK,
                                margin = margin(b = 6)),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.tag = element_text(size = rel(1.3), face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = INK),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = INK),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks = element_line(colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4),
      legend.background = element_blank(),
      legend.key.height = unit(10, "pt"),
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 6, 6)
    )
}
theme_set(theme_fig())

save_fig <- function(plot, file, width, height) {
  ggsave(file.path(OUT, file), plot, width = width, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
}
```

## Load raw data

`asv_sparse.npz` is a SciPy CSR checkpoint. Rather than add a Python
dependency, the two functions below read the `.npy` members directly: an
`.npy` file is a short ASCII header (dtype, shape) followed by a raw
little-endian buffer.

```{r ms-read-npz, eval = MS_READY}
read_npy <- function(path) {
  con <- file(path, "rb"); on.exit(close(con))
  stopifnot(identical(readBin(con, "raw", 6),
                      as.raw(c(0x93, 0x4e, 0x55, 0x4d, 0x50, 0x59))))
  ver  <- readBin(con, "integer", 2, size = 1)
  hlen <- if (ver[1] == 1) readBin(con, "integer", 1, size = 2, signed = FALSE)
          else             readBin(con, "integer", 1, size = 4)
  hdr  <- rawToChar(readBin(con, "raw", hlen))

  descr <- sub(".*'descr': *'([^']+)'.*", "\\1", hdr)
  shp   <- sub(".*'shape': *\\(([^)]*)\\).*", "\\1", hdr)
  dims  <- as.numeric(regmatches(shp, gregexpr("[0-9]+", shp))[[1]])
  n     <- if (length(dims) == 0) 1 else prod(dims)

  switch(descr,
    "<i4" = readBin(con, "integer", n, size = 4),
    # readBin has no 8-byte integer: read hi/lo words and assert the high
    # word is empty (all values here are well under 2^31).
    "<i8" = { w <- readBin(con, "integer", 2 * n, size = 4)
              stopifnot(all(w[c(FALSE, TRUE)] == 0))
              w[c(TRUE, FALSE)] },
    stop("unsupported dtype: ", descr)
  )
}

read_npz_csr <- function(path) {
  dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "npz"); unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
  unzip(path, exdir = dir)
  indptr <- read_npy(file.path(dir, "indptr.npy"))
  shape  <- read_npy(file.path(dir, "shape.npy"))
  sparseMatrix(i = rep.int(seq_len(shape[1]), diff(indptr)),
               j = read_npy(file.path(dir, "indices.npy")) + 1L,
               x = as.numeric(read_npy(file.path(dir, "data.npy"))),
               dims = shape)
}

X   <- read_npz_csr(file.path(DATA, "asv_sparse.npz"))
md  <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "metadata_aligned.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
tax <- read_csv(file.path(DATA, "taxonomy_aligned.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Rows of X are aligned to md, columns to tax (both written out pre-aligned).
stopifnot(nrow(md) == nrow(X), nrow(tax) == ncol(X))
c(samples = nrow(X), features = ncol(X), reads = sum(X))
```

## Filtering cascade

Reproduces steps 1–10 of `TableS5`. Order matters: soil samples are dropped
**before** the library-size floor, so the 1,886 retained samples are already
plant-only.

```{r ms-cascade, eval = MS_READY}
blank_na <- function(v) ifelse(is.na(v), "", v)

fmask <- blank_na(tax$Kingdom) == "Bacteria" &
         blank_na(tax$Order)   != "Chloroplast" &
         blank_na(tax$Family)  != "Mitochondria" &
         !blank_na(tax$Phyla) %in% c("Cyanobacteria", "Cyanobacteriota")

smask <- md$Developmental_Stage != "soil"                      # 48 soil samples
smask <- smask & rowSums(X[, fmask, drop = FALSE]) >= 500      # min_library_size

# Feature filters apply to the surviving columns; lift the predicate back to
# full-matrix positions each time.
lift <- function(pred) {
  out <- logical(ncol(X)); out[which(fmask)[pred]] <- TRUE; out
}
S <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]; fmask <- lift(colSums(S) > 0)
S <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]; fmask <- lift(colSums(S > 0) >= 3)
S <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]; fmask <- lift(colSums(S) >= 10)

# Cap at the 2,000 most abundant features. Five features tie at 220 reads for
# the last three slots, so this cut is NOT uniquely defined -- tie order
# changes which features are kept and therefore the prevalence counts of
# low-abundance phyla. Ties are broken by feature index for determinism.
S  <- X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE]
ts <- colSums(S)
fmask <- lift(order(-ts, seq_along(ts))[1:2000])

Xf   <- as.matrix(X[smask, fmask, drop = FALSE])
mdf  <- md[smask, ]
taxf <- tax[fmask, ]
c(samples = nrow(Xf), features = ncol(Xf), reads = sum(Xf))
```

```{r ms-aggregate, eval = MS_READY}
# Sum feature columns within a taxonomic rank; blank/NA -> "Unassigned".
agg_rank <- function(counts, rank_values) {
  g <- blank_na(rank_values); g[g == ""] <- "Unassigned"
  t(rowsum(t(counts), g))
}

phylum_counts <- agg_rank(Xf, taxf$Phyla)
genus_counts  <- agg_rank(Xf, taxf$Genus)
```

## Figure 1 — Composition

```{r ms-fig1-data, eval = MS_READY}
# (a) per-sample relative abundance by phylum
phy_rel <- phylum_counts / pmax(rowSums(phylum_counts), 1)
phy <- tibble(
  phylum     = colnames(phy_rel),
  mean_rel   = colMeans(phy_rel),
  median_rel = apply(phy_rel, 2, median),
  prevalence = colSums(phy_rel > 0) / nrow(phy_rel)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(phylum != "Unassigned") |>
  slice_max(mean_rel, n = 6) |>
  # label sits clear of whichever marker extends further right
  mutate(phylum = fct_reorder(phylum, mean_rel),
         label_x = pmax(mean_rel, median_rel))

# (b) genus read totals. "Seed-enriched" is derived, not asserted: a genus is
# seed-side if its significant indicator ASVs are mostly Seeds-side (TableS3).
s3 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS3_indicator_taxa.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
seed_side <- s3 |>
  dplyr::filter(q_BH < 0.05) |>
  dplyr::count(Genus, group) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::filter(Seeds > Seedlings) |>
  pull(Genus)

gen <- tibble(
  genus      = colnames(genus_counts),
  total      = colSums(genus_counts),
  prevalence = colSums(genus_counts > 0)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(genus != "Unassigned") |>
  slice_max(total, n = 8) |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(genus %in% seed_side, "seed-enriched", "other"),
         genus = fct_reorder(genus, total))

top3_pct <- round(100 * sum(sort(gen$total, decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]) / sum(Xf))
```

```{r ms-fig1, fig.width=7.04, fig.height=3.06, eval = MS_READY}

            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.02, size = 2.9, colour = GREY) +
```

## Figure 2 — Alpha diversity

```{r ms-fig2-data, eval = MS_READY}
# (a) per-sample Shannon on the 2,000-feature matrix. Three samples have all
# their reads outside the cap; Shannon is undefined there and they are dropped
# (scoring them 0 is what inflates the published H to 38.2 at n = 1,886).
depth <- rowSums(Xf)
prop  <- Xf / pmax(depth, 1)
shannon <- -rowSums(ifelse(prop > 0, prop * log(prop), 0))
shannon[depth == 0] <- NA_real_

alpha <- tibble(stage = mdf$Developmental_Stage, shannon = shannon) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(shannon)) |>
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, c("Seeds", "Seedlings")))

s1 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS1_alpha_diversity.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
kw <- s1 |> dplyr::filter(variable == "Developmental_Stage", metric == "Shannon")

# (b) Kruskal-Wallis effect sizes, Shannon. Display order puts developmental
# stage first (the paper's focus), then the remaining variables ascending.
eps <- s1 |>
  dplyr::filter(metric == "Shannon") |>
  transmute(variable, epsilon_sq,
            label = recode(variable,
              Developmental_Stage = "Developmental\nstage", Family = "Plant family",
              Scientific_Name = "Host species", Cultivar = "Cultivar",
              Author = "Author", study_alias = "Study"),
            class = case_when(
              variable == "Developmental_Stage" ~ "stage",
              variable %in% c("study_alias", "Author") ~ "batch / provenance",
              TRUE ~ "host biology")) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, rev(c("Developmental\nstage", "Plant family",
                                     "Host species", "Cultivar", "Author", "Study"))),
         class = factor(class, c("stage", "host biology", "batch / provenance")))

# floor, not round: the published panel states 13x (0.254 / 0.019 = 13.5)
stage_ratio <- floor(max(eps$epsilon_sq) / eps$epsilon_sq[eps$class == "stage"])

# (c) stage coefficient under increasing control
s2 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS2_alpha_depth_models.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(metric == "Shannon") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, unique(model),
                        labels = c("stage\nonly", "+ depth", "+ depth\n+ study",
                                   "+ depth\n+ study\n+ species")),
         lo = stage_beta - 1.96 * se, hi = stage_beta + 1.96 * se)

shrink <- round(100 * (1 - dplyr::last(s2$stage_beta) / dplyr::first(s2$stage_beta)))
```

```{r ms-fig2, fig.width=7.48, fig.height=3.05, eval = MS_READY}
n_lab <- dplyr::count(alpha, stage)

# p in mantissa/exponent form, taken from TableS1 rather than retyped
p_exp <- floor(log10(kw$p))
p_lab <- sprintf("H = %.1f, p = %.1f×10<sup>%d</sup>",
                 kw$H, kw$p / 10^p_exp, p_exp)

set.seed(42)   # reproducible jitter
p2a <- ggplot(alpha, aes(stage, shannon, colour = stage)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.24, height = 0, size = 0.3, alpha = 0.25) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, fun.min = mean, fun.max = mean, geom = "errorbar",
               width = 0.5, linewidth = 1.1, colour = INK) +
  annotate("text", x = seq_len(nrow(n_lab)), y = 5.5,
           label = paste0("n=", n_lab$n), colour = GREY, size = 2.8) +
  annotate("segment", x = 1, xend = 2, y = 4.9, yend = 4.9,
           colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4) +
  # vjust/padding pinned: richtext padding otherwise floats the label upward
  annotate("richtext", x = 1.5, y = 5.12, label.colour = NA, fill = NA,
           label.padding = unit(rep(0, 4), "pt"), vjust = 0.5, hjust = 0.5,
           size = 2.9, colour = INK, label = p_lab) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Seeds = RED, Seedlings = BLUE), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 5.65), breaks = 0:5) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Stage difference is real but small\n(ε² = %.3f)",
                       kw$epsilon_sq),
       x = NULL, y = "Shannon diversity")

p2b <- ggplot(eps, aes(epsilon_sq, label, colour = class)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = epsilon_sq, yend = label), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", epsilon_sq),
                colour = if_else(class == "host biology", "grey", as.character(class))),
            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.008, size = 2.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(stage = RED, `host biology` = BLUE,
                                 `batch / provenance` = PURPL, grey = GREY),
                      breaks = c("stage", "host biology", "batch / provenance")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.34), breaks = seq(0, 0.3, 0.1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Study identity explains %d× more\nvariance than stage", stage_ratio),
       x = "Kruskal–Wallis ε²  (variance explained)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.99, 0.86),
        legend.justification = c(1, 0.5), legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

p2c <- ggplot(s2, aes(model, stage_beta)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = RED,
                  linewidth = 0.6, size = 0.45) +
  geom_text(data = dplyr::slice(s2, c(1, n())),
            aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", stage_beta)),
            colour = RED, size = 2.9, hjust = c(0, 1),
            nudge_x = c(-0.4, -0.12), nudge_y = c(-0.062, 0.064)) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.4, y = -0.255, label = "95% CI", colour = GREY,
           size = 2.8, hjust = 1) +
  labs(title = sprintf("Effect shrinks %d%% once depth and\nstudy are controlled", shrink),
       x = NULL, y = "Seedling − seed Shannon (β)")

fig2 <- p2a + p2b + p2c + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
fig2
save_fig(fig2, "fig2_alpha_R.png", 7.48, 3.05)
```

## Figure 3 — Beta diversity

All three panels read the audit's PERMANOVA / PERMDISP outputs. The key point
is the basis: the manuscript's Table 4 values reproduce on **ASV-level raw
counts at n = 1,553**, not the genus-level relative abundances at n = 1,883
that the caption claims.

```{r ms-fig3-data, eval = MS_READY}
TERMS <- c("Developmental_Stage", "study_alias", "Author",
           "Scientific_Name", "Cultivar")   # published panel order, top to bottom
TERM_LAB <- c(Developmental_Stage = "Developmental\nstage", study_alias = "Study",
              Author = "Author", Scientific_Name = "Host species",
              Cultivar = "Cultivar")

as_term <- function(x) factor(TERM_LAB[x], rev(unname(TERM_LAB[TERMS])))

uni <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "permanova_univariate_recomputed.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(basis = if_else(str_detect(basis, "^ASV"), "asv", "genus"),
         term = as_term(term))

marg <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "permanova_marginal_recomputed.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(basis == "ASV top100 raw") |>
  mutate(term = as_term(term))

disp <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "permdisp_recomputed.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(basis = if_else(str_detect(basis, "^ASV"), "asv", "genus"),
         term = as_term(term))

# (b) univariate vs marginal for the three terms that share a model
pan_b <- marg |>
  transmute(term, marginal = R2) |>
  left_join(uni |> dplyr::filter(basis == "asv") |> transmute(term, univariate = R2),
            by = "term") |>
  pivot_longer(c(univariate, marginal), names_to = "model", values_to = "R2") |>
  mutate(term = factor(term, c("Study", "Developmental\nstage", "Host species"),
                       labels = c("Study", "Stage", "Host\nspecies")),
         model = factor(model, c("univariate", "marginal"),
                        labels = c("univariate (as published)", "marginal (adjusted)")))

stage_drop <- pan_b |>
  dplyr::filter(term == "Stage") |>
  summarise(x = R2[str_starts(model, "univariate")] /
                R2[str_starts(model, "marginal")]) |>
  pull(x) |> round(1)
stage_gap  <- uni |> dplyr::filter(term == "Developmental\nstage") |>
  dplyr::select(basis, R2) |> deframe()
disp_genus <- disp |> dplyr::filter(basis == "genus", term == "Developmental\nstage")
```

```{r ms-fig3, fig.width=7.92, fig.height=3.11, eval = MS_READY}

    geom_point(aes(shape = basis, colour = basis, fill = basis),

    scale_fill_manual(values = c(asv = RED, genus = "transparent")) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL)
}
```

## Figure 4 — Indicator taxa

```{r ms-fig4-data, eval = MS_READY}
sig <- dplyr::filter(s3, q_BH < 0.05)

# Named in the manuscript's indicator-taxa claims, with the direction the text
# reports. Panel (a) shows that four of the six carry significant ASVs in both
# directions, so a single reported direction is not supportable.
NAMED <- tribble(
  ~Genus,            ~reported,
  "Pantoea",         "seedling",
  "Enterobacter",    "seedling",
  "Kosakonia",       "seedling",
  "Pseudomonas",     "seedling",
  "Exiguobacterium", "seed",
  "Erwinia",         "seed"
)

counts <- sig |>
  dplyr::filter(Genus %in% NAMED$Genus) |>
  dplyr::count(Genus, group) |>
  complete(Genus, group, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  mutate(signed = if_else(group == "Seeds", -n, n),
         Genus = factor(Genus, rev(NAMED$Genus)))

arrows <- NAMED |>
  mutate(Genus = factor(Genus, rev(NAMED$Genus)),
         glyph = if_else(reported == "seedling", "→", "←"))

# Several genera appear more than once, so rank (not genus) is the y position;
# duplicate factor labels would otherwise be merged into one level.
top12 <- sig |>
  slice_max(indval, n = 12) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(indval)) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), y = factor(rank, levels = rev(rank)))

top12_labels <- setNames(top12$Genus, as.character(top12$rank))

both_ways <- counts |> group_by(Genus) |> dplyr::filter(all(n > 0)) |> n_groups()
```

## Validation

Recomputed values against the audit's tables of record.

```{r ms-validate, eval = MS_READY}
s5 <- read_csv(file.path(SUPP, "TableS5_filtering_accounting.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE) |> slice_tail(n = 1)

kw_r <- kruskal.test(shannon ~ stage, data = alpha)

checks <- tribble(
  ~quantity,                        ~recomputed,                  ~audit,
  "samples retained",               nrow(Xf),                     s5$n_samples,
  "features retained",              ncol(Xf),                     s5$n_features,
  "reads retained",                 sum(Xf),                      s5$total_reads,
  "Shannon n (stage test)",         nrow(alpha),                  kw$n_samples,
  "Proteobacteria prevalence (n)",  sum(phy_rel[, "Proteobacteria"] > 0), 1770L,
  "Pantoea total reads",            max(colSums(genus_counts[, "Pantoea", drop = FALSE])), 4468686L
) |>
  mutate(across(c(recomputed, audit), as.numeric),
         agrees = recomputed == audit)

knitr::kable(checks)

tibble(statistic = "Kruskal-Wallis H (Shannon ~ stage)",
       recomputed = round(unname(kw_r$statistic), 3),
       audit_TableS1 = kw$H) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

**On the H discrepancy.** The recomputed H differs from `TableS1` in the third
decimal (36.354 vs 36.357). The cause is the tie at the 2,000-feature cut
documented in the cascade chunk: five features tie at 220 reads for three
slots, so the retained feature set — and every per-sample Shannon value
computed from it — depends on sort order. The same tie makes Actinobacteriota
prevalence 937 under index-order tie-breaking (the value the manuscript
reports) and 940 under NumPy's unstable `argsort` (the value the audit script
comments). Neither figure annotation is affected at the precision shown, but
the cap should be made explicitly deterministic in the pipeline.

### Overview

This document consolidates the overlapping logic from the imported strawberry `.qmd` analyses into a single workflow adapted to the local repository data in `Datesets/`.

The merged workflow covers:

- sample metadata inspection
- construction of a count matrix aligned to metadata and taxonomy
- taxonomic composition summaries
- alpha diversity analysis
- beta diversity ordination and PERMANOVA
- tree-based alpha and beta diversity using `Datesets/tree.nexus`

### Load Data

```{r sma-load-data, eval = FALSE}
metadata_raw <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/metadata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
counts_raw <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/asv-counts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
taxonomy_raw <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/taxa.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
tree_raw <- ape::read.nexus("Datesets/tree.nexus")

if (inherits(tree_raw, "multiPhylo")) {
  tree_raw <- tree_raw[[1]]
}

if (names(metadata_raw)[2] == "") {
  names(metadata_raw)[2] <- "blank_column"
}

metadata <- metadata_raw %>%
  rename(sample_id = run_accession) %>%
  select(sample_id, everything()) %>%
  distinct(sample_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# align samples and metadata
sample_ids <- intersect(metadata$sample_id, counts_raw[[1]])
counts_filtered <- counts_raw %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% sample_ids)

count_matrix <- counts_filtered %>%
  dplyr::select(-sample_id) %>%
  as.matrix()
rownames(count_matrix) <- counts_filtered$sample_id
storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"

feature_ids <- colnames(count_matrix)
tree_feature_ids <- intersect(feature_ids, tree_raw$tip.label)

metadata <- metadata %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(count_matrix))

taxonomy <- taxonomy_raw %>%
  filter(OTUID %in% feature_ids)
taxonomy <- taxonomy %>%
  mutate(across(c(Kingdom:Species), ~replace_na(.x, "Unassigned")))

common_features <- intersect(colnames(count_matrix), tree_raw$tip.label)
if (length(common_features) == 0) {
  stop("No overlapping OTUs between counts and the tree.")
}

count_matrix <- count_matrix[, common_features, drop = FALSE]
taxonomy <- taxonomy[match(common_features, taxonomy$OTUID), ]
metadata <- metadata[match(rownames(count_matrix), metadata$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]

sample_totals <- rowSums(count_matrix)
keep_samples <- sample_totals > 0

count_matrix <- count_matrix[keep_samples, , drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(count_matrix))

taxonomy <- taxonomy %>%
  filter(OTUID %in% colnames(count_matrix))

count_matrix <- count_matrix[, taxonomy$OTUID, drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata[match(rownames(count_matrix), metadata$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
phylo_tree <- ape::keep.tip(tree_raw, colnames(count_matrix))

saveRDS(count_matrix, "analysis_outputs/objects/count_matrix.rds")
saveRDS(metadata, "analysis_outputs/objects/metadata.rds")
saveRDS(taxonomy, "analysis_outputs/objects/taxonomy.rds")
saveRDS(phylo_tree, "analysis_outputs/objects/phylo_tree.rds")

cat("Samples retained:", nrow(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Features retained:", ncol(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Metadata columns:", ncol(metadata), "\n")
cat("Tree tips retained:", length(phylo_tree$tip.label), "\n")

aggregate_by_rank <- function(mat, taxonomy_tbl, rank_col) {
  rank_vals <- taxonomy_tbl[[rank_col]]
  rank_vals[is.na(rank_vals) | rank_vals == ""] <- "Unassigned"
  levels <- unique(rank_vals)
  result <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = nrow(mat),
    ncol = length(levels),
    dimnames = list(rownames(mat), levels)
  )
  for (lvl in levels) {
    cols <- which(rank_vals == lvl)
    if (length(cols) > 0) {
      result[, lvl] <- rowSums(mat[, cols, drop = FALSE])
    }
  }
  result
}
```

#### Alpha Diversity Statistics

```{r sma-alpha-stats, eval = FALSE}
run_kruskal <- function(df, metric, group_var) {
  subset_df <- df %>%
    select(all_of(c(metric, group_var))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[metric]]), !is.na(.data[[group_var]]))

  if (dplyr::n_distinct(subset_df[[group_var]]) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  test <- kruskal.test(stats::as.formula(paste(metric, "~", group_var)), data = subset_df)
  tibble::tibble(
    metric = metric,
    variable = group_var,
    statistic = unname(test$statistic),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
}

alpha_stats <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Evenness", "Faith_PD"), function(metric) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_kruskal(alpha_df, metric, group_var)))
}))

readr::write_csv(alpha_stats, "analysis_outputs/tables/alpha_diversity_kruskal.csv")
knitr::kable(alpha_stats)
```

### Beta Diversity

```{r sma-beta-diversity, eval = FALSE}
relative_matrix <- sweep(count_matrix, 1, rowSums(count_matrix), "/")
relative_matrix[is.na(relative_matrix)] <- 0
presence_absence_matrix <- ifelse(count_matrix > 0, 1, 0)

bray_dist <- vegan::vegdist(relative_matrix, method = "bray")
jaccard_dist <- vegan::vegdist(presence_absence_matrix, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
phylo_beta_features <- head(
  names(sort(colSums(count_matrix), decreasing = TRUE)),
  n = min(2000, ncol(count_matrix))
)
phylo_beta_matrix <- count_matrix[, phylo_beta_features, drop = FALSE]
phylo_beta_tree <- ape::keep.tip(phylo_tree, phylo_beta_features)
phylo_beta_dist <- GUniFrac::GUniFrac(phylo_beta_matrix, phylo_beta_tree, alpha = 0.5)$unifracs[, , "d_0.5"]

bray_pcoa <- cmdscale(bray_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2)
jaccard_pcoa <- cmdscale(jaccard_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2)
phylo_pcoa <- cmdscale(as.dist(phylo_beta_dist), eig = TRUE, k = 2)

bray_df <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Axis1 = bray_pcoa$points[, 1],
    Axis2 = bray_pcoa$points[, 2]
  )

jaccard_df <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Axis1 = jaccard_pcoa$points[, 1],
    Axis2 = jaccard_pcoa$points[, 2]
  )

phylo_df <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    Axis1 = phylo_pcoa$points[, 1],
    Axis2 = phylo_pcoa$points[, 2]
  )
```

```{r sma-jaccard-ordination, eval = FALSE}
if (length(plot_group_vars) == 0) {
  cat("No multi-level metadata grouping variable found for Jaccard plotting.\n")
} else {
  for (group_var in plot_group_vars) {
    jaccard_plot <- ggplot(jaccard_df, aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, color = .data[[group_var]])) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
      labs(
        title = paste("PCoA on Jaccard Distances by", group_var),
        x = "Axis 1",
        y = "Axis 2",
        color = group_var
      )

    print(jaccard_plot)
    ggsave(
      paste0("analysis_outputs/figures/jaccard_pcoa_", group_var, ".png"),
      jaccard_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300
    )
  }
}
```

#### PERMANOVA

```{r sma-permanova, eval = FALSE}
run_permanova <- function(distance_object, metadata_df, group_var, distance_name) {
  subset_df <- metadata_df %>%
    select(sample_id, all_of(group_var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[group_var]]))

  if (dplyr::n_distinct(subset_df[[group_var]]) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  sample_keep <- subset_df$sample_id
  subset_dist <- as.dist(as.matrix(distance_object)[sample_keep, sample_keep])
  subset_df <- subset_df[match(sample_keep, subset_df$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
  formula <- stats::as.formula(paste("subset_dist ~", group_var))
  test <- vegan::adonis2(formula, data = subset_df)

  tibble::tibble(
    distance = distance_name,
    variable = group_var,
    df = test$Df[1],
    r2 = test$R2[1],
    f = test$F[1],
    p_value = test$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  )
}

permanova_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_permanova(bray_dist, metadata, group_var, "bray")),
  lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_permanova(jaccard_dist, metadata, group_var, "jaccard")),
  lapply(categorical_group_vars, function(group_var) run_permanova(as.dist(phylo_beta_dist), metadata, group_var, "phylogenetic"))
)

readr::write_csv(permanova_results, "analysis_outputs/tables/permanova_results.csv")
knitr::kable(permanova_results)
```
