### Project Scope

This joined project notebook is adapted to the metadata variables present in `Datesets/metadata.csv`:

- `Author`
- `Geography`
- `Cultivar`
- `Developmental_Stage`
- `Scientific_Name`
- `sample_description`

It does not assume strawberry-specific variables such as `TreatmentCode`, `EnvZone`, or `Management`.

### Build Analysis Objects

```{r pj1-build-objects, eval = FALSE}
metadata <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/metadata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
counts <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/asv-counts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
taxonomy <- readr::read_csv("Datesets/taxa.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
tree <- ape::read.nexus("Datesets/tree.nexus")

if (inherits(tree, "multiPhylo")) {
  tree <- tree[[1]]
}

if (names(metadata)[2] == "") {
  names(metadata)[2] <- "blank_column"
}

metadata <- metadata %>%
  rename(sample_id = run_accession) %>%
  select(-blank_column, -command_to_download_the_reads)

counts_long <- counts %>%
  rename(sample_id = 1) %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "OTUID", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
  mutate(Abundance = as.numeric(Abundance))

common_samples <- intersect(metadata$sample_id, unique(counts_long$sample_id))
common_features <- Reduce(intersect, list(unique(counts_long$OTUID), taxonomy$OTUID, tree$tip.label))

metadata <- metadata %>% filter(sample_id %in% common_samples)
taxonomy <- taxonomy %>% filter(OTUID %in% common_features)
counts_long <- counts_long %>% filter(sample_id %in% common_samples, OTUID %in% common_features)

count_matrix <- counts_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = OTUID, values_from = Abundance, values_fill = 0) %>%
  as.data.frame()

rownames(count_matrix) <- count_matrix$sample_id
count_matrix$sample_id <- NULL
count_matrix <- as.matrix(count_matrix)
storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "numeric"

count_matrix <- count_matrix[rowSums(count_matrix) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata[match(rownames(count_matrix), metadata$sample_id), , drop = FALSE]
tree <- ape::keep.tip(tree, colnames(count_matrix))

saveRDS(metadata, "analysis_outputs/objects/metadata_joined.rds")
saveRDS(taxonomy, "analysis_outputs/objects/taxonomy_joined.rds")
saveRDS(count_matrix, "analysis_outputs/objects/count_matrix_joined.rds")
saveRDS(tree, "analysis_outputs/objects/tree_joined.rds")

cat("Samples:", nrow(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Features:", ncol(count_matrix), "\n")
cat("Metadata variables:", paste(names(metadata), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

#Filter data at 0.0025 prevalence
#Obtained from: https://f1000research.com/articles/5-1492/v1;#One of the reasons to filter by prevalence is to avoid spending #much time analyzing taxa that were only rarely seen. This also turns out to be a useful filter of noise (taxa that are #actually just artifacts of the data collection process)
### Define prevalence of each taxa; # (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)

```{r pj2-c2, echo = FALSE,warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
load("phyloseq-objects/ps.RData")

prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

prevdf = data.frame(Prevalence = prev0,
                    TotalAbundance = taxa_sums(ps),
                    tax_table(ps))# the most prevalent ASVs present therein the composition

#only for reference, in case we want to filter Phylum that appear less than X times
keepPhylum = table(prevdf$Phylum)[(table(prevdf$Phylum) > 0)]

prevasv = subset(prevdf, Phylum %in% names(keepPhylum))

# Define prevalence threshold as 0.25% of total samples# 
prevalenceThreshold = 0.0025 * nsamples(ps)
prevalenceThreshold

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
prevalence_filter_result <- (prev0 > prevalenceThreshold)
if(sum(prevalence_filter_result) == 0) {
  stop("Error: Prevalence filter would remove all taxa. Consider adjusting the prevalence threshold.")
}

ps1 = prune_taxa(prevalence_filter_result, ps);ps1

# Filter entries with unidentified Phylum.
ps2 = subset_taxa(ps1, Phylum %in% names(keepPhylum));ps2

#Plot prevalence of different Phylum
#https://github.com/joey711/phyloseq/issues/1474

print(paste0("Initial #ASVs:", ntaxa(ps), ". #ASVs after prevalence filtering:", ntaxa(ps2), ". #ASVs removed: ", ntaxa(ps)-ntaxa(ps2)))
```

### Rerefaction curves at different sampling depths and including the lost samples

```{r pj2-alpha-diversity-analysis, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Load the phyloseq object, but only if it doesn't already exist
# Set working directory
setwd("/Users/expeditoolimi/Documents/TUG-schrodinger-Return/FOEKL/EXC_16S_FOE_KOB/Extensive-system-microbiome/")
load("phyloseq-objects/ps2.RData")
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(microbiome)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(FSA)
library(multcompView)
library(kableExtra)

# Define rarefaction depths
depths <- c(500, 1000,2500)

#colour pellets
my_palette <- c("500" = "grey35", "1000" = "#00AFBB", "2500" = "goldenrod")


# Initialize lists
alpha_list <- list()
lost_samples <- data.frame(Depth = integer(), Retained = integer(), Lost = integer())
lost_sample_names <- list()

# Rarefy and compute alpha diversity
alpha_list <- list()
ps <- ps2
total_samples <- nsamples(ps)

for (d in depths) {
  rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(ps, sample.size = d, rngseed = 123, verbose = FALSE)
  
  retained_samples <- sample_names(rarefied)
  original_samples <- sample_names(ps)
  lost <- setdiff(original_samples, retained_samples)
  
  lost_samples <- rbind(lost_samples, data.frame(Depth = d, Retained = length(retained_samples), Lost = length(lost)))
  lost_sample_names[[as.character(d)]] <- lost
  
  alpha_df <- estimate_richness(rarefied, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "Chao1", "ACE"))
  alpha_df$Depth <- d
  alpha_df$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_df)
  alpha_list[[as.character(d)]] <- alpha_df
}

# Combine all alpha diversity dataframes
alpha_all <- do.call(rbind, alpha_list);alpha_all

# Reshape for ggplot (long format)
alpha_long <- alpha_all %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "Chao1", "ACE"),
               names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value");alpha_long

# Function to compute significance letters
get_significance_letters <- function(df) {
  if (length(unique(df$Depth)) < 2 || nrow(df) < 2) return(data.frame())
  dunn_res <- dunnTest(Value ~ factor(Depth), data = df, method = "bh")
  pvals <- dunn_res$res$P.adj
  names(pvals) <- dunn_res$res$Comparison
  letters <- multcompLetters(pvals)$Letters
  depth_levels <- sort(unique(df$Depth))
  label_map <- setNames(letters[1:length(depth_levels)], depth_levels)
  df %>%
    group_by(Depth) %>%
    summarise(ypos = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.5) %>%
    mutate(label = label_map[as.character(Depth)],
           Metric = unique(df$Metric)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(label), !is.na(ypos))
}

# Compute annotations for all metrics
annot_all <- alpha_long %>%
  group_by(Metric) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  lapply(get_significance_letters) %>%
  bind_rows();annot_all

p <- ggplot(alpha_long, aes(x = factor(Depth), y = Value)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = factor(Depth))) +   # Depth stays numeric for fill
  geom_text(data = annot_all, aes(x = factor(Depth), y = ypos, label = label),
            color = "black", size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = my_palette) +
      labs(
    x = "Sequencing Depth",
    y = "Alpha Diversity",
    title = "Alpha Diversity Metrics Across Sequencing Depths"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave(
  "alpha_diversity_plot.tiff",
  plot = p,
  width = 4,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)


# Print lost sample summary
print(lost_samples)

# Print lost sample names per depth
for (depth in names(lost_sample_names)) {
  cat("\nDepth:", depth, "\nLost Samples:", paste(lost_sample_names[[depth]], collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

```{r pj2-u8, eval = FALSE}
# Set working directory
setwd("/Users/expeditoolimi/Documents/TUG-schrodinger-Return/FOEKL/EXC_16S_FOE_KOB/Extensive-system-microbiome/")
load("phyloseq-objects/ps2.RData")
# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Normalize and Prepare Data for Plotting
# --------------------------------------------------
# Transform counts to relative abundance across the entire dataset
ps.rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps2, function(x) x / sum(x) * 100)

# Melt the phyloseq object for easy plotting with ggplot2
ps_melt <- psmelt(ps.rel)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Select Top 20 Classes for Visualization
# --------------------------------------------------
# We find the most abundant classes to show them individually.
# The rest will be grouped into an "Others" category.
# Note: The original comment mentioned 29 classes, but the code used 20.
top_classes <- ps_melt %>%
  group_by(Class) %>%
  summarise(total_abund = sum(Abundance)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_abund)) %>%
  slice(1:20) %>% 
  pull(Class)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create "Others" and Re-aggregate
# --------------------------------------------------
# ASVs from classes not in the top 20 are grouped into an "Others" category.
ps_melt_aggregated <- ps_melt %>%
  mutate(Class_grouped = ifelse(Class %in% top_classes, as.character(Class), "Others")) %>%
  group_by(Sample, TreatmentCode, EnvZone, Class_grouped) %>%
  summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Set Factor Levels (Legend Order)
# --------------------------------------------------
class_order <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
  group_by(Class_grouped) %>%
  summarise(MeanAbund = sum(Abundance)) %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanAbund)) %>%
  pull(Class_grouped)

class_order <- c(setdiff(class_order, "Others"), "Others")
ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped <- factor(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped, levels = rev(class_order))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build your 30-color palette from your selection
# --------------------------------------------------
color_pool <- unique(c(mycolors))
color_pool <- unique(c(mycolors, master_palette))
color_pool <- color_pool[!color_pool %in% c("grey85", "grey70", "white", "#E3DDDD")]

n_needed <- length(levels(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped))
final_palette <- color_pool[1:n_needed]
names(final_palette) <- levels(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped)

if("Others" %in% names(final_palette)) {
  final_palette["Others"] <- "grey35" 
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. NEW: Define Sorting Order by Vicinamibacteria
# --------------------------------------------------
# We create a reference dataframe with the abundance of the target class per sample
vici_order <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
  filter(Class_grouped == "Vicinamibacteria") %>%
  select(Sample, Abundance) %>%
  rename(vici_abund = Abundance)

# Join it back so we can use vici_abund in the reorder function
ps_melt_aggregated <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
  left_join(vici_order, by = "Sample") %>%
  mutate(vici_abund = ifelse(is.na(vici_abund), 0, vici_abund))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Plot (Sorted by Vicinamibacteria)
# --------------------------------------------------
Region_treatment <- ggplot(
  ps_melt_aggregated,
  # reorder(Sample, -vici_abund) sorts from highest to lowest abundance
  aes(x = reorder(Sample, -vici_abund), y = Abundance, fill = Class_grouped)
) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "black", linewidth = 0.05) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = final_palette) + 
  facet_wrap(~TreatmentCode, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  labs(

  ) +

    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),

  ) +

print(Region_treatment)
```

#3. Normalization Functions

```{r pj2-u12, eval = FALSE}
# Relative abundance (TSS)
normalize_relative <- function(ps) {
  transform_sample_counts(ps, function(x) x / sum(x))
}

# CSS normalization
normalize_css <- function(ps) {
  mgs <- phyloseq_to_metagenomeSeq(ps)
  p <- cumNormStatFast(mgs)
  mgs <- cumNorm(mgs, p = p)
  norm_counts <- MRcounts(mgs, norm = TRUE)
  otu_table(ps) <- otu_table(norm_counts, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
  return(ps)
}

# Hellinger transformation
normalize_hellinger <- function(ps) {
  asv_tab <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) {
    asv_tab <- t(asv_tab)
  }
  otu_hell <- decostand(asv_tab, method = "hellinger")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) {
    otu_hell <- t(otu_hell)
  }
  otu_table(ps) <- otu_table(otu_hell, taxa_are_rows = taxa_are_rows(ps))
  return(ps)
}
```

#Filter data at 0.0025 prevalence
#Obtained from: https://f1000research.com/articles/5-1492/v1;#One of the reasons to filter by prevalence is to avoid spending #much time analyzing taxa that were only rarely seen. This also turns out to be a useful filter of noise (taxa that are #actually just artifacts of the data collection process)
### Define prevalence of each taxa; # (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)

```{r pj3-c2, echo = FALSE,warning = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
load("phyloseq-objects/ps.RData")

prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

prevdf = data.frame(Prevalence = prev0,
                    TotalAbundance = taxa_sums(ps),
                    tax_table(ps))# the most prevalent ASVs present therein the composition

#only for reference, in case we want to filter Phylum that appear less than X times
keepPhylum = table(prevdf$Phylum)[(table(prevdf$Phylum) > 0)]

prevasv = subset(prevdf, Phylum %in% names(keepPhylum))

# Define prevalence threshold as 0.25% of total samples# 
prevalenceThreshold = 0.0025 * nsamples(ps)
prevalenceThreshold

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
prevalence_filter_result <- (prev0 > prevalenceThreshold)
if(sum(prevalence_filter_result) == 0) {
  stop("Error: Prevalence filter would remove all taxa. Consider adjusting the prevalence threshold.")
}

ps1 = prune_taxa(prevalence_filter_result, ps);ps1

# Filter entries with unidentified Phylum.
ps2 = subset_taxa(ps1, Phylum %in% names(keepPhylum));ps2

#Plot prevalence of different Phylum
#https://github.com/joey711/phyloseq/issues/1474

print(paste0("Initial #ASVs:", ntaxa(ps), ". #ASVs after prevalence filtering:", ntaxa(ps2), ". #ASVs removed: ", ntaxa(ps)-ntaxa(ps2)))
```

### Rerefaction curves at different sampling depths and including the lost samples

```{r pj3-alpha-diversity-analysis, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Load the phyloseq object, but only if it doesn't already exist
load("phyloseq-objects/ps2.RData")
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(microbiome)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(FSA)
library(multcompView)

# Define rarefaction depths
depths <- c(500, 1000,2500)

#colour pellets
my_palette <- c("500" = "grey35", "1000" = "#00AFBB", "2500" = "goldenrod")


# Initialize lists
alpha_list <- list()
lost_samples <- data.frame(Depth = integer(), Retained = integer(), Lost = integer())
lost_sample_names <- list()

# Rarefy and compute alpha diversity
alpha_list <- list()
ps <- ps2
total_samples <- nsamples(ps)

for (d in depths) {
  rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(ps, sample.size = d, rngseed = 123, verbose = FALSE)
  
  retained_samples <- sample_names(rarefied)
  original_samples <- sample_names(ps)
  lost <- setdiff(original_samples, retained_samples)
  
  lost_samples <- rbind(lost_samples, data.frame(Depth = d, Retained = length(retained_samples), Lost = length(lost)))
  lost_sample_names[[as.character(d)]] <- lost
  
  alpha_df <- estimate_richness(rarefied, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "Chao1", "ACE"))
  alpha_df$Depth <- d
  alpha_df$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_df)
  alpha_list[[as.character(d)]] <- alpha_df
}

# Combine all alpha diversity dataframes
alpha_all <- do.call(rbind, alpha_list);alpha_all

# Reshape for ggplot (long format)
alpha_long <- alpha_all %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "Chao1", "ACE"),
               names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value");alpha_long

# Function to compute significance letters
get_significance_letters <- function(df) {
  if (length(unique(df$Depth)) < 2 || nrow(df) < 2) return(data.frame())
  dunn_res <- dunnTest(Value ~ factor(Depth), data = df, method = "bh")
  pvals <- dunn_res$res$P.adj
  names(pvals) <- dunn_res$res$Comparison
  letters <- multcompLetters(pvals)$Letters
  depth_levels <- sort(unique(df$Depth))
  label_map <- setNames(letters[1:length(depth_levels)], depth_levels)
  df %>%
    group_by(Depth) %>%
    summarise(ypos = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.5) %>%
    mutate(label = label_map[as.character(Depth)],
           Metric = unique(df$Metric)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(label), !is.na(ypos))
}

# Compute annotations for all metrics
annot_all <- alpha_long %>%
  group_by(Metric) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  lapply(get_significance_letters) %>%
  bind_rows();annot_all

p <- ggplot(alpha_long, aes(x = factor(Depth), y = Value)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = factor(Depth))) +   # Depth stays numeric for fill
  geom_text(data = annot_all, aes(x = factor(Depth), y = ypos, label = label),
            color = "black", size = 4) +
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = my_palette) +
      labs(
    x = "Sequencing Depth",
    y = "Alpha Diversity",
    title = "Alpha Diversity Metrics Across Sequencing Depths"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave(
  "alpha_diversity_plot.tiff",
  plot = p,
  width = 4,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)


# Print lost sample summary
print(lost_samples)

# Print lost sample names per depth
for (depth in names(lost_sample_names)) {
  cat("\nDepth:", depth, "\nLost Samples:", paste(lost_sample_names[[depth]], collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```



```{r pj3-u8, eval = FALSE}
load("phyloseq-objects/ps2.RData")
# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Normalize and Prepare Data for Plotting
# --------------------------------------------------
# Transform counts to relative abundance across the entire dataset
ps.rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps2, function(x) x / sum(x) * 100)

# Melt the phyloseq object for easy plotting with ggplot2
ps_melt <- psmelt(ps.rel)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Select Top 20 Classes for Visualization
# --------------------------------------------------
# We find the most abundant classes to show them individually.
# The rest will be grouped into an "Others" category.
# Note: The original comment mentioned 29 classes, but the code used 20.
top_classes <- ps_melt %>%
  group_by(Class) %>%
  summarise(total_abund = sum(Abundance)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_abund)) %>%
  slice(1:20) %>% 
  pull(Class)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create "Others" and Re-aggregate
# --------------------------------------------------
# ASVs from classes not in the top 20 are grouped into an "Others" category.
ps_melt_aggregated <- ps_melt %>%
  mutate(Class_grouped = ifelse(Class %in% top_classes, as.character(Class), "Others")) %>%
  group_by(Sample, TreatmentCode, EnvZone, Class_grouped) %>%
  summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Set Factor Levels (Legend Order)
# --------------------------------------------------
class_order <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
  group_by(Class_grouped) %>%
  summarise(MeanAbund = sum(Abundance)) %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanAbund)) %>%
  pull(Class_grouped)

class_order <- c(setdiff(class_order, "Others"), "Others")
ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped <- factor(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped, levels = rev(class_order))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Build your 30-color palette from your selection
# --------------------------------------------------
color_pool <- unique(c(mycolors))
color_pool <- unique(c(mycolors, master_palette))
color_pool <- color_pool[!color_pool %in% c("grey85", "grey70", "white", "#E3DDDD")]

n_needed <- length(levels(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped))
final_palette <- color_pool[1:n_needed]
names(final_palette) <- levels(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped)

if("Others" %in% names(final_palette)) {
  final_palette["Others"] <- "grey35" 
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. NEW: Define Sorting Order by Vicinamibacteria
# --------------------------------------------------
# We create a reference dataframe with the abundance of the target class per sample
vici_order <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
  filter(Class_grouped == "Vicinamibacteria") %>%
  select(Sample, Abundance) %>%
  rename(vici_abund = Abundance)

# Join it back so we can use vici_abund in the reorder function
ps_melt_aggregated <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
  left_join(vici_order, by = "Sample") %>%
  mutate(vici_abund = ifelse(is.na(vici_abund), 0, vici_abund))

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Plot (Sorted by Vicinamibacteria)
# --------------------------------------------------
Region_treatment <- ggplot(
  ps_melt_aggregated,
  # reorder(Sample, -vici_abund) sorts from highest to lowest abundance
  aes(x = reorder(Sample, -vici_abund), y = Abundance, fill = Class_grouped)
) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "black", linewidth = 0.05) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = final_palette) + 
  facet_wrap(~TreatmentCode, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Samples (Sorted by Vicinamibacteria Abundance)",
    y = "Relative Abundance (%)",
    fill = "Class"
  ) +
  theme_pubclean() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1, reverse = TRUE))

print(Region_treatment)


# Save plot
library(ggpubr)
tiff("Region_treatment.tiff", units="in", width=10, height=6, res=300)
print(Region_treatment)
dev.off()
```

```{r pj3-u11, eval = FALSE}
cat("Total samples:", nsamples(ps_subset), "\n")
cat("Total taxa:", ntaxa(ps_subset), "\n\n")

  data.frame() %>%
  group_by(EnvZone, TreatmentCode) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(EnvZone, desc(n));genotype_summary
write.csv(genotype_summary, "genotype_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

kable(genotype_summary,
      col.names = c("EnvZone", "Treatment", "Samples"),
      caption = "Treatment Distribution by Environmental Zone") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
```

#3. Normalization Functions

```{r pj3-u12, eval = FALSE}
# Relative abundance (TSS)
normalize_relative <- function(ps) {
  transform_sample_counts(ps, function(x) x / sum(x))
}

# CSS normalization
normalize_css <- function(ps) {
  mgs <- phyloseq_to_metagenomeSeq(ps)
  p <- cumNormStatFast(mgs)
  mgs <- cumNorm(mgs, p = p)
  norm_counts <- MRcounts(mgs, norm = TRUE)
  otu_table(ps) <- otu_table(norm_counts, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
  return(ps)
}

# Hellinger transformation
normalize_hellinger <- function(ps) {
  asv_tab <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) {
    asv_tab <- t(asv_tab)
  }
  otu_hell <- decostand(asv_tab, method = "hellinger")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) {
    otu_hell <- t(otu_hell)
  }
  otu_table(ps) <- otu_table(otu_hell, taxa_are_rows = taxa_are_rows(ps))
  return(ps)
}
```

```{r pj3-c3, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Load the phyloseq object
load("phyloseq-objects/ps2.RData")

# Create compositional plots for different partners under each field type and treatment
# First, let's determine what partner/treatment variables exist in the metadata
metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps2))
print("Available metadata columns:")
print(colnames(metadata))

# Transform to relative abundance for compositional analysis
ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps2, function(x) x / sum(x) * 100)

# Melt the phyloseq object for plotting
ps_melt <- psmelt(ps_rel)

# Get top 20 most abundant classes for visualization
top_classes <- ps_melt %>%
  group_by(Class) %>%
  summarise(total_abund = sum(Abundance)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_abund)) %>%
  slice(1:20) %>%
  pull(Class)

# Create grouped data with "Others" category
ps_melt_aggregated <- ps_melt %>%
  mutate(Class_grouped = ifelse(Class %in% top_classes, as.character(Class), "Others")) %>%
  group_by(Sample, EnvZone, TreatmentCode, Class_grouped) %>%
  summarise(Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")

# Set factor levels for consistent ordering
class_order <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
  group_by(Class_grouped) %>%
  summarise(MeanAbund = sum(Abundance)) %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanAbund)) %>%
  pull(Class_grouped)

class_order <- c(setdiff(class_order, "Others"), "Others")
ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped <- factor(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped, levels = rev(class_order))

# Build color palette
color_pool <- unique(c(mycolors))
color_pool <- unique(c(mycolors, master_palette))
color_pool <- color_pool[!color_pool %in% c("grey85", "grey70", "white", "#E3DDDD")]

n_needed <- length(levels(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped))
final_palette <- color_pool[1:n_needed]
names(final_palette) <- levels(ps_melt_aggregated$Class_grouped)

if("Others" %in% names(final_palette)) {
  final_palette["Others"] <- "grey35"
}

# Create compositional plots by partners (assuming TreatmentCode represents partners)
# and faceted by field type (EnvZone)
compositional_plot_partners <- ggplot(
  ps_melt_aggregated,
  aes(x = reorder(Sample, Abundance), y = Abundance, fill = Class_grouped)
) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "black", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = final_palette) +
  facet_grid(EnvZone ~ TreatmentCode, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Samples",
    y = "Relative abundance (%)",
    fill = "Taxonomic Class",
    title = "Compositional Plots by Partners and Field Types",
    subtitle = "Distribution of microbial communities by treatment and environmental zone"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1, reverse = TRUE))

print(compositional_plot_partners)

# Save the plot
tiff("compositional_plots_partners.tiff", units="in", width=14, height=10, res=300)
print(compositional_plot_partners)
dev.off()

# Alternative: Create separate plots for each combination of field type and partner
unique_env_zones <- unique(ps_melt_aggregated$EnvZone)
unique_treatments <- unique(ps_melt_aggregated$TreatmentCode)

for(env_zone in unique_env_zones) {
  for(treatment in unique_treatments) {
    # Filter data for specific combination
    subset_data <- ps_melt_aggregated %>%
      filter(EnvZone == env_zone & TreatmentCode == treatment)

    if(nrow(subset_data) > 0) {
      # Create plot for this combination
      p <- ggplot(
        subset_data,
        aes(x = reorder(Sample, Abundance), y = Abundance, fill = Class_grouped)
      ) +
        geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "black", linewidth = 0.05) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = final_palette) +
        labs(
          x = "Samples",
          y = "Relative abundance (%)",
          fill = "Taxonomic Class",
          title = paste("Compositional Plot -", env_zone, "| Partner:", treatment),
          subtitle = "Distribution of microbial communities"
        ) +
        theme_classic() +
        theme(
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
        ) +
        guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1, reverse = TRUE))

      # Save individual plot
      filename <- paste0("compositional_plot_", gsub(" ", "_", env_zone), "_", gsub(" ", "_", treatment), ".tiff")
      tiff(filename, units="in", width=12, height=8, res=300)
      print(p)
      dev.off()
    }
  }
}
```

```{r bd1-ordinations, eval = FALSE}
make_ord_df <- function(dist_obj) {
  ord <- cmdscale(dist_obj, eig = TRUE, k = 2)
  metadata %>%
    mutate(Axis1 = ord$points[, 1], Axis2 = ord$points[, 2])
}

bray_df <- make_ord_df(bray_dist)
jaccard_df <- make_ord_df(jaccard_dist)
phylo_df <- make_ord_df(phylo_dist)

plot_ordination_by_var <- function(df, group_var, title_text) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, color = .data[[group_var]])) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    labs(title = paste(title_text, "by", group_var), color = group_var)
}

for (var in plot_vars) {
  print(plot_ordination_by_var(bray_df, var, "Bray-Curtis PCoA"))
  print(plot_ordination_by_var(jaccard_df, var, "Jaccard PCoA"))
  print(plot_ordination_by_var(phylo_df, var, "Phylogenetic PCoA"))
}
```

### PERMANOVA

```{r bd1-permanova, eval = FALSE}
run_permanova <- function(distance_object, group_var, distance_name) {
  subset_df <- metadata %>%
    select(sample_id, all_of(group_var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[group_var]]), .data[[group_var]] != "")

  if (dplyr::n_distinct(subset_df[[group_var]]) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  sample_keep <- subset_df$sample_id
  subset_dist <- as.dist(as.matrix(distance_object)[sample_keep, sample_keep])
  test <- vegan::adonis2(stats::as.formula(paste("subset_dist ~", group_var)), data = subset_df)

  tibble::tibble(
    distance = distance_name,
    variable = group_var,
    r2 = test$R2[1],
    f = test$F[1],
    p_value = test$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  )
}

permanova_results <- bind_rows(
  lapply(group_vars, function(x) run_permanova(bray_dist, x, "bray")),
  lapply(group_vars, function(x) run_permanova(jaccard_dist, x, "jaccard")),
  lapply(group_vars, function(x) run_permanova(phylo_dist, x, "phylogenetic"))
)

knitr::kable(permanova_results)
```

##### Calculate CSS-Normalized Distance Matrices

```{r bd2-css-distance-matrices, eval = FALSE}
# Normalize data using CSS normalization for Bray-Curtis and UniFrac
# Since metagenomeSeq is not available, we'll use relative abundance normalization
ps2_css <- transform_sample_counts(ps2, function(x) x/sum(x)*10000)  # Convert to relative abundance then scale to 10000

# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity using CSS-normalized data
bray_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps2_css, method = "bray")

# UniFrac distances (if tree available) using CSS-normalized data
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps2_css, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  unifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps2_css, method = "unifrac")
  wunifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps2_css, method = "wunifrac")
  cat("Phylogenetic distances calculated (UniFrac)\n")
} else {
  cat("No phylogenetic tree available - skipping UniFrac\n")
}
```

```{r bd2-pa-ordination, eval = FALSE}
p_nmds_jaccard <- plot_ordination(ps2_pa, ord_nmds_jaccard,
                          title = paste0("NMDS - Jaccard Distance (Stress = ",
```

#### PERMANOVA Analysis with All Variables

```{r bd2-permanova-all, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, error=TRUE, eval = FALSE}
# Ensure required packages are loaded
if (!require(vegan)) {
  stop("vegan package is required for PERMANOVA analysis")
}

# Verify that required objects exist before proceeding
if (!exists("ps2")) {
  stop("ps2 object not found. Please run the 'Load Data' chunk first.")
}

if (!exists("bray_dist") || !exists("jaccard_dist")) {
  cat("Distance matrices not found. Computing them now...\n")

  # Create CSS-normalized data if not already done
  if (!exists("ps2_css")) {
    ps2_css <- transform_sample_counts(ps2, function(x) x/sum(x)*10000)
  }

  # Create presence-absence data if not already done
  if (!exists("ps2_pa")) {
    ps2_pa <- transform_sample_counts(ps2, function(x) ifelse(x > 0, 1, 0))
  }

  # Compute distance matrices if not already done
  if (!exists("bray_dist")) {
    bray_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps2_css, method = "bray")
  }

  if (!exists("jaccard_dist")) {
    jaccard_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps2_pa, method = "jaccard")
  }
}

# Get metadata directly from the phyloseq objects
meta_css <- data.frame(sample_data(ps2_css))
meta_pa <- data.frame(sample_data(ps2_pa))

# Function to run PERMANOVA for a variable
run_permanova <- function(distance_matrix, data, var_name) {
  if(!var_name %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("Variable", var_name, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  formula_str <- paste("distance_matrix ~", var_name)
  permanova_result <- adonis2(
    as.formula(formula_str),
    data = data,
    permutations = 999,
    by = "margin"
  )

  return(permanova_result)
}

# Function to run PERMANOVA for interaction terms
run_interaction_permanova <- function(distance_matrix, data, var1, var2) {
  if(!var1 %in% colnames(data) || !var2 %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("One or both variables", var1, "and", var2, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  formula_str <- paste("distance_matrix ~", var1, "*", var2)
  permanova_result <- adonis2(
    as.formula(formula_str),
    data = data,
    permutations = 999,
    by = "margin"
  )

  return(permanova_result)
}

# Function to run three-way interaction PERMANOVA
run_three_way_permanova <- function(distance_matrix, data, var1, var2, var3) {
  if(!var1 %in% colnames(data) || !var2 %in% colnames(data) || !var3 %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("One or more variables", var1, ",", var2, "and", var3, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  formula_str <- paste("distance_matrix ~", var1, "*", var2, "*", var3)
  permanova_result <- adonis2(
    as.formula(formula_str),
    data = data,
    permutations = 999,
    by = "margin"
  )

  return(permanova_result)
}

# Run PERMANOVA for all specified variables using both CSS-normalized and presence-absence data
permanova_results <- list()

# Main effects
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_css)) {
  permanova_results[["TreatmentCode_bray"]] <- run_permanova(bray_dist, meta_css, "TreatmentCode")
  if(!is.null(permanova_results[["TreatmentCode_bray"]])) {
    cat("PERMANOVA: Effect of TreatmentCode on Community Composition (Bray-Curtis, CSS-normalized)\n")
    cat("=====================================================================================\n")
    print(permanova_results[["TreatmentCode_bray"]])
  }

  # Jaccard version
  permanova_results[["TreatmentCode_jaccard"]] <- run_permanova(jaccard_dist, meta_pa, "TreatmentCode")
  if(!is.null(permanova_results[["TreatmentCode_jaccard"]])) {
    cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of TreatmentCode on Community Composition (Jaccard, Presence-Absence)\n")
    cat("=====================================================================================\n")
    print(permanova_results[["TreatmentCode_jaccard"]])
  }
} else {
  cat("Warning: TreatmentCode variable not found in metadata\n")
}


if("Timepoint" %in% colnames(meta_css)) {
  permanova_results[["Timepoint_bray"]] <- run_permanova(bray_dist, meta_css, "Timepoint")
  if(!is.null(permanova_results[["Timepoint_bray"]])) {
    cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Timepoint (Bray-Curtis, CSS-normalized)\n")
    cat("=============================================================\n")
    print(permanova_results[["Timepoint_bray"]])
  }

  # Jaccard version
  permanova_results[["Timepoint_jaccard"]] <- run_permanova(jaccard_dist, meta_pa, "Timepoint")
  if(!is.null(permanova_results[["Timepoint_jaccard"]])) {
    cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Timepoint (Jaccard, Presence-Absence)\n")
    cat("=============================================================\n")
    print(permanova_results[["Timepoint_jaccard"]])
  }
} else {
  cat("Warning: Timepoint variable not found in metadata\n")
}



if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_css) && "Timepoint" %in% colnames(meta_css)) {
  permanova_results[["Treatment_Time_bray"]] <- run_interaction_permanova(bray_dist, meta_css, "TreatmentCode", "Timepoint")
  if(!is.null(permanova_results[["Treatment_Time_bray"]])) {
    cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Treatment*Time Interaction (Bray-Curtis, CSS-normalized)\n")
    cat("============================================================================\n")
    print(permanova_results[["Treatment_Time_bray"]])
  }

  # Jaccard version
  permanova_results[["Treatment_Time_jaccard"]] <- run_interaction_permanova(jaccard_dist, meta_pa, "TreatmentCode", "Timepoint")
  if(!is.null(permanova_results[["Treatment_Time_jaccard"]])) {
    cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Treatment*Time Interaction (Jaccard, Presence-Absence)\n")
    cat("============================================================================\n")
    print(permanova_results[["Treatment_Time_jaccard"]])
  }
} else {
  cat("Warning: TreatmentCode or Timepoint variable not found for interaction analysis\n")
}


# Create summary table for all variables tested
permanova_summary_list <- list()

for(var_name in names(permanova_results)) {
  if(!is.null(permanova_results[[var_name]])) {
    result <- permanova_results[[var_name]]
    # Determine the distance method from the variable name
    distance_method <- if(grepl("_jaccard$", var_name)) "Jaccard" else "Bray-Curtis"

    # Extract components for main effects vs interactions
    var_names <- gsub("_bray|_jaccard", "", var_name)

    summary_row <- data.frame(
      Factor = var_names,
      Method = distance_method,
      R2 = result$R2[1],  # Overall R2 for the model
      F_value = result$F[1],
      p_value = result$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    )
    summary_row$Significance <- ifelse(summary_row$p_value < 0.001, "***",
                                      ifelse(summary_row$p_value < 0.01, "**",
                                            ifelse(summary_row$p_value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))

    permanova_summary_list[[var_name]] <- summary_row
  }
}

if(length(permanova_summary_list) > 0) {
  permanova_summary <- do.call(rbind, permanova_summary_list)

  kable(permanova_summary,
        caption = "PERMANOVA Summary for All Variables and Interactions (Bray-Curtis and Jaccard)",
        digits = c(0, 0, 4, 2, 4, 0)) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

  # Generate Detailed Interaction Summary from existing results
  interaction_keys <- grep("_Time_", names(permanova_results), value = TRUE)
  interaction_summary <- data.frame(
    Model = character(),
    Term = character(),
    R2 = numeric(),
    F_Value = numeric(),
    P_Value = numeric(),
    Significance = character(),
    Distance_Method = character(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  if(length(interaction_keys) > 0) {
    for(key in interaction_keys) {
      result <- permanova_results[[key]]
      distance_method <- if(grepl("_jaccard$", key)) "Jaccard" else "Bray-Curtis"

      for(i in 1:nrow(result)) {
        term <- rownames(result)[i]
        interaction_summary <- rbind(interaction_summary, data.frame(
          Model = gsub("_bray|_jaccard", "", key),
          Term = term,
          R2 = round(result$R2[i], 4),
          F_Value = round(result$F[i], 4),
          P_Value = round(result$`Pr(>F)`[i], 4),
          Significance = ifelse(result$`Pr(>F)`[i] < 0.001, "***",
                                ifelse(result$`Pr(>F)`[i] < 0.01, "**",
                                       ifelse(result$`Pr(>F)`[i] < 0.05, "*", "ns"))),
          Distance_Method = distance_method
        ))
      }
    }
  }

  if(nrow(interaction_summary) > 0) {
    kable(interaction_summary,
          caption = "Detailed PERMANOVA Results for Key Interactions",
          digits = c(0, 0, 0, 4, 4, 4, 0)) %>%
      kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
  }
} else {
  cat("No PERMANOVA results to summarize - check that the required variables exist in your metadata\n")
}
```


#### Extended Interaction Effects Analysis

```{r bd2-interaction-effects-analysis, eval = FALSE}
# Load required libraries
library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Note: Metadata and distance matrices (bray_dist and jaccard_dist) and functions are defined in previous chunks
# Using the same variables from the main PERMANOVA analysis

# Create results directory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists("results")) {
  dir.create("results")
}

# Run interaction analyses
interaction_results <- list()


# Treatment * Timepoint interaction (Bray-Curtis)
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(metadata) && "Timepoint" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
  interaction_results[["Treatment_Time_bray"]] <- run_interaction_permanova(bray_dist, metadata, "TreatmentCode", "Timepoint")
  cat("PERMANOVA: Effect of Treatment*Time Interaction (Bray-Curtis)\n")
  cat("=============================================================\n")
  print(interaction_results[["Treatment_Time_bray"]])
  cat("\n")
}


# Treatment * Timepoint interaction (Jaccard)
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(metadata) && "Timepoint" %in% colnames(metadata)) {
  interaction_results[["Treatment_Time_jaccard"]] <- run_interaction_permanova(jaccard_dist, metadata, "TreatmentCode", "Timepoint")
  cat("PERMANOVA: Effect of Treatment*Time Interaction (Jaccard)\n")
  cat("========================================================\n")
  print(interaction_results[["Treatment_Time_jaccard"]])

# Extract and save interaction results to CSV
extract_interaction_results <- function(interaction_results) {
  results_list <- list()

  for(name in names(interaction_results)) {
    if(!is.null(interaction_results[[name]])) {
      result_table <- interaction_results[[name]]

      # Add the model name as a column
      temp_df <- as.data.frame(result_table)
      temp_df$Model <- name
      temp_df$Distance_Method <- ifelse(grepl("_jaccard$", name), "Jaccard", "Bray-Curtis")

      # Reorder columns to put Model and Distance_Method first
      # Get the original column names from the data frame
      original_cols <- colnames(temp_df)[!colnames(temp_df) %in% c("Model", "Distance_Method")]
      temp_df <- temp_df[, c("Model", "Distance_Method", original_cols)]

      results_list[[name]] <- temp_df
    }
  }

  # Combine all results
  if(length(results_list) > 0) {
    all_results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
    rownames(all_results) <- NULL  # Reset row numbers

    return(all_results)
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
}

# Extract all interaction results
all_interaction_results <- extract_interaction_results(interaction_results)

# Save the combined interaction results to CSV
if(!is.null(all_interaction_results)) {
  write.csv(all_interaction_results, "results/beta_diversity_interaction_effects.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Beta diversity interaction effects saved to 'results/beta_diversity_interaction_effects.csv'\n")
} else {
  cat("No interaction results to save.\n")
}

# Save individual interaction results as well
for(name in names(interaction_results)) {
  if(!is.null(interaction_results[[name]])) {
    result_df <- as.data.frame(interaction_results[[name]])
    result_df$Model <- name
    result_df$Distance_Method <- ifelse(grepl("_jaccard$", name), "Jaccard", "Bray-Curtis")

    # Reorder columns
    original_cols <- colnames(result_df)[!colnames(result_df) %in% c("Model", "Distance_Method")]
    result_df <- result_df[, c("Model", "Distance_Method", original_cols)]

    filename <- paste0("results/beta_diversity_interaction_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", name), ".csv")
    write.csv(result_df, filename, row.names = FALSE)
    cat("Saved", filename, "\n")
  }
}

# Save the interaction results object
saveRDS(interaction_results, "results/beta_diversity_interaction_results.rds")
cat("Raw interaction results saved to 'results/beta_diversity_interaction_results.rds'\n")

cat("All interaction effect analyses have been saved in CSV format to the 'results' directory.\n")
```

#### Combined PCoA Plots Using Cowplot

```{r bd2-combined-pcoa-plots, fig.width=16, fig.height=16, eval = FALSE}
# Separate plots by method
bray_plots <- pcoa_plots_list[grep("_bray$", names(pcoa_plots_list))]
jaccard_plots <- pcoa_plots_list[grep("_jaccard$", names(pcoa_plots_list))]

# Function to process and save combined plots
process_combined_plot <- function(plot_list, title_text, filename_suffix) {
  if(length(plot_list) > 0) {
    # Position legends at bottom
    plots_formatted <- lapply(plot_list, function(p) p + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
    
    # Create grid
    # Calculate appropriate dimensions (e.g., 3 columns)
    n_plots <- length(plots_formatted)
    n_col <- min(3, n_plots)
    n_row <- ceiling(n_plots / n_col)
    
    combined_grid <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = plots_formatted, ncol = n_col, nrow = n_row)
    
    # Title
    title_plot <- cowplot::ggdraw() +
      cowplot::draw_label(title_text, fontface = 'bold', size = 16) +
      theme_void()
      
    # Combine
    final_plot <- cowplot::plot_grid(
      title_plot, combined_grid,
      ncol = 1,
      rel_heights = c(0.05, 1)
    )
    
    print(final_plot)
    
    # Save
    ggsave(paste0("figures/beta_diversity_pcoa_", filename_suffix, "_combined.tiff"),
           final_plot, width = 5 * n_col, height = 5 * n_row + 1, dpi = 300,
           units = "in", device = "tiff", compression = "lzw")
  } else {
    cat(paste("No plots available for", filename_suffix, "\n"))
  }
}

# Generate for Bray-Curtis
process_combined_plot(bray_plots, "Beta Diversity (Bray-Curtis) - PCoA Plots", "bray")

# Generate for Jaccard
process_combined_plot(jaccard_plots, "Beta Diversity (Jaccard) - PCoA Plots", "jaccard")
```

```{r bd3-libraries, eval = FALSE}
library(reshape2)
library(cowplot)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
set.seed(123)
```

### Load Functional Data

```{r bd3-load-functional-data, eval = FALSE}
# Load the original COG pathways data
cog_data_raw <- read.csv("COG-pathways.csv", row.names = 1)

# The raw COG data has sample IDs as row names and functional categories as columns
func_data <- cog_data_raw

# Load the metadata separately
meta_data_raw <- read.csv("metadata_simple.csv")

# Match samples between functional data and metadata
common_samples <- intersect(rownames(func_data), meta_data_raw$id)

# Subset both datasets to common samples
func_data <- func_data[common_samples, ]
meta_data <- meta_data_raw[match(common_samples, meta_data_raw$id), ]

# Make sure row names are properly set for both datasets
rownames(func_data) <- common_samples
rownames(meta_data) <- common_samples

cat("Functional data loaded:\n")
cat("- Number of samples with both functional data and metadata:", nrow(func_data), "\n")
cat("- Number of functional categories:", ncol(func_data), "\n")
cat("- Metadata variables available:", paste(colnames(meta_data), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

### Overview of Functional Profiles

```{r bd3-functional-overview, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate summary statistics for functional categories
func_summary <- data.frame(
  Function = colnames(func_data),
  Mean_Expression = apply(func_data, 2, mean),
  Median_Expression = apply(func_data, 2, median),
  SD_Expression = apply(func_data, 2, sd),
  Min_Expression = apply(func_data, 2, min),
  Max_Expression = apply(func_data, 2, max)
)

# Sort by mean expression
func_summary <- func_summary[order(func_summary$Mean_Expression, decreasing = TRUE), ]

# Display top 10 most expressed functions
kable(head(func_summary, 10), caption = "Top 10 Most Expressed Functional Categories") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))

# Distribution of functional category expressions
expression_long <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(func_data))
colnames(expression_long) <- c("Sample", "Function", "Expression")

p_hist <- ggplot(expression_long, aes(x = Expression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Functional Category Expressions",
       x = "Expression Level (Log10 + 1)",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.2),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey95", size = 0.1)
  )

print(p_hist)

# Save the histogram
ggsave("figures/functional_expression_distribution.tiff", p_hist, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

### Heatmap of Microbial Functions

```{r bd3-microbial-function-heatmap, fig.width=15, fig.height=12, eval = FALSE}
# Select key categorical variables for annotation
annotation_cols <- c("TreatmentCode", "Management", "Timepoint", "EnvZone", "TrialType")
available_annotation_cols <- intersect(annotation_cols, colnames(meta_data))

if(length(available_annotation_cols) > 0) {
  # Prepare annotation data
  ann_data <- meta_data[, available_annotation_cols, drop = FALSE]

  # Convert to factor for proper coloring
  for(col in colnames(ann_data)) {
    ann_data[[col]] <- as.factor(ann_data[[col]])
  }

  # Create colors for annotations
  ann_colors <- list()
  for(col in colnames(ann_data)) {
    n_levels <- nlevels(ann_data[[col]])
    if(n_levels <= 8) {
      ann_colors[[col]] <- colorRampPalette(c("#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c", "#d62728", "#9467bd", "#8c564b", "#e377c2", "#7f7f7f"))(n_levels)
      names(ann_colors[[col]]) <- levels(ann_data[[col]])
    } else {
      ann_colors[[col]] <- colorRampPalette(c("#1f77b4", "#aec7e8", "#ff7f0e", "#ffbb78", "#2ca02c", "#98df8a", "#d62728", "#ff9896", "#9467bd", "#c5b0d5", "#8c564b", "#c49c94", "#e377c2", "#f7b6d3", "#7f7f7f", "#c7c7c7"))(n_levels)
      names(ann_colors[[col]]) <- levels(ann_data[[col]])
    }
  }

  # Name the color vectors appropriately
  names(ann_colors) <- colnames(ann_data)

  # To avoid naming conflicts with pheatmap, ensure clean annotation data
  rownames(ann_data) <- rownames(func_log)  # Make sure row names match the matrix
} else {
  ann_data <- NULL
  ann_colors <- NULL
}

# For the heatmap, focus on a subset of pathways
# Select top pathways based on variance across samples
pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
top_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:30]  # Top 30 most variable pathways

# Subset the data to top pathways
func_subset <- func_data[, top_pathways, drop = FALSE]

# Log-transform the data for better visualization (add pseudocount to avoid log(0))
func_log <- log10(func_subset + 1)

# Ensure row names match for annotation
rownames(func_log) <- rownames(func_subset)

# Create the heatmap
if(!is.null(ann_data)) {
  # Save the heatmap to file
  pheatmap(
    func_log,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_rownames = TRUE,
    show_colnames = TRUE,
    annotation_row = ann_data,
    annotation_colors = ann_colors,
    scale = "none",  # Already log-transformed
    color = colorRampPalette(c("#F0F8FF", "#D0E6F8", "#A2CFFE", "#7FB0D0", "#1A5490"))(100),
    main = "Heatmap of Top 30 Most Variable Microbial Functions",
    fontsize = 8,
    fontsize_row = 6,
    fontsize_col = 8
  )

  # Save separately as file
  pheatmap(
    func_log,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_rownames = TRUE,
    show_colnames = TRUE,
    annotation_row = ann_data,
    annotation_colors = ann_colors,
    scale = "none",  # Already log-transformed
    color = colorRampPalette(c("#F0F8FF", "#D0E6F8", "#A2CFFE", "#7FB0D0", "#1A5490"))(100),
    main = "Heatmap of Top 30 Most Variable Microbial Functions",
    fontsize = 8,
    fontsize_row = 6,
    fontsize_col = 8,
    filename = "figures/microbial_function_heatmap.tiff"
  )
} else {
  # Save the heatmap to file
  pheatmap(
    func_log,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_rownames = TRUE,
    show_colnames = TRUE,
    scale = "none",  # Already log-transformed
    color = colorRampPalette(c("#F0F8FF", "#D0E6F8", "#A2CFFE", "#7FB0D0", "#1A5490"))(100),
    main = "Heatmap of Top 30 Most Variable Microbial Functions",
    fontsize = 8,
    fontsize_row = 6,
    fontsize_col = 8
  )

  # Save separately as file
  pheatmap(
    func_log,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = TRUE,
    show_rownames = TRUE,
    show_colnames = TRUE,
    scale = "none",  # Already log-transformed
    color = colorRampPalette(c("#F0F8FF", "#D0E6F8", "#A2CFFE", "#7FB0D0", "#1A5490"))(100),
    main = "Heatmap of Top 30 Most Variable Microbial Functions",
    fontsize = 8,
    fontsize_row = 6,
    fontsize_col = 8,
    filename = "figures/microbial_function_heatmap.tiff"
  )
}

# Print summary statistics
cat("Heatmap created using top 30 most variable microbial functions\n")
cat("Variables included in annotation:", paste(available_annotation_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Number of samples:", nrow(func_data), "\n")
cat("Selected functional categories:", ncol(func_subset), "\n")
```

### Differential Functional Profiles by Treatment

```{r bd3-treatment-differences, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate average functional profiles by TreatmentCode
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
  # Select top 15 most variable pathways for clearer visualization
  top15_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]
  func_top15 <- func_data[, top15_pathways, drop = FALSE]

  # Calculate means by treatment
  treatment_means <- aggregate(func_top15, by = list(Treatment = meta_data$TreatmentCode), FUN = mean)
  rownames(treatment_means) <- treatment_means$Treatment
  treatment_means <- treatment_means[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt the data for ggplot
  melted_treatment <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(treatment_means))
  colnames(melted_treatment) <- c("Function", "Treatment", "Expression")

  # Create the heatmap
  p_treatment <- ggplot(melted_treatment, aes(x = Function, y = Treatment, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_treatment$Expression),
                         low = "#2E86AB",
                         mid = "#A2CFFE",
                         high = "#FFFFFF",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey95", size = 0.1)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Average Functional Profiles by Treatment") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)

  print(p_treatment)

  # Save the treatment heatmap
  ggsave("figures/treatment_functional_profiles.tiff", p_treatment, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)

  # Statistical comparison between treatments (Kruskal-Wallis for each function)
  kw_results <- data.frame(
    Function = character(),
    KW_Statistic = numeric(),
    P_Value = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  for(func in top15_pathways) {
    formula_str <- paste0(func, " ~ TreatmentCode")
    kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(formula_str), data = cbind(func_data[, func, drop = FALSE], meta_data))
    kw_results <- rbind(kw_results, data.frame(
      Function = func,
      KW_Statistic = kw_test$statistic,
      P_Value = kw_test$p.value
    ))
  }

  # Adjust p-values for multiple testing
  kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted <- p.adjust(kw_results$P_Value, method = "BH")
  kw_results <- kw_results[order(kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted), ]

  # Show significant differences
  sig_functions <- kw_results[kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted < 0.05, ]
  if(nrow(sig_functions) > 0) {
    cat("\nFunctions significantly different by treatment (FDR < 0.05):\n")
    print(kable(sig_functions, digits = 4))
  } else {
    cat("\nNo functions showed significant differences by treatment (FDR < 0.05)\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("TreatmentCode variable not available in metadata\n")
}
```

### Functional Profiles by Management and Timepoint

```{r bd3-management-timepoint-profiles, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, eval = FALSE}
# Create combined plots for Management and Timepoint if available
available_vars <- intersect(c("Management", "Timepoint"), colnames(meta_data))

if(length(available_vars) >= 2) {
  # Select top 12 most variable pathways
  top12_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:12]
  func_top12 <- func_data[, top12_pathways, drop = FALSE]

  # Combine management and timepoint for analysis
  meta_combo <- meta_data
  meta_combo$Management_Timepoint <- paste(meta_combo$Management, meta_combo$Timepoint, sep = "_")

  # Calculate means by management and timepoint combination
  combo_means <- aggregate(func_top12, by = list(Combo = meta_combo$Management_Timepoint), FUN = mean)
  rownames(combo_means) <- combo_means$Combo
  combo_means <- combo_means[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt the data for ggplot
  melted_combo <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(combo_means))
  colnames(melted_combo) <- c("Function", "Management_Timepoint", "Expression")

  # Create the heatmap
  p_combo <- ggplot(melted_combo, aes(x = Function, y = Management_Timepoint, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_combo$Expression),
                         low = "#1A5490",
                         mid = "#7FB0D0",
                         high = "#F0F8FF",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey95", size = 0.1)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Management and Timepoint Combination") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.6)

  print(p_combo)

  # Save the management-timepoint heatmap
  ggsave("figures/management_timepoint_functional_profiles.tiff", p_combo, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)

  cat("Functional profiles by Management and Timepoint combinations displayed\n")
} else {
  cat("Management and/or Timepoint variables not available in sufficient quantity\n")
  cat("Available variables:", paste(available_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

#### Advanced Heatmaps with ComplexHeatmap

```{r bd3-complex-heatmap-analysis, fig.width=15, fig.height=12, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Prepare data for ComplexHeatmap
# Select top pathways based on variance
pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
top_pathways_complex <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:25]  # Top 25 for ComplexHeatmap
func_subset_complex <- func_data[, top_pathways_complex, drop = FALSE]

# Log-transform the data for better visualization
func_log_complex <- log10(func_subset_complex + 1)

# Prepare annotation data for ComplexHeatmap
selected_metadata <- c("TreatmentCode", "Management", "Timepoint", "EnvZone")
available_metadata <- intersect(selected_metadata, colnames(meta_data))

# Create top annotation if metadata is available
if(length(available_metadata) > 0) {
  # Prepare annotation data for heatmap columns (which will be the samples).
  top_annotation_df <- meta_data[, available_metadata, drop = FALSE]

  # Check if annotation rows match data rows (samples) before we transpose the matrix.
  if(nrow(top_annotation_df) == nrow(func_log_complex)) {
    # Create color mapping for each variable
    col_mapping <- list()
    for(col_name in available_metadata) {
      x <- top_annotation_df[[col_name]]
      if(is.factor(x) || is.character(x)) {
        unique_vals <- unique(x)
        col_mapping[[col_name]] <- setNames(rainbow(length(unique_vals)), unique_vals)
      } else {
        unique_vals <- unique(x)
        col_mapping[[col_name]] <- setNames(colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(length(unique_vals)), unique_vals)
      }
    }

    # Convert to proper format for ComplexHeatmap
    ha_column <- HeatmapAnnotation(
      df = top_annotation_df,
      col = col_mapping,
      show_annotation_name = TRUE
    )
  } else {
    ha_column <- NULL
  }
} else {
  ha_column <- NULL
}

# Create the ComplexHeatmap
# We transpose the matrix to have functions as rows and samples as columns,
# so the top_annotation (for columns) correctly annotates the samples.
ht <- Heatmap(
  t(as.matrix(func_log_complex)),
  name = "Log10(Expression + 1)",
  col = colorRamp2(seq(min(func_log_complex), max(func_log_complex), length.out = 100),
                   colorRampPalette(c("#F0F8FF", "#D0E6F8", "#A2CFFE", "#7FB0D0", "#1A5490"))(100)),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  top_annotation = ha_column,
  column_title = "Samples",
  row_title = "Functional Categories"
)

# Draw the heatmap
draw(ht,
     padding = unit(c(2, 10, 2, 2), "mm"),
     row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
     column_dend_reorder = TRUE)

# Save the ComplexHeatmap as a PDF (ComplexHeatmap works better with PDF)
pdf("figures/complex_functional_heatmap.pdf", width = 15, height = 12)
draw(ht,
     padding = unit(c(2, 10, 2, 2), "mm"),
     row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
     column_dend_reorder = TRUE)
dev.off()

# Save the ComplexHeatmap as a TIFF
tiff("figures/complex_functional_heatmap.tiff", width = 15, height = 12, units = "in", res = 300)
draw(ht,
     padding = unit(c(2, 10, 2, 2), "mm"),
     row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
     column_dend_reorder = TRUE)
dev.off()

cat("ComplexHeatmap created with top 25 most variable functional categories\n")
cat("Variables included in annotation:", paste(available_metadata, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Complex heatmap saved as 'figures/complex_functional_heatmap.pdf' and 'figures/complex_functional_heatmap.tiff'\n")
```


#### Combined Figure of Key Functional Profiles
```{r bd3-combined-functional-figures, fig.width=16, fig.height=14, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Load required library for combining plots
library(cowplot)

# Note: Since the individual plots were saved as TIFF files, we'll create a combined visualization
# using the same data that generated those individual plots

# Select top pathways based on variance
pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
top_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]  # Top 15 for visualization
func_top <- func_data[, top_pathways, drop = FALSE]

# Create the three plots that would have been saved as separate files

# 1. Treatment functional profiles
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
  # Calculate means by treatment
  treatment_col <- meta_data[["TreatmentCode"]]
  treatment_means <- aggregate(func_top, by = list(Treatment = treatment_col), FUN = mean)
  rownames(treatment_means) <- treatment_means$Treatment
  treatment_means <- treatment_means[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt the data for ggplot
  melted_treatment <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(treatment_means))
  colnames(melted_treatment) <- c("Function", "Treatment", "Expression")

  # Create the treatment heatmap
  p_treatment <- ggplot(melted_treatment, aes(x = Function, y = Treatment, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_treatment$Expression),
                         low = "#2E86AB",
                         mid = "#A2CFFE",
                         high = "#FFFFFF",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Treatment") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)
} else {
  # Create empty plot if TreatmentCode not available
  p_treatment <- ggplot() +
    geom_text(x = 1, y = 1, label = "Treatment data not available", size = 8) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Treatment")
}

# 2. Management and Timepoint profiles
available_vars <- intersect(c("Management", "Timepoint"), colnames(meta_data))
if(length(available_vars) >= 2) {
  # Combine management and timepoint for analysis
  management_col <- meta_data[["Management"]]
  timepoint_col <- meta_data[["Timepoint"]]
  meta_combo <- meta_data
  meta_combo$Management_Timepoint <- paste(management_col, timepoint_col, sep = "_")

  # Calculate means by management and timepoint combination
  combo_means <- aggregate(func_top, by = list(Combo = meta_combo[["Management_Timepoint"]]), FUN = mean)
  rownames(combo_means) <- combo_means$Combo
  combo_means <- combo_means[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt the data for ggplot
  melted_combo <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(combo_means))
  colnames(melted_combo) <- c("Function", "Management_Timepoint", "Expression")

  # Create the management-timepoint heatmap
  p_combo <- ggplot(melted_combo, aes(x = Function, y = Management_Timepoint, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_combo$Expression),
                         low = "#1A5490",
                         mid = "#7FB0D0",
                         high = "#F0F8FF",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Management and Timepoint") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)
} else {
  # Create empty plot if Management and/or Timepoint not available
  p_combo <- ggplot() +
    geom_text(x = 1, y = 1, label = "Management/Timepoint data not available", size = 8) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Management and Timepoint")
}

# 3. Complex heatmap - recreate the data representation
# Select top pathways for the complex heatmap
top_pathways_complex <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:20]  # Top 20 for complex view
func_subset_complex <- func_data[, top_pathways_complex, drop = FALSE]
func_log_complex <- log10(func_subset_complex + 1)

# Create a simplified version of the complex heatmap as a third panel
# Aggregate by a key variable if available
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
  # Create aggregated view by treatment for the complex representation
  treatment_col <- meta_data[["TreatmentCode"]]
  complex_agg <- aggregate(func_log_complex, by = list(Group = treatment_col), FUN = mean)
  rownames(complex_agg) <- complex_agg$Group
  complex_agg <- complex_agg[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt for plotting
  melted_complex <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(complex_agg))
  colnames(melted_complex) <- c("Treatment", "Function", "Expression")

  p_complex <- ggplot(melted_complex, aes(x = Function, y = Treatment, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_complex$Expression),
                         low = "#F0F8FF",
                         mid = "#A2CFFE",
                         high = "#1A5490",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Complex Functional Patterns") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)
} else {
  # Create empty plot if no grouping variable available
  p_complex <- ggplot() +
    geom_text(x = 1, y = 1, label = "Complex pattern data not available", size = 8) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = "Complex Functional Patterns")
}

# Combine the plots using cowplot
combined_plot <- plot_grid(p_treatment, p_combo, p_complex,
                          labels = c("A", "B", "C"),
                          label_size = 20,
                          ncol = 1,
                          align = "v")

# Print the combined plot
print(combined_plot)

# Save the combined plot
ggsave("figures/combined_functional_profiles.tiff",
       combined_plot,
       width = 16,
       height = 14,
       dpi = 300)

cat("Combined figure saved as 'figures/combined_functional_profiles.tiff'\n")
cat("The combined figure includes:\n")
cat("- Functional profiles by treatment (Panel A)\n")
cat("- Functional profiles by management and timepoint (Panel B)\n")
cat("- Complex functional patterns (Panel C)\n")
```

#### Individual Variable Analysis of Microbial Functions

```{r bd3-individual-variable-analysis, fig.width=14, fig.height=12, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Select key variables for individual analysis
key_vars <- c("TreatmentCode", "Management", "Timepoint", "EnvZone", "TrialType")
available_key_vars <- intersect(key_vars, colnames(meta_data))

# Select top 15 most variable pathways for clearer visualization
pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
top15_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]
func_top15 <- func_data[, top15_pathways, drop = FALSE]

# Create individual plots for each variable
if(length(available_key_vars) > 0) {
  for(meta_var in available_key_vars) {
    # Calculate means by the variable
    var_col <- meta_data[[meta_var]]
    agg_data <- aggregate(func_top15, by = list(group = var_col), FUN = mean)
    rownames(agg_data) <- agg_data$group
    agg_data <- agg_data[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

    # Melt the data for ggplot
    melted_data <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(agg_data))
    colnames(melted_data) <- c("Sample", "Function", "Value")
    melted_data[[meta_var]] <- rep(rownames(agg_data), each = ncol(agg_data))

    # Create the plot
    p <- ggplot(melted_data, aes_string(x = "Function", y = "Value", fill = meta_var)) +
      geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_fill_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Set2") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.2),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey95", size = 0.1)
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Microbial Functions by", meta_var),
        x = "Functional Category",
        y = "Expression Level (Log10 + 1)"
      ) +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
      coord_flip()

    print(p)

    # Save the plot
    ggsave(paste0("figures/individual_variable_", tolower(meta_var), "_functional_profiles.tiff"),
           p, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 300)

    # Perform statistical tests for each function
    cat("\nStatistical significance for", meta_var, "on functional categories:\n")

    # Prepare data for ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis tests
    test_data <- data.frame(func_top15)
    test_data[[meta_var]] <- meta_data[[meta_var]]

    # Perform Kruskal-Wallis test for each function (non-parametric alternative to ANOVA)
    kw_results <- data.frame(
      Function = character(),
      Statistic = numeric(),
      P_Value = numeric(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    for(func in top15_pathways) {
      formula_str <- paste0(func, " ~ ", meta_var)
      kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(formula_str), data = test_data)

      kw_results <- rbind(kw_results, data.frame(
        Function = func,
        Statistic = kw_test$statistic,
        P_Value = kw_test$p.value
      ))
    }

    # Adjust p-values for multiple testing
    kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted <- p.adjust(kw_results$P_Value, method = "BH")
    kw_results <- kw_results[order(kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted), ]

    # Show significant differences
    sig_functions <- kw_results[kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted < 0.05, ]
    if(nrow(sig_functions) > 0) {
      cat("Functions significantly affected by", meta_var, "(FDR < 0.05):\n")
      print(kable(sig_functions[1:min(5, nrow(sig_functions)), ], digits = 4))
    } else {
      cat("No functions showed significant differences by", meta_var, "(FDR < 0.05)\n")
    }
    cat("---\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No key variables found in metadata for individual variable analysis\n")
}
```

```{r bd4-load-functional-data, eval = FALSE}
# Load the original COG pathways data

func_data <- cog_data_raw

# Load the metadata separately
meta_data_raw <- read.csv("Data/metadata_simple.csv")

# Match samples between functional data and metadata
common_samples <- intersect(rownames(func_data), meta_data_raw$id)

# Subset both datasets to common samples
func_data <- func_data[common_samples, ]
meta_data <- meta_data_raw[match(common_samples, meta_data_raw$id), ]

# Make sure row names are properly set for both datasets
rownames(func_data) <- common_samples
rownames(meta_data) <- common_samples

cat("Functional data loaded:\n")
cat("- Number of samples with both functional data and metadata:", nrow(func_data), "\n")
cat("- Number of functional categories:", ncol(func_data), "\n")
```

### Heatmap of Microbial Functions

```{r bd4-microbial-function-heatmap, fig.width=15, fig.height=12, eval = FALSE}
# Select key categorical variables for annotation
annotation_cols <- c("TreatmentCode", "Management", "Timepoint", "EnvZone", "TrialType")
available_annotation_cols <- intersect(annotation_cols, colnames(meta_data))

if(length(available_annotation_cols) > 0) {
  # Prepare annotation data
  ann_data <- meta_data[, available_annotation_cols, drop = FALSE]

  # Convert to factor for proper coloring
  for(col in colnames(ann_data)) {
    ann_data[[col]] <- as.factor(ann_data[[col]])
  }

  # Create colors for annotations
  ann_colors <- list()
  for(col in colnames(ann_data)) {
    n_levels <- nlevels(ann_data[[col]])
    if(n_levels <= 8) {
      ann_colors[[col]] <- colorRampPalette(c("#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c", "#d62728", "#9467bd", "#8c564b", "#e377c2", "#7f7f7f"))(n_levels)
      names(ann_colors[[col]]) <- levels(ann_data[[col]])
    } else {
      ann_colors[[col]] <- colorRampPalette(c("#1f77b4", "#aec7e8", "#ff7f0e", "#ffbb78", "#2ca02c", "#98df8a", "#d62728", "#ff9896", "#9467bd", "#c5b0d5", "#8c564b", "#c49c94", "#e377c2", "#f7b6d3", "#7f7f7f", "#c7c7c7"))(n_levels)
      names(ann_colors[[col]]) <- levels(ann_data[[col]])
    }
  }

  # Name the color vectors appropriately
  names(ann_colors) <- colnames(ann_data)

  # To avoid naming conflicts with pheatmap, ensure clean annotation data
  rownames(ann_data) <- rownames(func_log)  # Make sure row names match the matrix
} else {
  ann_data <- NULL
  ann_colors <- NULL
}

# For the heatmap, focus on a subset of pathways

pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
```

### Differential Functional Profiles by Treatment

```{r bd4-treatment-differences, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate average functional profiles by TreatmentCode
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
  # Select top 15 most variable pathways for clearer visualization
  top15_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]
  func_top15 <- func_data[, top15_pathways, drop = FALSE]

  # Calculate means by treatment
  treatment_means <- aggregate(func_top15, by = list(Treatment = meta_data$TreatmentCode), FUN = mean)
  rownames(treatment_means) <- treatment_means$Treatment
  treatment_means <- treatment_means[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt the data for ggplot
  melted_treatment <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(treatment_means))
  colnames(melted_treatment) <- c("Function", "Treatment", "Expression")

  # Create the heatmap
  p_treatment <- ggplot(melted_treatment, aes(x = Function, y = Treatment, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_treatment$Expression),
                         low = "#2E86AB",
                         mid = "#A2CFFE",
                         high = "#FFFFFF",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey95", size = 0.1)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Average Functional Profiles by Treatment") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)

  print(p_treatment)

  # Save the treatment heatmap
  ggsave("figures/treatment_functional_profiles.tiff", p_treatment, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = 300)

  # Statistical comparison between treatments (Kruskal-Wallis for each function)
  kw_results <- data.frame(
    Function = character(),
    KW_Statistic = numeric(),
    P_Value = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  for(func in top15_pathways) {
    formula_str <- paste0(func, " ~ TreatmentCode")
    kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(formula_str), data = cbind(func_data[, func, drop = FALSE], meta_data))
    kw_results <- rbind(kw_results, data.frame(
      Function = func,
      KW_Statistic = kw_test$statistic,
      P_Value = kw_test$p.value
    ))
  }

  # Adjust p-values for multiple testing
  kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted <- p.adjust(kw_results$P_Value, method = "BH")
  kw_results <- kw_results[order(kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted), ]

  # Show significant differences
  sig_functions <- kw_results[kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted < 0.05, ]
  if(nrow(sig_functions) > 0) {
    cat("\nFunctions significantly different by treatment (FDR < 0.05):\n")
    print(kable(sig_functions, digits = 4))
  } else {
    cat("\nNo functions showed significant differences by treatment (FDR < 0.05)\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("TreatmentCode variable not available in metadata\n")
}
```
