#### Advanced Heatmaps with ComplexHeatmap

```{r bd4-complex-heatmap-analysis, fig.width=15, fig.height=12, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Prepare data for ComplexHeatmap
# Select top pathways based on variance
pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
top_pathways_complex <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:25]  # Top 25 for ComplexHeatmap
func_subset_complex <- func_data[, top_pathways_complex, drop = FALSE]

# Log-transform the data for better visualization
func_log_complex <- log10(func_subset_complex + 1)

# Prepare annotation data for ComplexHeatmap
selected_metadata <- c("TreatmentCode", "Management", "Timepoint", "EnvZone")
available_metadata <- intersect(selected_metadata, colnames(meta_data))

# Create top annotation if metadata is available
if(length(available_metadata) > 0) {
  # Prepare annotation data for heatmap columns (which will be the samples).
  top_annotation_df <- meta_data[, available_metadata, drop = FALSE]

  # Check if annotation rows match data rows (samples) before we transpose the matrix.
  if(nrow(top_annotation_df) == nrow(func_log_complex)) {
    # Create color mapping for each variable
    col_mapping <- list()
    for(col_name in available_metadata) {
      x <- top_annotation_df[[col_name]]
      if(is.factor(x) || is.character(x)) {
        unique_vals <- unique(x)
        col_mapping[[col_name]] <- setNames(rainbow(length(unique_vals)), unique_vals)
      } else {
        unique_vals <- unique(x)
        col_mapping[[col_name]] <- setNames(colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(length(unique_vals)), unique_vals)
      }
    }

    # Convert to proper format for ComplexHeatmap
    ha_column <- HeatmapAnnotation(
      df = top_annotation_df,
      col = col_mapping,
      show_annotation_name = TRUE
    )
  } else {
    ha_column <- NULL
  }
} else {
  ha_column <- NULL
}

# Create the ComplexHeatmap
# We transpose the matrix to have functions as rows and samples as columns,
# so the top_annotation (for columns) correctly annotates the samples.
ht <- Heatmap(
  t(as.matrix(func_log_complex)),
  name = "Log10(Expression + 1)",
  col = colorRamp2(seq(min(func_log_complex), max(func_log_complex), length.out = 100),
                   colorRampPalette(c("#F0F8FF", "#D0E6F8", "#A2CFFE", "#7FB0D0", "#1A5490"))(100)),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  top_annotation = ha_column,
  column_title = "Samples",
  row_title = "Functional Categories"
)

# Draw the heatmap
draw(ht,
     padding = unit(c(2, 10, 2, 2), "mm"),
     row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
     column_dend_reorder = TRUE)

# Save the ComplexHeatmap as a PDF (ComplexHeatmap works better with PDF)
pdf("figures/complex_functional_heatmap.pdf", width = 15, height = 12)
draw(ht,
     padding = unit(c(2, 10, 2, 2), "mm"),
     row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
     column_dend_reorder = TRUE)
dev.off()

# Save the ComplexHeatmap as a TIFF
tiff("figures/complex_functional_heatmap.tiff", width = 15, height = 12, units = "in", res = 300)
draw(ht,
     padding = unit(c(2, 10, 2, 2), "mm"),
     row_dend_reorder = TRUE,
     column_dend_reorder = TRUE)
dev.off()

cat("ComplexHeatmap created with top 25 most variable functional categories\n")
cat("Variables included in annotation:", paste(available_metadata, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Complex heatmap saved as 'figures/complex_functional_heatmap.pdf' and 'figures/complex_functional_heatmap.tiff'\n")
```


#### Combined Figure of Key Functional Profiles
```{r bd4-combined-functional-figures, fig.width=16, fig.height=14, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Load required library for combining plots
library(cowplot)

# Note: Since the individual plots were saved as TIFF files, we'll create a combined visualization
# using the same data that generated those individual plots

# Select top pathways based on variance
pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
top_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]  # Top 15 for visualization
func_top <- func_data[, top_pathways, drop = FALSE]

# Create the three plots that would have been saved as separate files

# 1. Treatment functional profiles
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
  # Calculate means by treatment
  treatment_col <- meta_data[["TreatmentCode"]]
  treatment_means <- aggregate(func_top, by = list(Treatment = treatment_col), FUN = mean)
  rownames(treatment_means) <- treatment_means$Treatment
  treatment_means <- treatment_means[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt the data for ggplot
  melted_treatment <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(treatment_means))
  colnames(melted_treatment) <- c("Function", "Treatment", "Expression")

  # Create the treatment heatmap
  p_treatment <- ggplot(melted_treatment, aes(x = Function, y = Treatment, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_treatment$Expression),
                         low = "#2E86AB",
                         mid = "#A2CFFE",
                         high = "#FFFFFF",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Treatment") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)
} else {
  # Create empty plot if TreatmentCode not available
  p_treatment <- ggplot() +
    geom_text(x = 1, y = 1, label = "Treatment data not available", size = 8) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Treatment")
}

# 2. Management and Timepoint profiles
available_vars <- intersect(c("Management", "Timepoint"), colnames(meta_data))
if(length(available_vars) >= 2) {
  # Combine management and timepoint for analysis
  management_col <- meta_data[["Management"]]
  timepoint_col <- meta_data[["Timepoint"]]
  meta_combo <- meta_data
  meta_combo$Management_Timepoint <- paste(management_col, timepoint_col, sep = "_")

  # Calculate means by management and timepoint combination
  combo_means <- aggregate(func_top, by = list(Combo = meta_combo[["Management_Timepoint"]]), FUN = mean)
  rownames(combo_means) <- combo_means$Combo
  combo_means <- combo_means[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt the data for ggplot
  melted_combo <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(combo_means))
  colnames(melted_combo) <- c("Function", "Management_Timepoint", "Expression")

  # Create the management-timepoint heatmap
  p_combo <- ggplot(melted_combo, aes(x = Function, y = Management_Timepoint, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_combo$Expression),
                         low = "#1A5490",
                         mid = "#7FB0D0",
                         high = "#F0F8FF",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Management and Timepoint") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)
} else {
  # Create empty plot if Management and/or Timepoint not available
  p_combo <- ggplot() +
    geom_text(x = 1, y = 1, label = "Management/Timepoint data not available", size = 8) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = "Functional Profiles by Management and Timepoint")
}

# 3. Complex heatmap - recreate the data representation
# Select top pathways for the complex heatmap
top_pathways_complex <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:20]  # Top 20 for complex view
func_subset_complex <- func_data[, top_pathways_complex, drop = FALSE]
func_log_complex <- log10(func_subset_complex + 1)

# Create a simplified version of the complex heatmap as a third panel
# Aggregate by a key variable if available
if("TreatmentCode" %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
  # Create aggregated view by treatment for the complex representation
  treatment_col <- meta_data[["TreatmentCode"]]
  complex_agg <- aggregate(func_log_complex, by = list(Group = treatment_col), FUN = mean)
  rownames(complex_agg) <- complex_agg$Group
  complex_agg <- complex_agg[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

  # Melt for plotting
  melted_complex <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(complex_agg))
  colnames(melted_complex) <- c("Treatment", "Function", "Expression")

  p_complex <- ggplot(melted_complex, aes(x = Function, y = Treatment, fill = Expression)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(midpoint = median(melted_complex$Expression),
                         low = "#F0F8FF",
                         mid = "#A2CFFE",
                         high = "#1A5490",
                         name = "Log10(Expression + 1)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
    labs(title = "Complex Functional Patterns") +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 0.8)
} else {
  # Create empty plot if no grouping variable available
  p_complex <- ggplot() +
    geom_text(x = 1, y = 1, label = "Complex pattern data not available", size = 8) +
    theme_void() +
    labs(title = "Complex Functional Patterns")
}

# Combine the plots using cowplot
combined_plot <- plot_grid(p_treatment, p_combo, p_complex,
                          labels = c("A", "B", "C"),
                          label_size = 20,
                          ncol = 1,
                          align = "v")

# Print the combined plot
```

#### Individual Variable Analysis of Microbial Functions

```{r bd4-individual-variable-analysis, fig.width=14, fig.height=12, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# Select key variables for individual analysis
key_vars <- c("TreatmentCode", "Management", "Timepoint", "EnvZone", "TrialType")
available_key_vars <- intersect(key_vars, colnames(meta_data))

# Select top 15 most variable pathways for clearer visualization
pathway_var <- apply(func_data, 2, stats::var)
top15_pathways <- names(sort(pathway_var, decreasing = TRUE))[1:15]
func_top15 <- func_data[, top15_pathways, drop = FALSE]

# Create individual plots for each variable
if(length(available_key_vars) > 0) {
  for(meta_var in available_key_vars) {
    # Calculate means by the variable
    var_col <- meta_data[[meta_var]]
    agg_data <- aggregate(func_top15, by = list(group = var_col), FUN = mean)
    rownames(agg_data) <- agg_data$group
    agg_data <- agg_data[, -1]  # Remove grouping column

    # Melt the data for ggplot
    melted_data <- reshape2::melt(as.matrix(agg_data))
    colnames(melted_data) <- c("Sample", "Function", "Value")
    melted_data[[meta_var]] <- rep(rownames(agg_data), each = ncol(agg_data))

    # Create the plot
    p <- ggplot(melted_data, aes_string(x = "Function", y = "Value", fill = meta_var)) +
      geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_fill_brewer(type = "qual", palette = "Set2") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.2),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey95", size = 0.1)
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Microbial Functions by", meta_var),
        x = "Functional Category",
        y = "Expression Level (Log10 + 1)"
      ) +
      guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
      coord_flip()

    print(p)

    # Save the plot
    ggsave(paste0("figures/individual_variable_", tolower(meta_var), "_functional_profiles.tiff"),
           p, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = 300)

    # Perform statistical tests for each function
    cat("\nStatistical significance for", meta_var, "on functional categories:\n")

    # Prepare data for ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis tests
    test_data <- data.frame(func_top15)
    test_data[[meta_var]] <- meta_data[[meta_var]]

    # Perform Kruskal-Wallis test for each function (non-parametric alternative to ANOVA)
    kw_results <- data.frame(
      Function = character(),
      Statistic = numeric(),
      P_Value = numeric(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    for(func in top15_pathways) {
      formula_str <- paste0(func, " ~ ", meta_var)
      kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(formula_str), data = test_data)

      kw_results <- rbind(kw_results, data.frame(
        Function = func,
        Statistic = kw_test$statistic,
        P_Value = kw_test$p.value
      ))
    }

    # Adjust p-values for multiple testing
    kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted <- p.adjust(kw_results$P_Value, method = "BH")
    kw_results <- kw_results[order(kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted), ]

    # Show significant differences
    sig_functions <- kw_results[kw_results$P_Value_Adjusted < 0.05, ]
    if(nrow(sig_functions) > 0) {
      cat("Functions significantly affected by", meta_var, "(FDR < 0.05):\n")
      print(kable(sig_functions[1:min(5, nrow(sig_functions)), ], digits = 4))
    } else {
      cat("No functions showed significant differences by", meta_var, "(FDR < 0.05)\n")
    }
    cat("---\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No key variables found in metadata for individual variable analysis\n")
}
```

### Alpha Diversity

```{r da1-alpha-diversity, eval = FALSE}
alpha_df <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    total_reads = rowSums(count_matrix),
    Observed = vegan::specnumber(count_matrix),
    Shannon = vegan::diversity(count_matrix, index = "shannon"),
    Simpson = vegan::diversity(count_matrix, index = "simpson"),
    Evenness = ifelse(Observed > 1, Shannon / log(Observed), NA_real_)
  )

pd_df <- picante::pd(count_matrix, tree, include.root = FALSE)
alpha_df$Faith_PD <- pd_df$PD[match(alpha_df$sample_id, rownames(pd_df))]

knitr::kable(summary(alpha_df[, c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Evenness", "Faith_PD")]))
```

### Kruskal Tests Across Metadata Variables

```{r da1-alpha-stats, eval = FALSE}
run_kruskal <- function(metric, group_var) {
  subset_df <- alpha_df %>%
    select(all_of(c(metric, group_var))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[metric]]), !is.na(.data[[group_var]]), .data[[group_var]] != "")

  if (dplyr::n_distinct(subset_df[[group_var]]) < 2) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  test <- kruskal.test(stats::as.formula(paste(metric, "~", group_var)), data = subset_df)
  tibble::tibble(metric = metric, variable = group_var, statistic = unname(test$statistic), p_value = test$p.value)
}

alpha_stats <- bind_rows(lapply(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Evenness", "Faith_PD"), function(metric) {
  bind_rows(lapply(group_vars, function(var) run_kruskal(metric, var)))
}))

knitr::kable(alpha_stats)
```

### Rarefaction Analysis

```{r da2-rarefaction, eval = FALSE}
# Check minimum sequencing depth
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(ps2))
cat("Minimum sequencing depth:", min_depth, "\n")

# Rarefaction curve data
rarefaction_depth <- 3109  # Adjust based on your data

# Rarefy to even depth
ps_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(
  ps2,
  sample.size = rarefaction_depth,
  rngseed = 123,
  replace = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("After rarefaction:\n")
cat("Samples remaining:", nsamples(ps_rarefied), "\n")
cat("Taxa remaining:", ntaxa(ps_rarefied), "\n")
```

### Alpha Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Alpha Diversity Metrics

```{r da2-alpha-diversity, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate standard alpha diversity metrics - Only Observed, Shannon, Evenness, and PD
alpha_div <- estimate_richness(
  ps_rarefied,
  measures = c("Observed", "Shannon")
)

# Add sample metadata
alpha_div$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_div)
alpha_df <- merge(alpha_div, metadata_merged, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "row.names")


# Calculate Pielou's Evenness
alpha_df$Evenness <- alpha_df$Shannon / log(alpha_df$Observed)

# Faith's PD (if tree is available) - IMPROVED VERSION WITH ERROR HANDLING
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_rarefied, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  otu_mat <- as.data.frame(t(otu_table(ps_rarefied)))
  tree <- phy_tree(ps_rarefied)

  # Check for taxa name compatibility to prevent "replacement has length zero" error
  otu_taxa <- colnames(otu_mat)  # After transposing, taxa names become column names
  tree_taxa <- tree$tip.label

  # Find intersection of taxa
  common_taxa <- intersect(otu_taxa, tree_taxa)

  if(length(common_taxa) == 0) {
    cat("Warning: No overlapping taxa found between OTU table and phylogenetic tree!\n")
    alpha_df$PD <- NA
  } else {
    # Filter OTU table to only include taxa present in the tree
    otu_filtered <- otu_mat[, common_taxa, drop = FALSE]

    # Ensure the tree also only contains the common taxa
    tree_filtered <- tryCatch({
      drop.tip(tree, setdiff(tree$tip.label, common_taxa))
    }, error = function(e) {
      cat("Error filtering tree:", e$message, "\n")
      return(NULL)
    })

    if(is.null(tree_filtered)) {
      cat("Failed to filter phylogenetic tree - skipping PD calculation\n")
      alpha_df$PD <- NA
    } else {
      # Double-check that taxa match
      if(identical(sort(colnames(otu_filtered)), sort(tree_filtered$tip.label))) {
        tryCatch({
          # Calculate PD using picante with the filtered data
          pd_result <- pd(otu_filtered, tree_filtered, include.root = FALSE)

          # Match samples correctly
          alpha_df$PD <- pd_result$PD[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]

          # Fill in any missing values with 0
          alpha_df$PD[is.na(alpha_df$PD)] <- 0

          cat("Faith's PD successfully calculated for", sum(!is.na(pd_result$PD)), "samples\n")
        }, error = function(e) {
          cat("Error in PD calculation:", e$message, "\n")
          alpha_df$PD <- NA
        })
      } else {
        cat("Taxa in filtered OTU table and tree still don't match - skipping PD calculation\n")
        alpha_df$PD <- NA
      }
    }
  }
} else {
  cat("No phylogenetic tree available - skipping Faith's PD calculation\n")
  alpha_df$PD <- NA
}

# Summary statistics - Only Observed, Shannon, Evenness, and PD
alpha_summary <- alpha_df %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(Observed, Shannon, Evenness),
           list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
  )

cat("Alpha Diversity Summary:\n")
print(t(alpha_summary))
```


#### Statistical Tests for Alpha Diversity by All Variables

```{r da2-u1, eval = FALSE}
# Kruskal-Wallis tests by all specified variables
alpha_metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Evenness", "PD")

# Function to run Kruskal-Wallis tests for a variable
run_kruskal_tests <- function(data, var_name, metrics) {
  if(!var_name %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("Variable", var_name, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  results_list <- list()

  for(metric in metrics) {
    if(!metric %in% colnames(data)) next

    # Check if the variable has more than one unique value to avoid "all observations in same group" error
    var_values <- data[[var_name]]
    var_values <- var_values[!is.na(var_values)]  # Remove NAs for counting unique values

    if(length(unique(var_values)) <= 1) {
      # If there's only one group, we can't run Kruskal-Wallis test
      result_df <- data.frame(
        Metric = metric,
        Chi_squared = NA,
        df = NA,
        p_value = NA,
        Significance = "NA (single group)"
      )
    } else {
      # Only run the test if there are multiple groups
      formula_str <- paste(metric, "~", var_name)

      tryCatch({
        test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(formula_str), data = data)

        result_df <- data.frame(
          Metric = metric,
          Chi_squared = round(test$statistic, 3),
          df = test$parameter,
          p_value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3),
          Significance = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                               ifelse(test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                                     ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
        )
      }, error = function(e) {
        # Handle any other errors in the test
        cat("Error in Kruskal-Wallis test for", metric, "vs", var_name, ":", e$message, "\n")
        result_df <- data.frame(
          Metric = metric,
          Chi_squared = NA,
          df = NA,
          p_value = NA,
          Significance = paste("Error:", e$message)
        )
      })
    }

    results_list[[metric]] <- result_df
  }

  return(do.call(rbind, results_list))
}

# Function to run Dunn's post-hoc tests for a variable
run_dunn_tests <- function(data, var_name, metrics) {
  if(!var_name %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("Variable", var_name, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  results_list <- list()

  for(metric in metrics) {
    if(!metric %in% colnames(data)) next

    # Perform Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction
    if(require(FSA, quietly = TRUE)) {
      formula_str <- as.formula(paste(metric, "~", var_name))
      
      tryCatch({
        dunn_test <- dunnTest(formula_str, data = data, method = "bonferroni")

        # Extract results
        dunn_results <- dunn_test$res
        if(!is.null(dunn_results)) {
          dunn_results$Metric <- metric
          
          # Parse Comparison column to get group1 and group2
          if("Comparison" %in% colnames(dunn_results)) {
            split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_results$Comparison), " - ")
            dunn_results$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, function(x) x[1])
            dunn_results$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, function(x) x[2])
          }
          
          # Add significance column
          dunn_results$signif <- ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.001, "***",
                               ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.01, "**",
                                     ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
          
          # Reorder columns to put Metric first
          cols_to_keep <- c("Metric", "group1", "group2", "Z", "P.unadj", "P.adj", "signif")
          cols_to_keep <- intersect(cols_to_keep, colnames(dunn_results))
          dunn_results <- dunn_results[, cols_to_keep]
          results_list[[metric]] <- dunn_results
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("Error in Dunn's test for", metric, ":", e$message, "\n")
      })
    } else {
      cat("FSA package not available for Dunn's test.\n")
      return(NULL)
    }
  }

  return(do.call(rbind, results_list))
}

# Function to calculate group letters from Dunn's test results
calculate_group_letters <- function(dunn_results, var_name, metric) {
  if(is.null(dunn_results) || nrow(dunn_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Filter results for the specific metric
  metric_results <- dunn_results[dunn_results$Metric == metric, ]

  if(nrow(metric_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Create comparison names for multcompLetters
  # It expects "Group1-Group2"
  comparisons <- paste(metric_results$group1, metric_results$group2, sep = "-")
  p_values <- metric_results$P.adj
  names(p_values) <- comparisons
  
  # Calculate letters using multcompView
  tryCatch({
    mcl <- multcompView::multcompLetters(p_values, threshold = 0.05)
    
    # Create result dataframe
    group_letters <- data.frame(
      group = names(mcl$Letters),
      letter = mcl$Letters,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    return(group_letters)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error calculating letters for", metric, ":", e$message, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  })
}
```

#### Alpha Diversity Plots with Significance Letters
```{r da2-alpha-plots-with-letters, fig.width=12, fig.height=15, eval = FALSE}

# Create plots for all specified variables if they exist in the dataset
attach(alpha_df)
plots_list <- list()

# Define publication quality theme for alpha plots
pub_theme <- theme(
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.box = "horizontal",
  axis.text.x = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
  text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
  panel.border = element_blank(),
  axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
)

# Define a function to add significance letters to plots
add_significance_letters <- function(data, var_name, metric, dunn_results) {
  if(is.null(dunn_results) || nrow(dunn_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Get group letters for the specific metric
  group_letters <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_results, var_name, metric)

  if(is.null(group_letters) || nrow(group_letters) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Create a mapping of group to letter
  group_to_letter <- setNames(group_letters$letter, as.character(group_letters$group))

  # Add letters to the data frame
  data_with_letters <- data
  data_with_letters$letter_labels <- ""
  for(grp in names(group_to_letter)) {
    data_with_labels_idx <- data_with_letters[[var_name]] == grp
    data_with_letters$letter_labels[data_with_labels_idx] <- group_to_letter[grp]
  }

  return(data_with_letters)
}

          geom_text(data = data_with_letters,
                    aes_string(x = "Partner.x", y = paste0("max(", metric, ") * 1.05"), label = "letter_labels"),
                    inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 0, size = 6) +
          theme_bw() +
          labs(y = metric, x = "Partner") +
          pub_theme
      } else {
        p <- ggboxplot(alpha_df, x = "Partner.x", y = metric,
                       fill = "Partner.x") +
          scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
          geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
          theme_bw() +
          labs(y = metric, x = "Partner") +
          pub_theme
      }
    } else {
      p <- ggboxplot(alpha_df, x = "Partner.x", y = metric,
                     fill = "Partner.x") +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        labs(y = metric, x = "Partner") +
        theme_bw() +
        pub_theme
    }

    # Add Kruskal-Wallis result annotation
    if(!is.null(partner_kw)) {
      kw_row <- partner_kw[partner_kw$Metric == metric, ]
      if(nrow(kw_row) > 0) {
        kw_label <- paste0("KW p = ", kw_row$p_value, " ", kw_row$Significance)
        p <- p + annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = kw_label, hjust = -0.1, vjust = -0.5, size = 4)
      }
    }

    plots_list[[plot_name]] <- p
  }
}


# By Pool

# Display all plots in a grid
if(length(plots_list) > 0) {
  # Create figures directory if it doesn't exist
  if (!dir.exists("figures")) {
    dir.create("figures")
  }

  # Calculate number of rows needed for the grid
  n_plots <- length(plots_list)
  n_cols <- 2  # Fixed number of columns
  n_rows <- ceiling(n_plots / n_cols)

  # Create the grid of plots
  combined_plot <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = plots_list, ncol = n_cols)
  print(combined_plot)

  # Save combined plot
  ggsave("figures/alpha_diversity_combined.tiff", combined_plot, width = 16, height = n_rows * 4, limitsize = FALSE, dpi = 300)

  # Save individual plots
  for(plot_name in names(plots_list)) {
    ggsave(paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_", plot_name, ".tiff"), plots_list[[plot_name]], width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  }

  # Create and save combined plots for each metric (Index) where all variables are in one plot
  var_prefixes <- c("TreatmentCode", "Timepoint")
  
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    metric_plots <- list()
    for(var in var_prefixes) {
      plot_key <- paste0(var, "_", metric)
      if(plot_key %in% names(plots_list)) {
        metric_plots[[plot_key]] <- plots_list[[plot_key]]
      }
    }
    
    if(length(metric_plots) > 0) {
      # Calculate layout
      n_m_plots <- length(metric_plots)
      n_m_cols <- min(2, n_m_plots)
      n_m_rows <- ceiling(n_m_plots / n_m_cols)
      
      # Create grid
      metric_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = metric_plots, ncol = n_m_cols)
      
      # Print to report
      print(metric_combined)
      
      # Save
      ggsave(paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_all_variables_", metric, ".tiff"), 
             metric_combined, 
             width = 12, height = 4 * n_m_rows, 
             limitsize = FALSE, dpi = 300)
    }
  }

  # Create and save combined plot for Pool variable containing all indices
  pool_plots <- list()
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    plot_key <- paste0("Pool_", metric)
    if(plot_key %in% names(plots_list)) {
      pool_plots[[plot_key]] <- plots_list[[plot_key]]
    }
  }

  if(length(pool_plots) > 0) {
    # Calculate layout
    n_p_plots <- length(pool_plots)
    n_p_cols <- 3
    n_p_rows <- ceiling(n_p_plots / n_p_cols)

    # Create grid
    pool_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = pool_plots, ncol = n_p_cols)

    # Print to report
    print(pool_combined)

    # Save
    ggsave("figures/alpha_diversity_Pool_all_indices.tiff",
           pool_combined,
           width = 15, height = 6 * n_p_rows,
           limitsize = FALSE, dpi = 300)
  }

  # Create and save combined plot for Partner variable containing all indices
  partner_plots <- list()
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    plot_key <- paste0("Partner_", metric)
    if(plot_key %in% names(plots_list)) {
      partner_plots[[plot_key]] <- plots_list[[plot_key]]
    }
  }

  if(length(partner_plots) > 0) {
    # Calculate layout
    n_pr_plots <- length(partner_plots)
    n_pr_cols <- 3
    n_pr_rows <- ceiling(n_pr_plots / n_pr_cols)

    # Create grid
    partner_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = partner_plots, ncol = n_pr_cols)

    # Print to report
    print(partner_combined)

    # Save
    ggsave("figures/alpha_diversity_Partner_all_indices.tiff",
           partner_combined,
           width = 15, height = 6 * n_pr_rows,
           limitsize = FALSE, dpi = 300)
  }

}
detach(alpha_df)
```

```{r da2-combined-partner-plots, fig.width=14, fig.height=12, eval = FALSE}
# Load required libraries
library(cowplot)

# Create combined plots for treatment and timepoint faceted by partner
# This will combine all the individual plots that were created earlier

# Collect all treatment plots faceted by partner
treatment_plots_combined <- list()
timepoint_plots_combined <- list()

# Since we don't have direct access to the individual plots here,
# we'll create a new section to generate combined plots
# First, let's check which alpha diversity metrics were plotted
alpha_metrics_plotted <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Evenness"), colnames(alpha_df))

# Create combined plots for each metric
if(length(alpha_metrics_plotted) > 0) {
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_plotted) {
    # TreatmentCode plots faceted by Partner
    if("TreatmentCode.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df) && "Partner.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
      # Calculate Kruskal-Wallis p-value for this metric
      tryCatch({
        kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ TreatmentCode.x")), data = alpha_df)
        p_value <- kw_test$p.value
        p_label <- paste0("KW p = ", format.pval(p_value, digits = 3))
      }, error = function(e) {
        p_label <- "KW p = NA"
      })

      p_treatment <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes_string(x = "TreatmentCode.x", y = metric, fill = "TreatmentCode.x")) +
        geom_boxplot() +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        facet_wrap(~Partner.x, scales = "free") +
        labs(y = metric, x = "Treatment Code",
             title = paste("Alpha Diversity:", metric, "by Treatment Code faceted by Partner"),
             caption = p_label) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.box = "horizontal",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "italic")
        )

      treatment_plots_combined[[metric]] <- p_treatment
    }

    # Timepoint plots faceted by Partner
    if("Timepoint.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df) && "Partner.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
      # Calculate Kruskal-Wallis p-value for this metric
      tryCatch({
        kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ Timepoint.x")), data = alpha_df)
        p_value <- kw_test$p.value
        p_label <- paste0("KW p = ", format.pval(p_value, digits = 3))
      }, error = function(e) {
        p_label <- "KW p = NA"
      })

      p_timepoint <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes_string(x = "Timepoint.x", y = metric, fill = "Timepoint.x")) +
        geom_boxplot() +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        facet_wrap(~Partner.x, scales = "free") +
        labs(y = metric, x = "Timepoint",
             title = paste("Alpha Diversity:", metric, "by Timepoint faceted by Partner"),
             caption = p_label) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.box = "horizontal",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "italic")
        )

      timepoint_plots_combined[[metric]] <- p_timepoint
    }
  }

  # Print combined treatment plots
  if(length(treatment_plots_combined) > 0) {
    n_treatment_plots <- length(treatment_plots_combined)
    n_treatment_cols <- min(2, n_treatment_plots)  # Maximum 2 columns
    n_treatment_rows <- ceiling(n_treatment_plots / n_treatment_cols)

    combined_treatment_grid <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = treatment_plots_combined, ncol = n_treatment_cols)

    print(combined_treatment_grid)

    # Save the combined treatment plot
    ggsave("figures/combined_alpha_diversity_by_treatment_faceted_by_partner.tiff",
           combined_treatment_grid,
           width = 14, height = 7 * n_treatment_rows,
           dpi = 300)
  }

  # Print combined timepoint plots
  if(length(timepoint_plots_combined) > 0) {
    n_timepoint_plots <- length(timepoint_plots_combined)
    n_timepoint_cols <- min(2, n_timepoint_plots)  # Maximum 2 columns
    n_timepoint_rows <- ceiling(n_timepoint_plots / n_timepoint_cols)

    combined_timepoint_grid <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = timepoint_plots_combined, ncol = n_timepoint_cols)

    print(combined_timepoint_grid)

    # Save the combined timepoint plot
    ggsave("figures/combined_alpha_diversity_by_timepoint_faceted_by_partner.tiff",
           combined_timepoint_grid,
           width = 14, height = 7 * n_timepoint_rows,
           dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

#### Alpha Diversity Plots by facet_wrapping Partner with different TreatmentCodes

```{r da2-alpha-plots-facet-partner-treatment, fig.width=5, fig.height=8, eval = FALSE}
# Check if required columns exist
if(all(c("Partner.x", "TreatmentCode.x") %in% colnames(alpha_df))) {
  # Define alpha diversity metrics to plot - Only Observed, Shannon, and Evenness (no PD)
  alpha_metrics_to_plot <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Evenness"), colnames(alpha_df))

  # Initialize dataframe to store Kruskal-Wallis results
  kw_partner_results <- data.frame()

  # Loop through each metric
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    if(metric %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
      
      # Calculate significance letters for each Partner subset
      sig_letters_df <- data.frame()
      kw_ann_df <- data.frame()
      partners <- unique(as.character(alpha_df$Partner.x[!is.na(alpha_df$Partner.x)]))
      
      for(pt in partners) {
        subset_data <- alpha_df[alpha_df$Partner.x == pt, ]
        # Ensure factor and drop unused levels for this subset
        subset_data$TreatmentCode.x <- factor(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x)
        subset_data$TreatmentCode.x <- droplevels(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x)
        
        if(nlevels(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x) > 1) {
          # Calculate Kruskal-Wallis test for this facet
          tryCatch({
            kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ TreatmentCode.x")), data = subset_data)
            kw_row <- data.frame(
              Metric = metric,
              Partner = pt,
              Chi_squared = round(kw_test$statistic, 3),
              df = kw_test$parameter,
              p_value = kw_test$p.value,
              Significance = ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns"))),
              row.names = NULL
            )
            kw_partner_results <- rbind(kw_partner_results, kw_row)
            
            # Create annotation for plot
            p_label <- ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.3f", kw_test$p.value)))
            kw_ann_df <- rbind(kw_ann_df, data.frame(
              Partner.x = pt,
              label = paste0("KW: ", p_label),
              x = nlevels(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x) / 2 + 0.5,
              y = max(subset_data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25,
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE
            ))
          }, error = function(e) { })

          tryCatch({
            # Run Dunn's test using FSA package
            if(require(FSA, quietly = TRUE)) {
              dunn_res <- dunnTest(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ TreatmentCode.x")), 
                                   data = subset_data, 
                                   method = "bonferroni")$res
              
              if(!is.null(dunn_res)) {
                 # Format results to match what calculate_group_letters expects
                 dunn_res$Metric <- metric
                 split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_res$Comparison), " - ")
                 dunn_res$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 1)
                 dunn_res$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 2)
                 
                 # Reuse the existing function to get letters
                 letters_res <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_res, "TreatmentCode.x", metric)
                 
                 if(!is.null(letters_res)) {
                   letters_res$Partner.x <- pt
                   # Calculate y position for labels (slightly above max value of the subset)
                   letters_res$y_pos <- max(subset_data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
                   sig_letters_df <- rbind(sig_letters_df, letters_res)
                 }
              }
            }
          }, error = function(e) { })
        }
      }

      # Create the plot with facet wrap by Partner and TreatmentCode on x-axis
      p <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes_string(x = "TreatmentCode.x", y = metric, fill = "TreatmentCode.x")) +
        geom_boxplot() +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        facet_wrap(~Partner.x, scales = "free") +  # Facet by Partner with free scales to show only implemented treatments
        labs(y = metric, x = "Treatment Code", fill = "Treatment Code", title = paste("Alpha Diversity:", metric, "by Treatment Code across Partners")) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
          legend.position = "none",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgray"),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
        )
      
      # Add significance letters if available
      if(nrow(sig_letters_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = sig_letters_df, 
                           aes(x = group, y = y_pos, label = letter), 
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4)
      }
      
      # Add Kruskal-Wallis p-values
      if(nrow(kw_ann_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = kw_ann_df,
                           aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, vjust = 0)
      }

      print(p)

      # Save the plot
      ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_", metric, "_by_treatment_faceted_by_partner.tiff"),
             plot = p, width = 5, height = 8, dpi = 300, device = "tiff")
    }
  }
  
  # Export Kruskal-Wallis results to CSV
  if(nrow(kw_partner_results) > 0) {
    if (!dir.exists("results")) dir.create("results")
    write.csv(kw_partner_results, "results/kruskal_wallis_partner_treatment_facets.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("Kruskal-Wallis results for Partner facets saved to 'results/kruskal_wallis_partner_treatment_facets.csv'\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Required columns for Partner-TreatmentCode facet plots not found in alpha_df\n")
}
```

```{r da2-alpha-plots-facet-partner-timepoint, fig.width=4, fig.height=5, eval = FALSE}
  cat("Required columns for Partner-Timepoint facet plots not found in alpha_df\n")
}
```

### Temporal variations
```{r da2-temporal-variations, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, eval = FALSE}
# Subset data for TreatmentCode == "UTC"
if("TreatmentCode.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
  utc_data <- alpha_df[alpha_df$TreatmentCode.x == "UTC", ]
} else {
  # Fallback if column name is different
  utc_data <- alpha_df[alpha_df$TreatmentCode == "UTC", ]
}

# Determine correct column names for Partner and Timepoint
prt_col <- if("Partner.x" %in% colnames(utc_data)) "Partner.x" else "Partner"
time_col <- if("Timepoint.x" %in% colnames(utc_data)) "Timepoint.x" else "Timepoint"

# Check if required columns exist
if(nrow(utc_data) > 0 && all(c(prt_col, time_col) %in% colnames(utc_data))) {

  # Define alpha diversity metrics to plot - Only Observed, Shannon, and Evenness (no PD)
  alpha_metrics_to_plot <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Evenness"), colnames(utc_data))

  # Initialize dataframe to store Kruskal-Wallis results
  kw_temporal_results <- data.frame()

  # Loop through each metric
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    if(metric %in% colnames(utc_data)) {

      # Calculate significance letters for each Partner subset
      sig_letters_df <- data.frame()
      kw_ann_df <- data.frame()
      partners <- unique(as.character(utc_data[[prt_col]][!is.na(utc_data[[prt_col]])]))

      for(prt in partners) {
        subset_data <- utc_data[utc_data[[prt_col]] == prt, ]
        # Ensure factor and drop unused levels
        subset_data[[time_col]] <- factor(subset_data[[time_col]])
        subset_data[[time_col]] <- droplevels(subset_data[[time_col]])

        if(nlevels(subset_data[[time_col]]) > 1) {
          # Calculate Kruskal-Wallis test for this facet
          tryCatch({
            kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~", time_col)), data = subset_data)
            kw_row <- data.frame(
              Metric = metric,
              Partner = prt,
              Chi_squared = round(kw_test$statistic, 3),
              df = kw_test$parameter,
              p_value = kw_test$p.value,
              Significance = ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns"))),
              row.names = NULL
            )
            kw_temporal_results <- rbind(kw_temporal_results, kw_row)

            # Create annotation for plot
            p_label <- ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.3f", kw_test$p.value)))
            ann_row <- data.frame(
              label = paste0("KW: ", p_label),
              x = nlevels(subset_data[[time_col]]) / 2 + 0.5,
              y = -Inf,
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE
            )
            ann_row[[prt_col]] <- prt
            kw_ann_df <- rbind(kw_ann_df, ann_row)
          }, error = function(e) { })

          tryCatch({
            # Run Dunn's test
            if(require(FSA, quietly = TRUE)) {
              dunn_res <- dunnTest(as.formula(paste(metric, "~", time_col)),
                                   data = subset_data,
                                   method = "bonferroni")$res

              if(!is.null(dunn_res)) {
                 # Format results
                 dunn_res$Metric <- metric
                 split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_res$Comparison), " - ")
                 dunn_res$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 1)
                 dunn_res$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 2)

                 letters_res <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_res, time_col, metric)

                 if(!is.null(letters_res)) {
                   letters_res[[prt_col]] <- prt
                   # Calculate y position
                   letters_res$y_pos <- max(subset_data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
                   sig_letters_df <- rbind(sig_letters_df, letters_res)
                 }
              }
            }
          }, error = function(e) { })
        }
      }

      # Create the plot with facet wrap by Partner and Timepoint on x-axis
      p <- ggplot(utc_data, aes_string(x = time_col, y = metric, fill = time_col)) +
        geom_boxplot() +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", prt_col)), scales = "free") +  # Facet by Partner with free scales
        labs(y = metric, x = "Timepoint", fill = "Timepoint", title = paste("Temporal Variation (UTC):", metric, "by Partner")) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
          legend.position = "none",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgray"),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
        )

      # Add significance letters if available
      if(nrow(sig_letters_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = sig_letters_df,
                           aes(x = group, y = y_pos, label = letter),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4)
      }

      # Add Kruskal-Wallis p-values
      if(nrow(kw_ann_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = kw_ann_df,
                           aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, vjust = -0.5)
      }

      print(p)

      # Save the plot
      ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/temporal_variation_utc_", metric, ".tiff"),
             plot = p, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300, device = "tiff")
    }
  }

  # Export Kruskal-Wallis results to CSV
  if(nrow(kw_temporal_results) > 0) {
    if (!dir.exists("results")) dir.create("results")
    write.csv(kw_temporal_results, "results/kruskal_wallis_temporal_utc_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("Kruskal-Wallis results for Temporal variations (UTC) saved to 'results/kruskal_wallis_temporal_utc_results.csv'\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Required columns for Temporal variations analysis not found in alpha_df\n")
}
```


### Regression between TreatmentCode and TimePoint for the different Partners.

```{r da2-u2, eval = FALSE}
if(all(c("Partner.x", "Timepoint.x", "TreatmentCode.x") %in% colnames(alpha_df))) {

  # Create a copy of the data for regression and convert Timepoint to numeric
  regression_data <- alpha_df
  regression_data$Timepoint_num <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", regression_data$Timepoint.x))

  # Define alpha diversity metrics to model - Only Observed, Shannon, and Evenness (no PD)
  alpha_metrics_to_model <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Evenness"), colnames(regression_data))

  # Get unique partners
  partners <- unique(as.character(regression_data$Partner.x[!is.na(regression_data$Partner.x)]))

  # Loop through each partner
  for(prt in partners) {

    cat(paste("\n\n### Regression Analysis for Partner:", prt, "\n\n"))

    # Subset data for the current partner
    subset_data <- regression_data[regression_data$Partner.x == prt, ]

    # Loop through each alpha diversity metric
    for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_model) {

      cat(paste("\n#### Metric:", metric, "\n"))

      # Define the model formula with interaction
      formula_str <- paste(metric, "~ Timepoint_num * TreatmentCode.x")

      tryCatch({
        # Fit the linear model
        interaction_model <- lm(as.formula(formula_str), data = subset_data)

        # Print model summary
        cat("\n**Model Summary:**\n")
        print(summary(interaction_model))

        # Print ANOVA table to see significance of interaction
        cat("\n**ANOVA Table:**\n")
        print(kable(anova(interaction_model), caption = paste("ANOVA for", metric, "in", prt, "Partner")))

        # Visualize the interaction effect
        if(require(sjPlot, quietly = TRUE)) {
          cat("\n**Interaction Plot:**\n")

          interaction_plot <- plot_model(interaction_model, type = "int") +
            labs(
              title = paste("Interaction of Timepoint and Treatment on", metric),
              subtitle = paste("Partner:", prt),
              x = "Timepoint",
              y = metric
            ) +
            theme_bw() +
            theme(text = element_text(family = "Verdana"))

          print(interaction_plot)

          # Save the plot
          if (!dir.exists("figures")) dir.create("figures")
          ggsave(
            filename = paste0("figures/regression_interaction_", prt, "_", metric, ".tiff"),
            plot = interaction_plot,
            width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300
          )
        }

      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("Could not fit model for", metric, "in", prt, "partner:", e$message, "\n")
      })
    }
  }
} else {
  cat("Required columns for regression analysis not found in alpha_df.\n")
}
```

### Rarefaction Analysis

```{r da3-rarefaction, eval = FALSE}
# Check minimum sequencing depth

rarefaction_depth <- 2500  # Adjust based on your data

# Rarefy to even depth
ps_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(
  ps2,
  sample.size = rarefaction_depth,
  rngseed = 123,
  replace = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

### Alpha Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Alpha Diversity Metrics

```{r da3-alpha-diversity, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate standard alpha diversity metrics
alpha_div <- estimate_richness(
  ps_rarefied,
  measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "ACE")
)

# Calculate effective number of species (Hill numbers)
# Calculate before merging to avoid column name conflicts
alpha_div$Shannon_Effective <- exp(alpha_div$Shannon)
alpha_div$Simpson_Effective <- 1 / (1 - alpha_div$Simpson)

# Add sample metadata
alpha_div$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_div)

# Prepare metadata, removing potential duplicate columns
meta_df <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_rarefied))
dup_cols <- intersect(names(meta_df), names(alpha_div))
dup_cols <- setdiff(dup_cols, "SampleID") # Keep SampleID if it exists
if(length(dup_cols) > 0) {
  meta_df <- meta_df[, !names(meta_df) %in% dup_cols]
}

alpha_df <- merge(alpha_div, meta_df, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "row.names")

# Calculate Pielou's Evenness
alpha_df$Evenness <- alpha_df$Shannon / log(alpha_df$Observed)

# Faith's PD (if tree is available)
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_rarefied, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  otu_mat <- as.data.frame(t(otu_table(ps_rarefied)))
  tree <- phy_tree(ps_rarefied)

  # Check for taxa name compatibility to prevent "replacement has length zero" error
  # Note: After transposing, taxa names become column names
  otu_taxa <- colnames(otu_mat)
  tree_taxa <- tree$tip.label

  # Find intersection of taxa
  common_taxa <- intersect(otu_taxa, tree_taxa)

  if(length(common_taxa) == 0) {
    cat("Warning: No overlapping taxa found between OTU table and phylogenetic tree!\n")
    alpha_df$PD <- NA
    alpha_df$SR <- NA
  } else {
    # Filter OTU table to only include taxa present in the tree
    otu_filtered <- otu_mat[, common_taxa, drop = FALSE]

    # Ensure the tree also only contains the common taxa
    tree_filtered <- drop.tip(tree, setdiff(tree$tip.label, common_taxa))

    # Calculate PD using picante with the filtered data
    pd_result <- pd(otu_filtered, tree_filtered, include.root = FALSE)

    # Match samples correctly
    alpha_df$PD <- pd_result$PD[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
    alpha_df$SR <- pd_result$SR[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
  }
}

# Summary statistics
alpha_summary <- alpha_df %>%
  summarise(
    across(c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson"),
           list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE))),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

cat("Alpha Diversity Summary:\n")
print(t(alpha_summary))
```

#### Statistical Tests for Alpha Diversity

```{r da3-alpha-stats, eval = FALSE}
# Kruskal-Wallis tests by TreatmentCode
alpha_metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1", "InvSimpson")

kw_treatment_results <- lapply(alpha_metrics, function(metric) {
  test <- kruskal.test(reformulate("TreatmentCode", metric), data = alpha_df)
  data.frame(
    Metric = metric,
    Chi_squared = round(test$statistic, 3),
    df = test$parameter,
    p_value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3),
    Significance = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                         ifelse(test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                               ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
  )
})

kw_treatment_df <- do.call(rbind, kw_treatment_results)

kable(kw_treatment_df,
      caption = "Kruskal-Wallis Test: Alpha Diversity by Treatment",
      row.names = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Kruskal-Wallis tests by EnvZone
kw_envzone_results <- lapply(alpha_metrics, function(metric) {
  test <- kruskal.test(reformulate("EnvZone", metric), data = alpha_df)
  data.frame(
    Metric = metric,
    Chi_squared = round(test$statistic, 3),
    df = test$parameter,
    p_value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3),
    Significance = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                         ifelse(test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                               ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
  )
})

kw_envzone_df <- do.call(rbind, kw_envzone_results)

kable(kw_envzone_df,
      caption = "Kruskal-Wallis Test: Alpha Diversity by Environmental Zone",
      row.names = FALSE) %>%
```

#### Pairwise Comparisons (Dunn's Test)

```{r da3-dunn-test, eval = FALSE}
# Dunn's test for Shannon by TreatmentCode

  dunn_shannon_treatment <- dunnTest(Shannon ~ TreatmentCode,
                                      data = alpha_df,
                                      method = "bonferroni")
```

### Beta Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Distance Matrices

#### PCoA Ordination

```{r da3-pcoa-ordination, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, eval = FALSE}
# PCoA with Bray-Curtis
pcoa_bray <- ordinate(ps_rarefied, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")

# Variance explained
var_explained <- pcoa_bray$values$Relative_eig * 100

# PCoA plot by TreatmentCode
pcoa_treatment <- plot_ordination(ps_rarefied, pcoa_bray,
                                   color = "TreatmentCode") +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "PCoA (Bray-Curtis) by Treatment",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_explained[1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_explained[2], 1), "%)")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# PCoA plot by EnvZone
pcoa_envzone <- plot_ordination(ps_rarefied, pcoa_bray,
                                 color = "EnvZone") +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "PCoA (Bray-Curtis) by Environmental Zone",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_explained[1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_explained[2], 1), "%)")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Combined plot
beta_pcoa_plot <- pcoa_treatment / pcoa_envzone

print(beta_pcoa_plot)

ggsave("figures/beta_diversity_pcoa.tiff",
       beta_pcoa_plot, width = 10, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

#### PERMANOVA Analysis

```{r da3-permanova, eval = FALSE}
# Source utility functions
source("utils.R")

# Get metadata for rarefied samples
meta_rarefied <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_rarefied))

# PERMANOVA by TreatmentCode using utility function
permanova_treatment <- run_permanova(
  bray_dist,
  meta_rarefied,
  "TreatmentCode"
)

cat("PERMANOVA: Effect of Treatment on Community Composition\n")
cat("========================================================\n")
print(permanova_treatment)

# PERMANOVA by EnvZone using utility function
permanova_envzone <- run_permanova(
  bray_dist,
  meta_rarefied,
  "EnvZone"
)

cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Environmental Zone\n")
cat("========================================\n")
print(permanova_envzone)

# Combined model - note: this specific interaction model isn't in the utility function
# so we'll keep it as is for this specific case
permanova_combined <- adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ TreatmentCode + EnvZone + TreatmentCode:EnvZone,
  data = meta_rarefied,
  permutations = 999,
  by = "margin"
)

cat("\nPERMANOVA: Combined Model (Treatment + EnvZone + Interaction)\n")
cat("==============================================================\n")
print(permanova_combined)

# Summary table
permanova_summary <- data.frame(
  Factor = c("TreatmentCode", "EnvZone", "Treatment x EnvZone"),
  R2 = c(permanova_treatment$R2[1],
         permanova_envzone$R2[1],
         permanova_combined$R2[3]),
  F_value = c(permanova_treatment$F[1],
              permanova_envzone$F[1],
              permanova_combined$F[3]),
  p_value = c(permanova_treatment$`Pr(>F)`[1],
              permanova_envzone$`Pr(>F)`[1],
              permanova_combined$`Pr(>F)`[3])
)

permanova_summary$Significance <- ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.001, "***",
                                         ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.01, "**",
                                               ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))

kable(permanova_summary,
      caption = "PERMANOVA Summary",
      digits = c(0, 4, 2, 4, 0)) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

#### Beta Dispersion Test (PERMDISP)

```{r da3-betadisper, eval = FALSE}
# Test homogeneity of dispersions - TreatmentCode
betadisper_treatment <- betadisper(bray_dist, meta_rarefied$TreatmentCode)
permdisp_treatment <- permutest(betadisper_treatment, permutations = 999)

cat("Beta Dispersion Test: TreatmentCode\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(permdisp_treatment)

# Test homogeneity of dispersions - EnvZone
betadisper_envzone <- betadisper(bray_dist, meta_rarefied$EnvZone)
permdisp_envzone <- permutest(betadisper_envzone, permutations = 999)

cat("\nBeta Dispersion Test: EnvZone\n")
cat("==============================\n")
print(permdisp_envzone)

# Dispersion interpretation
cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
cat("If PERMDISP p > 0.05: Dispersions are homogeneous (PERMANOVA is valid)\n")
cat("If PERMDISP p < 0.05: Dispersions are heterogeneous (interpret PERMANOVA with caution)\n")
```

### Calculate richness and community composition based on presence or absence

### Preamble: This report demonstrates **beta diversity analysis** using **Jaccard distance** on presence-absence transformed microbiome data. Jaccard distance is particularly appropriate for:

- Presence-absence (binary) data
- Focus on shared species between samples
- Community composition comparisons
- Handling sparse microbiome datasets

#### Setup Color Palette
### final_palette

```{r da4-color-palette, eval = FALSE}
# Define or load your custom color palette
# If you have final_palette already defined, use it
# Otherwise, create one:

n_groups <- length(unique(metadata$TreatmentCode))

# Option 1: Use your existing final_palette
# final_palette <- your_predefined_colors

# Option 2: Create extended palette if needed
if (exists("final_palette") && length(final_palette) >= n_groups) {
  cat("Using existing final_palette palette\n")
} else {
  # Create a color palette with enough colors
  library(RColorBrewer)
  
  # Get all available colors from multiple palettes
  qual_col_pals <- brewer.pal.info[brewer.pal.info$category == 'qual',]
  final_palette <- unlist(mapply(brewer.pal, qual_col_pals$maxcolors, rownames(qual_col_pals)))
  
  # If still not enough, extend with colorRampPalette
  if (length(final_palette) < n_groups) {
    final_palette <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(12, "Set3"))(n_groups)
  }
  
  cat("Created color palette with", length(final_palette), "colors\n")
}

# Show color palette
barplot(rep(1, min(20, length(final_palette))), col = final_palette[1:min(20, length(final_palette))], 
        main = "Color Palette (first 20 colors)", axes = FALSE)
```

### Presence-Absence Transformation

#### Convert to Binary Data

```{r da4-pa-transformation, eval = FALSE}
# Transform abundance data to presence-absence (PA)
ps2_pa <- transform_sample_counts(ps2, function(x) ifelse(x > 0, 1, 0))

cat("Presence-Absence Transformation Complete\n")
cat("Original data type: abundance counts\n")
cat("Transformed data type: binary (0/1)\n")

# Compare before and after for one OTU
example_otu <- taxa_names(ps2)[1]
comparison <- data.frame(
  Sample = sample_names(ps2)[1:10],
  Original = as.vector(otu_table(ps2)[example_otu, 1:10]),
  PA = as.vector(otu_table(ps2_pa)[example_otu, 1:10])
)

kable(comparison, caption = paste("Example transformation for", example_otu))
```


#### Calculate OTU Richness
```{r da4-richness-calculation, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate richness (number of present OTUs per sample) and merge with metadata
richness_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = sample_names(ps2_pa),
  Richness = sample_sums(ps2_pa)
)

# Get metadata, ensuring it matches the samples in ps2_pa
meta_pa <- as(sample_data(ps2_pa), "data.frame") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("PD16S", "dpt", "Total reads", "Richness", "Shannon"))) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Sample")

# Join richness with metadata
richness_df <- left_join(richness_df, meta_pa, by = "Sample")

cat("Structure of the final richness dataframe:\n")
str(richness_df)

```


### Diversity across treaments and partners
```{r da4-u3, eval = FALSE}

richness_summary <- richness_df %>%
 group_by(TreatmentCode) %>%
  summarise(
   N = n(),
     Mean = round(mean(Richness), 2),
   SD = round(sd(Richness), 2),
    Min = min(Richness),
    Max = max(Richness)
 ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Mean))

kable(richness_summary, caption = "OTU Richness Summary by Group")

# Plot
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Ensure TreatmentCode is a factor and drop unused levels per Partner
richness_df <- richness_df %>%
  group_by(Partner) %>%
  mutate(TreatmentCode = factor(TreatmentCode)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Plot faceted by Partner
richness_treatments_jacxard <- ggplot(richness_df, 
                                      aes(x = TreatmentCode,
                                          y = Richness,
                                          fill = TreatmentCode)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = final_palette) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "OTU Richness Distribution by Group",
       x = "Group", y = "Number of Present OTUs") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Partner, scales = "free_x")  # free_x drops empty levels per facet

# Save plot
ggsave("figures/richness_treatments_jacxard.tiff",
       plot = richness_treatments_jacxard, scale = 1,
       width =8, height = 13, units = "cm", dpi = 600)



#  Compute stats per Partner (stratified)

# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(rstatix)
library(multcompView) # Better for generating CLD letters
library(knitr)
library(purrr)

# 1. Summarize richness per Partner × Treatment
richness_summary <- richness_df %>%
  group_by(Partner, TreatmentCode) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(Richness), 2),
    SD = round(sd(Richness), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Run Dunn test per Partner
dunn_results <- richness_df %>%
  group_by(Partner) %>%
  dunn_test(Richness ~ TreatmentCode, p.adjust.method = "BH")

# 3. Generate letters PER Partner
# We use a helper function to convert dunn_test output to letters
get_cld_letters <- function(dunn_sub) {
  # Create a named vector of p-values: "group1-group2" = p.adj
  p_vals <- dunn_sub$p.adj
  names(p_vals) <- paste0(dunn_sub$group1, "-", dunn_sub$group2)
  
  # Generate letters
  res <- multcompLetters(p_vals)
  
  # Return as a clean dataframe
  data.frame(
    TreatmentCode = names(res$Letters),
    Letter = res$Letters,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Apply the function to each Partner and bind results
all_letters <- dunn_results %>%
  group_split(Partner) %>%
  map_df(~{
    partner_name <- unique(.x$Partner)
    letters_df <- get_cld_letters(.x)
    letters_df$Partner <- partner_name
    letters_df
  })

# 4. Join letters back to the summary
final_table <- richness_summary %>%
  left_join(all_letters, by = c("Partner", "TreatmentCode")) %>%
  arrange(Partner, desc(Mean))

# 5. Display table
kable(
  final_table,
  caption = "OTU Richness Summary with Dunn Test Significance Letters (BH Adjusted)"
)


```

```{r da4-u4, eval = FALSE}
  summarise(
    N = n(),

  ) %>%

# Display initial summary table
kable(richness_summary, caption = "OTU Richness Summary by Production Site")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Visualization (Single Variable)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Ensure EnvZone is a factor
richness_df$EnvZone <- factor(richness_df$EnvZone)

richness_EnvZone_jacxard <- ggplot(richness_df, 
                        aes(x = EnvZone, y = Richness, fill = EnvZone)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = final_palette) + 
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "OTU Richness Distribution by Production Site",
       x = "Production Site", 
       y = "Number of Present OTUs") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 1, hjust = 1, size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

# Save plot - Adjusted dimensions for a single panel
ggsave("figures/richness_EnvZone_jacxard.tiff",
       plot = richness_EnvZone_jacxard, width = 6, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 600)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Statistical Analysis & Compact Letter Display (CLD)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
kruskal.test(Richness ~ EnvZone, data = richness_df)#Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 42.628, df = 1, p-value = 6.621e-11
# Run Dunn Test
dunn_results <- richness_df %>%
  dunn_test(Richness ~ EnvZone, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
#1 Richness Continental Mediterranean North   298   117     -6.53 6.62e-11 6.62e-11 ****   

# Create a named vector of p-values for the CLD function
# Format: "Group1-Group2" = p.adj
p_vals <- dunn_results$p.adj
names(p_vals) <- paste0(dunn_results$group1, "-", dunn_results$group2)

# Generate significance letters
cld_output <- multcompLetters(p_vals)

# Convert letters to a clean dataframe for joining
cld_df <- data.frame(
  EnvZone = names(cld_output$Letters),
  Letter = cld_output$Letters,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Final Merged Table
# ---------------------------------------------------------
final_table <- richness_summary %>%
  left_join(cld_df, by = "EnvZone") %>%
  arrange(desc(Mean))

# Display final table with significance letters
kable(
  final_table,
  caption = "OTU Richness Summary by Production Site with Dunn Test Significance Letters (Bonferroni)"
)
```

```{r da4-u5, eval = FALSE}
# 4. Join letters back to the summary

  left_join(all_letters, by = c("Management", "Timepoint")) %>%
  arrange(Management, desc(Mean))

# 5. Display table
kable(
  final_table,
  caption = "OTU Richness Summary with Dunn Test Significance Letters (BH Adjusted)"
)

```



### Linear modelling
```{r da4-u6, eval = FALSE}
# Fit the Multiple Linear Regression Model
richness_lm <- lm(Richness ~ Management + Timepoint + TreatmentCode + Partner + TrialType + EnvZone + Pool, 
                  data =richness_df );richness_lm

# View the results
summary(richness_lm)

# Tidy the model (This converts the 'lm' class to a 'data.frame')
model_results_df <- tidy(richness_lm)

#Now you can use kable
kable(model_results_df, 
      digits = 3, 
      caption = "Linear Model Coefficients for OTU Richness")

# Check for multicollinearity (VIF)
library(car)
vif(richness_lm)



# In a forest plot for a linear model, the values on the x-axis represent the Coefficient Estimates (the effect size). These values tell you both the direction and the strength of the relationship between your independent variables and your dependent variable (Richness).Here is how to interpret them:1. Positive Values ($> 0$)If a variable’s dot is on the right side of the vertical zero-line, it has a positive correlation with your diversity.Meaning: As this variable increases (or if this category is present), your OTU Richness increases.Example: If "Management: Organic" has an estimate of $+12.5$, it means that, on average, Organic sites have 12.5 more OTUs than the reference site, holding all other variables constant.2. Negative Values ($< 0$)If a variable’s dot is on the left side of the vertical zero-line, it has a negative correlation.Meaning: As this variable increases (or if this category is present), your OTU Richness decreases.Example: If "Timepoint: T2" has an estimate of $-8.2$, it means diversity dropped by 8.2 OTUs at that timepoint compared to the baseline (T0).3. The Zero Line (Line of Null Effect)The vertical line at 0 is the most important part of the plot.If the error bars (whisker) cross the zero line: The effect is not statistically significant. Even if the dot is at $+5$, if the bar stretches to $-2$, we cannot say for sure that the effect isn't just random noise.If the entire bar is away from the zero line: The effect is statistically significant ($p < 0.05$).

#install.packages("sjPlot")
library(sjPlot)

# Create a forest plot of the coefficients
Forest_plot_coefficients_jacxard=plot_model(richness_lm, 
           show.values = TRUE, 
           value.offset = .3,
           title = "Effect of Variables on OTU Richness") +
  theme_bw();Forest_plot_coefficients_jacxard

# Save plot
ggsave("figures/Forest_plot_coefficients_jacxard.tiff",
       plot = Forest_plot_coefficients_jacxard, scale = 1,
       width =10, height = 14, units = "cm", dpi = 600)


library(broom)
library(ggplot2)
# Tidy the model
model_data <- tidy(richness_lm) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") # Usually remove intercept for better scaling

# Plot
tidy_model_jacxard=ggplot(model_data, aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = estimate - std.error, xmax = estimate + std.error), height = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Forest Plot of Model Coefficients",
       x = "Estimate (Effect Size)", y = "Variable");tidy_model_jacxard
# Save plot
ggsave("figures/tidy_model_jacxard.tiff",
       plot = tidy_model_jacxard, scale = 1,
       width =10, height = 14, units = "cm", dpi = 600)
```

### Rarefaction Analysis

```{r da5-rarefaction, eval = FALSE}
# Check minimum sequencing depth
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(ps2))
cat("Minimum sequencing depth:", min_depth, "\n")

# Rarefaction curve data
rarefaction_depth <- 3109  # Adjust based on your data

# Rarefy to even depth
ps_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(
  ps2,
  sample.size = rarefaction_depth,
  rngseed = 123,
  replace = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("After rarefaction:\n")
cat("Samples remaining:", nsamples(ps_rarefied), "\n")
cat("Taxa remaining:", ntaxa(ps_rarefied), "\n")
```

### Alpha Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Alpha Diversity Metrics

```{r da5-alpha-diversity, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate standard alpha diversity metrics
alpha_div <- estimate_richness(
  ps_rarefied,
  measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "ACE")
)

# Add sample metadata
alpha_div$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_div)
alpha_df <- merge(alpha_div, metadata, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "row.names")

# Compute effective species numbers (Hill numbers)
alpha_df$Shannon_Effective <- exp(alpha_df$Shannon)
alpha_df$Simpson_Effective <- 1 / (1 - alpha_df$Simpson)

# Calculate Pielou's Evenness
alpha_df$Evenness <- alpha_df$Shannon / log(alpha_df$Observed)

# Faith's PD (if tree is available)
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_rarefied, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  otu_mat <- as.data.frame(t(otu_table(ps_rarefied)))
  tree <- phy_tree(ps_rarefied)
  pd_result <- pd(otu_mat, tree, include.root = TRUE)
  alpha_df$PD <- pd_result$PD[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
  alpha_df$SR <- pd_result$SR[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
}

# Summary statistics
alpha_summary <- alpha_df %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(Observed, Chao1, Shannon, Simpson, InvSimpson),
           list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
  )

cat("Alpha Diversity Summary:\n")
print(t(alpha_summary))
```

#### Alpha Diversity Plots by Management Type with Partner and Treatment Separation

```{r da5-alpha-management-partner-treatment, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, eval = FALSE}
# Define color palette for treatments
treatment_colors <- brewer.pal(length(unique(alpha_df$TreatmentCode)), "Set2")
names(treatment_colors) <- unique(alpha_df$TreatmentCode)

# Define shape palette for partners
partner_shapes <- 1:length(unique(alpha_df$Partner))
names(partner_shapes) <- unique(alpha_df$Partner)

# Create plots for each management type
alpha_metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1")

# Create plots for each management type
for(management_type in unique(alpha_df$Management)) {
  cat("\nCreating plots for Management Type:", management_type, "\n")
  
  # Filter data for current management type
  filtered_data <- alpha_df[alpha_df$Management == management_type, ]
  
  # Create plots for each alpha diversity metric
  for(metric in alpha_metrics) {
    p <- ggplot(filtered_data, aes_string(x = "Partner", y = metric)) +
      geom_point(aes(color = TreatmentCode, shape = Partner), size = 3, position = position_jitter(width = 0.1)) +
      scale_color_manual(values = treatment_colors) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = partner_shapes) +
      facet_wrap(~Management, scales = "free_x") +
      labs(title = paste("Alpha Diversity by Partner and Treatment for", management_type, "Management"),
           subtitle = paste("Metric:", metric),
           x = "Partner", 
           y = metric,
           color = "Treatment",
           shape = "Partner") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
    
    print(p)
    
    # Save the plot
    ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_", tolower(management_type), "_", tolower(metric), ".tiff"),
           plot = p, width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

### Beta Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Distance Matrices

```{r da5-beta-distances, eval = FALSE}
# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity
bray_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "bray")

# Jaccard distance
jaccard_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)

# UniFrac distances (if tree available)
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_rarefied, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  unifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "unifrac")
  wunifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "wunifrac")
  cat("Phylogenetic distances calculated (UniFrac)\n")
} else {
  cat("No phylogenetic tree available - skipping UniFrac\n")
}
```
