#### PERMANOVA Analysis

```{r da5-permanova, eval = FALSE}
# PERMANOVA by TreatmentCode
permanova_treatment <- adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ TreatmentCode,
  data = metadata,
  permutations = 999,
  by = "margin"
)

cat("PERMANOVA: Effect of Treatment on Community Composition\n")
cat("========================================================\n")
print(permanova_treatment)

# PERMANOVA by EnvZone
permanova_envzone <- adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ EnvZone,
  data = metadata,
  permutations = 999,
  by = "margin"
)

cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Environmental Zone\n")
cat("========================================\n")
print(permanova_envzone)

# PERMANOVA by Management
permanova_management <- adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ Management,
  data = metadata,
  permutations = 999,
  by = "margin"
)

cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Management Type\n")
cat("=====================================\n")
print(permanova_management)

# Combined model
permanova_combined <- adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ Management + TreatmentCode + Partner + EnvZone + Timepoint + Pool,
  data = metadata,
  permutations = 999,
  by = "margin"
)

cat("\nPERMANOVA: Combined Model (All Factors)\n")
cat("=======================================\n")
print(permanova_combined)

# Summary table
permanova_summary <- data.frame(
  Factor = c("Management", "TreatmentCode", "Partner", "EnvZone", "Timepoint", "Pool"),
  R2 = c(permanova_management$R2[1],
         permanova_treatment$R2[1],
         NA,  # Will calculate below
         permanova_envzone$R2[1],
         NA,  # Will calculate below
         NA), # Will calculate below
  F_value = c(permanova_management$F[1],
              permanova_treatment$F[1],
              NA,
              permanova_envzone$F[1],
              NA,
              NA),
  p_value = c(permanova_management$`Pr(>F)`[1],
              permanova_treatment$`Pr(>F)`[1],
              NA,
              permanova_envzone$`Pr(>F)`[1],
              NA,
              NA)
)

# Add additional factors to the summary
additional_factors <- c("Partner", "Timepoint", "Pool")
for(factor in additional_factors) {
  if(factor %in% colnames(metadata)) {
    formula_str <- paste("bray_dist ~", factor)
    temp_permanova <- adonis2(
      as.formula(formula_str),
      data = metadata,
      permutations = 999,
      by = "margin"
    )
    
    new_row <- data.frame(
      Factor = factor,
      R2 = temp_permanova$R2[1],
      F_value = temp_permanova$F[1],
      p_value = temp_permanova$`Pr(>F)`[1]
    )
    
    permanova_summary <- rbind(permanova_summary, new_row)
  }
}

permanova_summary$Significance <- ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.001, "***",
                                        ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.01, "**",
                                              ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))

kable(permanova_summary,
      caption = "PERMANOVA Summary",
      digits = c(0, 4, 2, 4, 0)) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

### Rarefaction Analysis

```{r da6-rarefaction, eval = FALSE}
# Check minimum sequencing depth
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(ps2))
cat("Minimum sequencing depth:", min_depth, "\n")

# Rarefaction curve data
rarefaction_depth <- 3109  # Adjust based on your data

# Rarefy to even depth
ps_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(
  ps2,
  sample.size = rarefaction_depth,
  rngseed = 123,
  replace = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("After rarefaction:\n")
cat("Samples remaining:", nsamples(ps_rarefied), "\n")
cat("Taxa remaining:", ntaxa(ps_rarefied), "\n")
```

### Alpha Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Alpha Diversity Metrics

```{r da6-alpha-diversity, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate standard alpha diversity metrics
alpha_div <- estimate_richness(
  ps_rarefied,
  measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "ACE")
)

# Add sample metadata
alpha_div$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_div)
alpha_df <- merge(alpha_div, metadata_merged, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "row.names")

# Compute effective species numbers (Hill numbers)
alpha_df$Shannon_Effective <- exp(alpha_df$Shannon)
alpha_df$Simpson_Effective <- 1 / (1 - alpha_df$Simpson)

# Calculate Pielou's Evenness
alpha_df$Evenness <- alpha_df$Shannon / log(alpha_df$Observed)

# Faith's PD (if tree is available)
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_rarefied, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  otu_mat <- as.data.frame(t(otu_table(ps_rarefied)))
  tree <- phy_tree(ps_rarefied)
  pd_result <- pd(otu_mat, tree, include.root = TRUE)
  alpha_df$PD <- pd_result$PD[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
  alpha_df$SR <- pd_result$SR[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
}

# Summary statistics
alpha_summary <- alpha_df %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(Observed, Chao1, Shannon, Simpson, InvSimpson),
           list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
  )

cat("Alpha Diversity Summary:\n")
print(t(alpha_summary))
```


#### Statistical Tests for Alpha Diversity by All Variables

```{r da6-u1, eval = FALSE}
# Kruskal-Wallis tests by all specified variables
alpha_metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1", "InvSimpson", "ACE", "Evenness", "PD", "SR", "Shannon_Effective", "Simpson_Effective")

# Function to run Kruskal-Wallis tests for a variable
run_kruskal_tests <- function(data, var_name, metrics) {
  if(!var_name %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("Variable", var_name, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  results_list <- list()

  for(metric in metrics) {
    if(!metric %in% colnames(data)) next

    formula_str <- paste(metric, "~", var_name)
    test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(formula_str), data = data)

    result_df <- data.frame(
      Metric = metric,
      Chi_squared = round(test$statistic, 3),
      df = test$parameter,
      p_value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3),
      Significance = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                           ifelse(test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                                 ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
    )

    results_list[[metric]] <- result_df
  }

  return(do.call(rbind, results_list))
}

# Function to run Dunn's post-hoc tests for a variable
run_dunn_tests <- function(data, var_name, metrics) {
  if(!var_name %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("Variable", var_name, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  results_list <- list()

  for(metric in metrics) {
    if(!metric %in% colnames(data)) next

    # Perform Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction
    if(require(FSA, quietly = TRUE)) {
      formula_str <- as.formula(paste(metric, "~", var_name))
      
      tryCatch({
        dunn_test <- dunnTest(formula_str, data = data, method = "bonferroni")

        # Extract results
        dunn_results <- dunn_test$res
        if(!is.null(dunn_results)) {
          dunn_results$Metric <- metric
          
          # Parse Comparison column to get group1 and group2
          if("Comparison" %in% colnames(dunn_results)) {
            split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_results$Comparison), " - ")
            dunn_results$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, function(x) x[1])
            dunn_results$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, function(x) x[2])
          }
          
          # Add significance column
          dunn_results$signif <- ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.001, "***",
                               ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.01, "**",
                                     ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
          
          # Reorder columns to put Metric first
          cols_to_keep <- c("Metric", "group1", "group2", "Z", "P.unadj", "P.adj", "signif")
          cols_to_keep <- intersect(cols_to_keep, colnames(dunn_results))
          dunn_results <- dunn_results[, cols_to_keep]
          results_list[[metric]] <- dunn_results
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("Error in Dunn's test for", metric, ":", e$message, "\n")
      })
    } else {
      cat("FSA package not available for Dunn's test.\n")
      return(NULL)
    }
  }

  return(do.call(rbind, results_list))
}

# Function to calculate group letters from Dunn's test results
calculate_group_letters <- function(dunn_results, var_name, metric) {
  if(is.null(dunn_results) || nrow(dunn_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Filter results for the specific metric
  metric_results <- dunn_results[dunn_results$Metric == metric, ]

  if(nrow(metric_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Create comparison names for multcompLetters
  # It expects "Group1-Group2"
  comparisons <- paste(metric_results$group1, metric_results$group2, sep = "-")
  p_values <- metric_results$P.adj
  names(p_values) <- comparisons
  
  # Calculate letters using multcompView
  tryCatch({
    mcl <- multcompView::multcompLetters(p_values, threshold = 0.05)
    
    # Create result dataframe
    group_letters <- data.frame(
      group = names(mcl$Letters),
      letter = mcl$Letters,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    return(group_letters)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error calculating letters for", metric, ":", e$message, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  })
}
```

#### Alpha Diversity Plots with Significance Letters
```{r da6-alpha-plots-with-letters, fig.width=12, fig.height=15, eval = FALSE}

# Create plots for all specified variables if they exist in the dataset
attach(alpha_df)
plots_list <- list()

# Define publication quality theme for alpha plots
pub_theme <- theme(
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.box = "horizontal",
  axis.text.x = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
  text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
  panel.border = element_blank(),
  axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
)

# Define a function to add significance letters to plots
add_significance_letters <- function(data, var_name, metric, dunn_results) {
  if(is.null(dunn_results) || nrow(dunn_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Get group letters for the specific metric
  group_letters <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_results, var_name, metric)

  if(is.null(group_letters) || nrow(group_letters) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Create a mapping of group to letter
  group_to_letter <- setNames(group_letters$letter, as.character(group_letters$group))

  # Add letters to the data frame
  data_with_letters <- data
  data_with_letters$letter_labels <- ""
  for(grp in names(group_to_letter)) {
    data_with_labels_idx <- data_with_letters[[var_name]] == grp
    data_with_letters$letter_labels[data_with_labels_idx] <- group_to_letter[grp]
  }

  return(data_with_letters)
}

      }

    plots_list[[plot_name]] <- p

# Display all plots in a grid
if(length(plots_list) > 0) {
  # Create figures directory if it doesn't exist
  if (!dir.exists("figures")) {
    dir.create("figures")
  }

  # Calculate number of rows needed for the grid
  n_plots <- length(plots_list)
  n_cols <- 2  # Fixed number of columns
  n_rows <- ceiling(n_plots / n_cols)

  # Create the grid of plots
  combined_plot <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = plots_list, ncol = n_cols)
  print(combined_plot)

  # Save combined plot
  ggsave("figures/alpha_diversity_combined.tiff", combined_plot, width = 16, height = n_rows * 4, limitsize = FALSE, dpi = 300)

  # Save individual plots
  for(plot_name in names(plots_list)) {
    ggsave(paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_", plot_name, ".tiff"), plots_list[[plot_name]], width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
  }

  # Create and save combined plots for each metric (Index) where all variables are in one plot
  var_prefixes <- c("TreatmentCode", "EnvZone", "Management", "Timepoint", "Partner", "TrialType")
  
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    metric_plots <- list()
    for(var in var_prefixes) {
      plot_key <- paste0(var, "_", metric)
      if(plot_key %in% names(plots_list)) {
        metric_plots[[plot_key]] <- plots_list[[plot_key]]
      }
    }
    
    if(length(metric_plots) > 0) {
      # Calculate layout
      n_m_plots <- length(metric_plots)
      n_m_cols <- min(2, n_m_plots)
      n_m_rows <- ceiling(n_m_plots / n_m_cols)
      
      # Create grid
      metric_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = metric_plots, ncol = n_m_cols)
      
      # Print to report
      print(metric_combined)
      
      # Save
      ggsave(paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_all_variables_", metric, ".tiff"), 
             metric_combined, 
             width = 12, height = 4 * n_m_rows, 
             limitsize = FALSE, dpi = 300)
    }
  }

  # Create and save combined plot for Pool variable containing all indices
  pool_plots <- list()
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    plot_key <- paste0("Pool_", metric)
    if(plot_key %in% names(plots_list)) {
      pool_plots[[plot_key]] <- plots_list[[plot_key]]
    }
  }
  
  if(length(pool_plots) > 0) {
    # Calculate layout
    n_p_plots <- length(pool_plots)
    n_p_cols <- 3
    n_p_rows <- ceiling(n_p_plots / n_p_cols)
    
    # Create grid
    pool_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = pool_plots, ncol = n_p_cols)
    
    # Print to report
    print(pool_combined)
    
    # Save
    ggsave("figures/alpha_diversity_Pool_all_indices.tiff", 
           pool_combined, 
           width = 15, height = 6 * n_p_rows, 
           limitsize = FALSE, dpi = 300)
  }
}
detach(alpha_df)
```

#### Alpha Diversity Plots by facet_wrapping Partner with different TreatmentCodes

```{r da6-alpha-plots-facet-partner-treatment, fig.width=5, fig.height=8, eval = FALSE}
# Check if required columns exist
if(all(c("Partner.x", "TreatmentCode.x") %in% colnames(alpha_df))) {
  # Define alpha diversity metrics to plot
  alpha_metrics_to_plot <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1", "InvSimpson", "ACE", "Evenness", "PD", "SR", "Shannon_Effective", "Simpson_Effective"), colnames(alpha_df))

  # Initialize dataframe to store Kruskal-Wallis results
  kw_partner_results <- data.frame()

  # Loop through each metric
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    if(metric %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
      
      # Calculate significance letters for each Partner subset
      sig_letters_df <- data.frame()
      kw_ann_df <- data.frame()
      partners <- unique(as.character(alpha_df$Partner.x[!is.na(alpha_df$Partner.x)]))
      
      for(pt in partners) {
        subset_data <- alpha_df[alpha_df$Partner.x == pt, ]
        # Ensure factor and drop unused levels for this subset
        subset_data$TreatmentCode.x <- factor(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x)
        subset_data$TreatmentCode.x <- droplevels(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x)
        
        if(nlevels(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x) > 1) {
          # Calculate Kruskal-Wallis test for this facet
          tryCatch({
            kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ TreatmentCode.x")), data = subset_data)
            kw_row <- data.frame(
              Metric = metric,
              Partner = pt,
              Chi_squared = round(kw_test$statistic, 3),
              df = kw_test$parameter,
              p_value = kw_test$p.value,
              Significance = ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns"))),
              row.names = NULL
            )
            kw_partner_results <- rbind(kw_partner_results, kw_row)
            
            # Create annotation for plot
            p_label <- ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.3f", kw_test$p.value)))
            kw_ann_df <- rbind(kw_ann_df, data.frame(
              Partner.x = pt,
              label = paste0("KW: ", p_label),
              x = nlevels(subset_data$TreatmentCode.x) / 2 + 0.5,
              y = max(subset_data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25,
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE
            ))
          }, error = function(e) { })

          tryCatch({
            # Run Dunn's test using FSA package
            if(require(FSA, quietly = TRUE)) {
              dunn_res <- dunnTest(as.formula(paste(metric, "~ TreatmentCode.x")), 
                                   data = subset_data, 
                                   method = "bonferroni")$res
              
              if(!is.null(dunn_res)) {
                 # Format results to match what calculate_group_letters expects
                 dunn_res$Metric <- metric
                 split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_res$Comparison), " - ")
                 dunn_res$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 1)
                 dunn_res$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 2)
                 
                 # Reuse the existing function to get letters
                 letters_res <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_res, "TreatmentCode.x", metric)
                 
                 if(!is.null(letters_res)) {
                   letters_res$Partner.x <- pt
                   # Calculate y position for labels (slightly above max value of the subset)
                   letters_res$y_pos <- max(subset_data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
                   sig_letters_df <- rbind(sig_letters_df, letters_res)
                 }
              }
            }
          }, error = function(e) { })
        }
      }

      # Create the plot with facet wrap by Partner and TreatmentCode on x-axis
      p <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes_string(x = "TreatmentCode.x", y = metric, fill = "TreatmentCode.x")) +
        geom_boxplot() +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        facet_wrap(~Partner.x, scales = "free") +  # Facet by Partner with free scales to show only implemented treatments
        labs(y = metric, x = "Treatment Code", fill = "Treatment Code", title = paste("Alpha Diversity:", metric, "by Treatment Code across Partners")) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
          legend.position = "none",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgray"),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
        )
      
      # Add significance letters if available
      if(nrow(sig_letters_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = sig_letters_df, 
                           aes(x = group, y = y_pos, label = letter), 
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4)
      }
      
      # Add Kruskal-Wallis p-values
      if(nrow(kw_ann_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = kw_ann_df,
                           aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, vjust = 0)
      }

      print(p)

      # Save the plot
      ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_", metric, "_by_treatment_faceted_by_partner.tiff"),
             plot = p, width = 5, height = 8, dpi = 300, device = "tiff")
    }
  }
  
  # Export Kruskal-Wallis results to CSV
  if(nrow(kw_partner_results) > 0) {
    if (!dir.exists("results")) dir.create("results")
    write.csv(kw_partner_results, "results/kruskal_wallis_partner_treatment_facets.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("Kruskal-Wallis results for Partner facets saved to 'results/kruskal_wallis_partner_treatment_facets.csv'\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Required columns for Partner-TreatmentCode facet plots not found in alpha_df\n")
}
```

```{r da6-alpha-plots-facet-management-timepoint, fig.width=4, fig.height=5, eval = FALSE}
                                   data = subset_data, 
                                   method = "bonferroni")$res
              
              if(!is.null(dunn_res)) {
                 # Format results
                 dunn_res$Metric <- metric
                 split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_res$Comparison), " - ")
                 dunn_res$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 1)
                 dunn_res$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 2)
                 
                 letters_res <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_res, "Timepoint.x", metric)
                 
                 if(!is.null(letters_res)) {
                   letters_res$Management.x <- mgt
                   # Calculate y position
                   letters_res$y_pos <- max(subset_data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
                   sig_letters_df <- rbind(sig_letters_df, letters_res)
                 }
              }
            }
          }, error = function(e) { })
        }
      }

      # Create the plot with facet wrap by Management and Timepoint on x-axis
      p <- ggplot(alpha_df, aes_string(x = "Timepoint.x", y = metric, fill = "Timepoint.x")) +
        geom_boxplot() +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        facet_wrap(~Management.x, scales = "free") +  # Facet by Management with free scales
        labs(y = metric, x = "Timepoint", fill = "Timepoint", title = paste("Alpha Diversity:", metric, "by Timepoint across Management Types")) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
          legend.position = "none",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgray"),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
        )
      
      # Add significance letters if available
      if(nrow(sig_letters_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = sig_letters_df, 
                           aes(x = group, y = y_pos, label = letter), 
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4)
      }
      
      # Add Kruskal-Wallis p-values
      if(nrow(kw_ann_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = kw_ann_df,
                           aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, vjust = 0)
      }

      print(p)

      # Save the plot
      ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/alpha_diversity_", metric, "_by_timepoint_faceted_by_management.tiff"),
             plot = p, width = 5, height = 5, dpi = 300, device = "tiff")
    }
  }
  
  # Export Kruskal-Wallis results to CSV
  if(nrow(kw_management_results) > 0) {
    if (!dir.exists("results")) dir.create("results")
    write.csv(kw_management_results, "results/kruskal_wallis_management_timepoint_facets.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("Kruskal-Wallis results for Management facets saved to 'results/kruskal_wallis_management_timepoint_facets.csv'\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Required columns for Management-Timepoint facet plots not found in alpha_df\n")
}
```

### Temporal variations
```{r da6-temporal-variations, fig.width=6, fig.height=5, eval = FALSE}
# Subset data for TreatmentCode == "UTC"
if("TreatmentCode.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
  utc_data <- alpha_df[alpha_df$TreatmentCode.x == "UTC", ]
} else {
  # Fallback if column name is different
  utc_data <- alpha_df[alpha_df$TreatmentCode == "UTC", ]
}

# Determine correct column names for Management and Timepoint
mgt_col <- if("Management.x" %in% colnames(utc_data)) "Management.x" else "Management"
time_col <- if("Timepoint.x" %in% colnames(utc_data)) "Timepoint.x" else "Timepoint"

# Check if required columns exist
if(nrow(utc_data) > 0 && all(c(mgt_col, time_col) %in% colnames(utc_data))) {
  
  # Define alpha diversity metrics to plot
  alpha_metrics_to_plot <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1", "InvSimpson", "ACE", "Evenness", "PD", "SR", "Shannon_Effective", "Simpson_Effective"), colnames(utc_data))

  # Initialize dataframe to store Kruskal-Wallis results
  kw_temporal_results <- data.frame()

  # Loop through each metric
  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    if(metric %in% colnames(utc_data)) {
      
      # Calculate significance letters for each Management subset
      sig_letters_df <- data.frame()
      kw_ann_df <- data.frame()
      managements <- unique(as.character(utc_data[[mgt_col]][!is.na(utc_data[[mgt_col]])]))
      
      for(mgt in managements) {
        subset_data <- utc_data[utc_data[[mgt_col]] == mgt, ]
        # Ensure factor and drop unused levels
        subset_data[[time_col]] <- factor(subset_data[[time_col]])
        subset_data[[time_col]] <- droplevels(subset_data[[time_col]])
        
        if(nlevels(subset_data[[time_col]]) > 1) {
          # Calculate Kruskal-Wallis test for this facet
          tryCatch({
            kw_test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(paste(metric, "~", time_col)), data = subset_data)
            kw_row <- data.frame(
              Metric = metric,
              Management = mgt,
              Chi_squared = round(kw_test$statistic, 3),
              df = kw_test$parameter,
              p_value = kw_test$p.value,
              Significance = ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                             ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns"))),
              row.names = NULL
            )
            kw_temporal_results <- rbind(kw_temporal_results, kw_row)
            
            # Create annotation for plot
            p_label <- ifelse(kw_test$p.value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", sprintf("%.3f", kw_test$p.value)))
            ann_row <- data.frame(
              label = paste0("KW: ", p_label),
              x = nlevels(subset_data[[time_col]]) / 2 + 0.5,
              y = -Inf,
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE
            )
            ann_row[[mgt_col]] <- mgt
            kw_ann_df <- rbind(kw_ann_df, ann_row)
          }, error = function(e) { })

          tryCatch({
            # Run Dunn's test
            if(require(FSA, quietly = TRUE)) {
              dunn_res <- dunnTest(as.formula(paste(metric, "~", time_col)), 
                                   data = subset_data, 
                                   method = "bonferroni")$res
              
              if(!is.null(dunn_res)) {
                 # Format results
                 dunn_res$Metric <- metric
                 split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_res$Comparison), " - ")
                 dunn_res$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 1)
                 dunn_res$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, `[`, 2)
                 
                 letters_res <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_res, time_col, metric)
                 
                 if(!is.null(letters_res)) {
                   letters_res[[mgt_col]] <- mgt
                   # Calculate y position
                   letters_res$y_pos <- max(subset_data[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
                   sig_letters_df <- rbind(sig_letters_df, letters_res)
                 }
              }
            }
          }, error = function(e) { })
        }
      }

      # Create the plot with facet wrap by Management and Timepoint on x-axis
      p <- ggplot(utc_data, aes_string(x = time_col, y = metric, fill = time_col)) +
        geom_boxplot() +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", mgt_col)), scales = "free") +  # Facet by Management with free scales
        labs(y = metric, x = "Timepoint", fill = "Timepoint", title = paste("Temporal Variation (UTC):", metric, "by Management")) +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(
          legend.position = "none",
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "lightgray"),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          text = element_text(family = "Verdana"),
          panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
        )
      
      # Add significance letters if available
      if(nrow(sig_letters_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = sig_letters_df, 
                           aes(x = group, y = y_pos, label = letter), 
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4)
      }
      
      # Add Kruskal-Wallis p-values
      if(nrow(kw_ann_df) > 0) {
        p <- p + geom_text(data = kw_ann_df,
                           aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, vjust = -0.5)
      }

      print(p)

      # Save the plot
      ggsave(filename = paste0("figures/temporal_variation_utc_", metric, ".tiff"),
             plot = p, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300, device = "tiff")
    }
  }
  
  # Export Kruskal-Wallis results to CSV
  if(nrow(kw_temporal_results) > 0) {
    if (!dir.exists("results")) dir.create("results")
    write.csv(kw_temporal_results, "results/kruskal_wallis_temporal_utc_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    cat("Kruskal-Wallis results for Temporal variations (UTC) saved to 'results/kruskal_wallis_temporal_utc_results.csv'\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Required columns for Temporal variations analysis not found in alpha_df\n")
}
```


### Regression between TreatmentCode and TimePoint for the different Managenent tpypes.

```{r da6-u2, eval = FALSE}
if(all(c("Management.x", "Timepoint.x", "TreatmentCode.x") %in% colnames(alpha_df))) {

  # Create a copy of the data for regression and convert Timepoint to numeric
  regression_data <- alpha_df
  regression_data$Timepoint_num <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", regression_data$Timepoint.x))

  # Define alpha diversity metrics to model
  alpha_metrics_to_model <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1"), colnames(regression_data))

  # Get unique management types
  managements <- unique(as.character(regression_data$Management.x[!is.na(regression_data$Management.x)]))

  # Loop through each management type
  for(mgt in managements) {
    
    cat(paste("\n\n### Regression Analysis for Management Type:", mgt, "\n\n"))
    
    # Subset data for the current management type
    subset_data <- regression_data[regression_data$Management.x == mgt, ]

    # Loop through each alpha diversity metric
    for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_model) {
      
      cat(paste("\n#### Metric:", metric, "\n"))
      
      # Define the model formula with interaction
      formula_str <- paste(metric, "~ Timepoint_num * TreatmentCode.x")
      
      tryCatch({
        # Fit the linear model
        interaction_model <- lm(as.formula(formula_str), data = subset_data)
        
        # Print model summary
        cat("\n**Model Summary:**\n")
        print(summary(interaction_model))
        
        # Print ANOVA table to see significance of interaction
        cat("\n**ANOVA Table:**\n")
        print(kable(anova(interaction_model), caption = paste("ANOVA for", metric, "in", mgt, "Management")))
        
        # Visualize the interaction effect
        if(require(sjPlot, quietly = TRUE)) {
          cat("\n**Interaction Plot:**\n")
          
          interaction_plot <- plot_model(interaction_model, type = "int") +
            labs(
              title = paste("Interaction of Timepoint and Treatment on", metric),
              subtitle = paste("Management Type:", mgt),
              x = "Timepoint",
              y = metric
            ) +
            theme_bw() +
            theme(text = element_text(family = "Verdana"))
          
          print(interaction_plot)
          
          # Save the plot
          if (!dir.exists("figures")) dir.create("figures")
          ggsave(
            filename = paste0("figures/regression_interaction_", mgt, "_", metric, ".tiff"),
            plot = interaction_plot,
            width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300
          )
        }
        
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("Could not fit model for", metric, "in", mgt, "management:", e$message, "\n")
      })
    }
  }
} else {
  cat("Required columns for regression analysis not found in alpha_df.\n")
}
```

### Rarefaction Analysis

```{r da7-rarefaction, eval = FALSE}
# Check minimum sequencing depth
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(ps2))
cat("Minimum sequencing depth:", min_depth, "\n")

# Rarefaction curve data
rarefaction_depth <- 2500  # Adjust based on your data

# Rarefy to even depth
ps_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(
  ps2,
  sample.size = rarefaction_depth,
  rngseed = 123,
  replace = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("After rarefaction:\n")
cat("Samples remaining:", nsamples(ps_rarefied), "\n")
cat("Taxa remaining:", ntaxa(ps_rarefied), "\n")
```

### Alpha Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Alpha Diversity Metrics

```{r da7-alpha-diversity, eval = FALSE}
# Calculate standard alpha diversity metrics
alpha_div <- estimate_richness(
  ps_rarefied,
  measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "ACE")
)

# Add sample metadata
alpha_div$SampleID <- rownames(alpha_div)
alpha_df <- merge(alpha_div, metadata, by.x = "SampleID", by.y = "row.names")

# Calculate effective number of species (Hill numbers)
alpha_df$Shannon_Effective <- exp(alpha_df$Shannon)
alpha_df$Simpson_Effective <- 1 / (1 - alpha_df$Simpson)

# Calculate Pielou's Evenness
alpha_df$Evenness <- alpha_df$Shannon / log(alpha_df$Observed)

# Faith's PD (if tree is available)
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_rarefied, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  otu_mat <- as.data.frame(t(otu_table(ps_rarefied)))
  tree <- phy_tree(ps_rarefied)
  pd_result <- pd(otu_mat, tree, include.root = TRUE)
  alpha_df$PD <- pd_result$PD[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
  alpha_df$SR <- pd_result$SR[match(alpha_df$SampleID, rownames(pd_result))]
}

# Summary statistics
alpha_summary <- alpha_df %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(Observed, Chao1, Shannon, Simpson, InvSimpson),
           list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
  )

cat("Alpha Diversity Summary:\n")
print(t(alpha_summary))
```

#### Statistical Tests for Alpha Diversity

```{r da7-alpha-stats, eval = FALSE}
# Kruskal-Wallis tests by TreatmentCode
alpha_metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1", "InvSimpson")

kw_treatment_results <- lapply(alpha_metrics, function(metric) {
  test <- kruskal.test(reformulate("TreatmentCode", metric), data = alpha_df)
  data.frame(
    Metric = metric,
    Chi_squared = round(test$statistic, 3),
    df = test$parameter,
    p_value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3),
    Significance = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                         ifelse(test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                               ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
  )
})

kw_treatment_df <- do.call(rbind, kw_treatment_results)

kable(kw_treatment_df,
      caption = "Kruskal-Wallis Test: Alpha Diversity by Treatment",
      row.names = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# Kruskal-Wallis tests by EnvZone
kw_envzone_results <- lapply(alpha_metrics, function(metric) {
  test <- kruskal.test(reformulate("EnvZone", metric), data = alpha_df)
  data.frame(
    Metric = metric,
    Chi_squared = round(test$statistic, 3),
    df = test$parameter,
    p_value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3),
    Significance = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                         ifelse(test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                               ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
  )
})

kw_envzone_df <- do.call(rbind, kw_envzone_results)

kable(kw_envzone_df,
      caption = "Kruskal-Wallis Test: Alpha Diversity by Environmental Zone",
      row.names = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

#### Pairwise Comparisons (Dunn's Test)

```{r da7-dunn-test, eval = FALSE}
library(FSA)

# Dunn's test for Shannon by TreatmentCode
if (length(unique(alpha_df$TreatmentCode)) > 2) {
  dunn_shannon_treatment <- dunnTest(Shannon ~ TreatmentCode,
                                      data = alpha_df,
                                      method = "bonferroni")

  cat("Dunn's Test: Shannon by Treatment\n")
  print(dunn_shannon_treatment)
}

# Dunn's test for Shannon by EnvZone
if (length(unique(alpha_df$EnvZone)) > 2) {
  dunn_shannon_envzone <- dunnTest(Shannon ~ EnvZone,
                                    data = alpha_df,
                                    method = "bonferroni")

  cat("\nDunn's Test: Shannon by Environmental Zone\n")
  print(dunn_shannon_envzone)
}
```

### Beta Diversity Analysis

#### Calculate Distance Matrices

```{r da7-beta-distances, eval = FALSE}
# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity
bray_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "bray")

# Jaccard distance
jaccard_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)

# UniFrac distances (if tree available)
if (!is.null(phy_tree(ps_rarefied, errorIfNULL = FALSE))) {
  unifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "unifrac")
  wunifrac_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rarefied, method = "wunifrac")
  cat("Phylogenetic distances calculated (UniFrac)\n")
} else {
  cat("No phylogenetic tree available - skipping UniFrac\n")
}
```

#### PCoA Ordination

```{r da7-pcoa-ordination, fig.width=12, fig.height=10, eval = FALSE}
# PCoA with Bray-Curtis
pcoa_bray <- ordinate(ps_rarefied, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")

# Variance explained
var_explained <- pcoa_bray$values$Relative_eig * 100

# PCoA plot by TreatmentCode
pcoa_treatment <- plot_ordination(ps_rarefied, pcoa_bray,
                                   color = "TreatmentCode") +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "PCoA (Bray-Curtis) by Treatment",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_explained[1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_explained[2], 1), "%)")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# PCoA plot by EnvZone
pcoa_envzone <- plot_ordination(ps_rarefied, pcoa_bray,
                                 color = "EnvZone") +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = "PCoA (Bray-Curtis) by Environmental Zone",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", round(var_explained[1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(var_explained[2], 1), "%)")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Combined plot
beta_pcoa_plot <- pcoa_treatment / pcoa_envzone

print(beta_pcoa_plot)

ggsave("figures/beta_diversity_pcoa.tiff",
       beta_pcoa_plot, width = 10, height = 12, dpi = 300)
```

#### NMDS Ordination

```{r da7-nmds-ordination, fig.width=12, fig.height=6, eval = FALSE}
# NMDS with Bray-Curtis
nmds_bray <- ordinate(ps_rarefied, method = "NMDS", distance = "bray",
                       trymax = 100, k = 2)

cat("NMDS Stress:", nmds_bray$stress, "\n")
cat("Stress interpretation: ",
    ifelse(nmds_bray$stress < 0.05, "Excellent",
          ifelse(nmds_bray$stress < 0.1, "Good",
                ifelse(nmds_bray$stress < 0.2, "Fair", "Poor"))), "\n")

# NMDS plots
nmds_treatment <- plot_ordination(ps_rarefied, nmds_bray,
                                   color = "TreatmentCode") +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = paste0("NMDS (Bray-Curtis) - Stress: ", round(nmds_bray$stress, 3))) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

nmds_envzone <- plot_ordination(ps_rarefied, nmds_bray,
                                 color = "EnvZone") +
  geom_point(size = 4, alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = paste0("NMDS (Bray-Curtis) - Stress: ", round(nmds_bray$stress, 3))) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

nmds_plot <- nmds_treatment | nmds_envzone
print(nmds_plot)

ggsave("figures/beta_diversity_nmds.tiff",
       nmds_plot, width = 14, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

#### PERMANOVA Analysis

```{r da7-permanova, eval = FALSE}
# Source utility functions
source("utils.R")

# Get metadata for rarefied samples
meta_rarefied <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_rarefied))

# PERMANOVA by TreatmentCode using utility function
permanova_treatment <- run_permanova(
  bray_dist,
  meta_rarefied,
  "TreatmentCode"
)

cat("PERMANOVA: Effect of Treatment on Community Composition\n")
cat("========================================================\n")
print(permanova_treatment)

# PERMANOVA by EnvZone using utility function
permanova_envzone <- run_permanova(
  bray_dist,
  meta_rarefied,
  "EnvZone"
)

cat("\nPERMANOVA: Effect of Environmental Zone\n")
cat("========================================\n")
print(permanova_envzone)

# Combined model - note: this specific interaction model isn't in the utility function
# so we'll keep it as is for this specific case
permanova_combined <- adonis2(
  bray_dist ~ TreatmentCode + EnvZone + TreatmentCode:EnvZone,
  data = meta_rarefied,
  permutations = 999,
  by = "margin"
)

cat("\nPERMANOVA: Combined Model (Treatment + EnvZone + Interaction)\n")
cat("==============================================================\n")
print(permanova_combined)

# Summary table
permanova_summary <- data.frame(
  Factor = c("TreatmentCode", "EnvZone", "Treatment x EnvZone"),
  R2 = c(permanova_treatment$R2[1],
         permanova_envzone$R2[1],
         permanova_combined$R2[3]),
  F_value = c(permanova_treatment$F[1],
              permanova_envzone$F[1],
              permanova_combined$F[3]),
  p_value = c(permanova_treatment$`Pr(>F)`[1],
              permanova_envzone$`Pr(>F)`[1],
              permanova_combined$`Pr(>F)`[3])
)

permanova_summary$Significance <- ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.001, "***",
                                         ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.01, "**",
                                               ifelse(permanova_summary$p_value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))

kable(permanova_summary,
      caption = "PERMANOVA Summary",
      digits = c(0, 4, 2, 4, 0)) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

#### Beta Dispersion Test (PERMDISP)

```{r da7-betadisper, eval = FALSE}
# Test homogeneity of dispersions - TreatmentCode
betadisper_treatment <- betadisper(bray_dist, meta_rarefied$TreatmentCode)
permdisp_treatment <- permutest(betadisper_treatment, permutations = 999)

cat("Beta Dispersion Test: TreatmentCode\n")
cat("====================================\n")
print(permdisp_treatment)

# Test homogeneity of dispersions - EnvZone
betadisper_envzone <- betadisper(bray_dist, meta_rarefied$EnvZone)
permdisp_envzone <- permutest(betadisper_envzone, permutations = 999)

cat("\nBeta Dispersion Test: EnvZone\n")
cat("==============================\n")
print(permdisp_envzone)

# Dispersion interpretation
cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
cat("If PERMDISP p > 0.05: Dispersions are homogeneous (PERMANOVA is valid)\n")
cat("If PERMDISP p < 0.05: Dispersions are heterogeneous (interpret PERMANOVA with caution)\n")
```

#### Beta Dispersion Visualization

```{r da7-betadisper-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=5, eval = FALSE}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Plot dispersion for TreatmentCode
plot(betadisper_treatment,
     main = "Beta Dispersion: Treatment",
     hull = FALSE, ellipse = TRUE)

# Plot dispersion for EnvZone
plot(betadisper_envzone,
     main = "Beta Dispersion: Environmental Zone",
     hull = FALSE, ellipse = TRUE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

#### Pairwise PERMANOVA

```{r da7-pairwise-permanova, eval = FALSE}
# Pairwise PERMANOVA for TreatmentCode
library(pairwiseAdonis)

if (length(unique(meta_rarefied$TreatmentCode)) > 2) {
  pairwise_treatment <- pairwise.adonis(
    bray_dist,
    meta_rarefied$TreatmentCode,
    p.adjust.m = "bonferroni",
    perm = 999
  )

  kable(pairwise_treatment,
        caption = "Pairwise PERMANOVA: Treatment Comparisons",
        digits = c(0, 0, 4, 2, 4, 4)) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
}

# Pairwise PERMANOVA for EnvZone
if (length(unique(meta_rarefied$EnvZone)) > 2) {
  pairwise_envzone <- pairwise.adonis(
    bray_dist,
    meta_rarefied$EnvZone,
    p.adjust.m = "bonferroni",
    perm = 999
  )

  kable(pairwise_envzone,
        caption = "Pairwise PERMANOVA: Environmental Zone Comparisons",
        digits = c(0, 0, 4, 2, 4, 4)) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
}
```

## Source: `joined-scripts/reports/Jorn_class_2_2025.qmd`


Original front matter:

``` yaml
title: "Aidea Tutorial for Students - Class of 2025"
author: "Expedito Olimi, PhD"
format: html
```


### Introduction to `aidea`

Welcome to this tutorial on `aidea`, an R package that combines the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) with your R environment to help you explore datasets. This tool can help you generate code, understand data, and perform statistical analyses.

In this tutorial, you will learn how to:
1.  Install and set up the `aidea` package.
2.  Use `aidea` to explore the `palmerpenguins` dataset.
3.  Perform various data analysis tasks, from summary statistics to statistical tests.
4.  Apply your skills to a more complex dataset, `nycflights13`.

**DISCLAIMER:** This package is a proof of concept. It's a fun tool for learning and exploration, but not for production use.

### Part 1: Setup

#### 1.1 Installation

First, you need to install the `aidea` package from GitHub. You will also need the `remotes` package to do this.

```{r rp1-u1, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
#remotes::install_github("cpsievert/aidea")
```

Now, let's load the library.
```{r rp1-u2, eval = FALSE}
library(aidea)
```

#### 1.2 Prerequisites: API Key

`aidea` uses an LLM to power its chat assistant. By default, it uses OpenAI's models. You will need an OpenAI API key.

1.  Get your key from [platform.openai.com/account/api-keys](https://platform.openai.com/account/api-keys).
2.  It is recommended to set this key as an environment variable. A good way to do this is by using `usethis::edit_r_environ()`. This will open your `.Renviron` file, where you can add the following line:

```
OPENAI_API_KEY='your-key-goes-here'
```
*Replace `your-key-goes-here` with your actual API key.*

1.3.  Restart your R session for the changes to take effect.

You can also use a `.env` file.
```{r rp1-u3, eval = FALSE}
# You might need to install the dotenv package
# install.packages("dotenv")
library(dotenv)
# Make sure you have a .env file with OPENAI_API_KEY="your-key"
# load_dot_env() 
```

Once your key is set up, you can create a `chat` object that `aidea` will use.

```{r rp1-u4, eval = FALSE}
# Make sure you're using a valid model
chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(
  model = "gpt-4o-mini",  # or "gpt-3.5-turbo"
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
)
```

If you are worried about privacy, consider using a local model (i.e., `assist(chat = ellmer::chat_ollama())`) instead of OpenAI. 

### Part 2: Exploring the `penguins` dataset

The `palmerpenguins` dataset is a popular dataset for data exploration and visualization in R. It contains data on 344 penguins from 3 different species.

#### 2.1 Load the data and start `aidea`

Let's load the `penguins` dataset and start the `aidea` assistant.

```{r rp1-u5, eval = FALSE}
# Load the dataset
library(palmerpenguins)
data(penguins)

# Start the aidea app assistant
aidea::assist(penguins)
```

When you run `assist(penguins)`, a new window will open with a chat interface. The assistant will greet you with an overview of the dataset.

#### 2.2 Asking questions

Now you can ask questions about the data. Let's go through some examples.

##### What is the average body mass for each species?

You can type this question directly into the chat. The assistant will provide you with R code to answer it.

```{r rp1-u6, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)

penguins %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_body_mass_g = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
The output will be a table showing the average body mass for each penguin species.

##### How do bill length and depth vary by island?

Let's ask another question. The assistant can provide both summary statistics and visualizations.

Here is the code to get summary statistics:
```{r rp1-u7, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)

penguins %>%
  group_by(island) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_bill_length_mm = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_bill_depth_mm = mean(bill_depth_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_bill_length_mm = sd(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_bill_depth_mm = sd(bill_depth_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

And here is the code for visualization with boxplots:
```{r rp1-u8, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

# Bill Length by Island
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = island, y = bill_length_mm)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Bill Length by Island", y = "Bill Length (mm)", x = "Island")

# Bill Depth by Island
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = island, y = bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Bill Depth by Island", y = "Bill Depth (mm)", x = "Island")
```

##### Are there differences in flipper length between male and female penguins?

Let's investigate the relationship between sex and flipper length.

Summary statistics:
```{r rp1-u9, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)

penguins %>%
  group_by(sex) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_flipper_length_mm = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_flipper_length_mm = sd(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    count = n()
  )
```

And a boxplot for visualization:
```{r rp1-u10, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = sex, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Flipper Length by Sex",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Flipper Length (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### 2.3 Deeper Analysis

`aidea` can also help with more advanced analysis.

##### Checking for outliers

Are there any outliers in the measurements?

```{r rp1-u11, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# Gather numeric columns for faceted boxplots
penguins_long <- penguins %>%
  select(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "measurement", values_to = "value")

ggplot(penguins_long, aes(x = measurement, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplots of Penguin Measurements",
    x = "Measurement",
    y = "Value"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

##### Correlations

What is the correlation between the different numeric measurements?

You can get a correlation matrix:
```{r rp1-u12, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)

penguins_numeric <- penguins %>%
  select(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) %>%
  na.omit()

cor(penguins_numeric)
```

Or a nice heatmap:
```{r rp1-u13, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

cor_matrix <- cor(penguins_numeric)
cor_long <- melt(cor_matrix)

ggplot(cor_long, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), color = "white", size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", 
                       midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1,1), space = "Lab",
                       name="Correlation") +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Heatmap of Penguin Measurements",
    x = "",
    y = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

##### Statistical Tests

`aidea` can also guide you on which statistical tests to use and how to run them.

###### Normality Test (Shapiro-Wilk)

Is the `body_mass_g` data normally distributed?

```{r rp1-u14, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)

penguins_clean <- penguins %>%
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g))

shapiro.test(penguins_clean$body_mass_g)
```
A small p-value suggests the data is not normally distributed.

Let's check for normality within each species:
```{r rp1-u15, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
penguins %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g)) %>%
  summarise(
    shapiro_p = shapiro.test(body_mass_g)$p.value,
    n = n()
  )
```

###### Kruskal-Wallis Test

Since the data may not be normal, we can use a non-parametric test like Kruskal-Wallis to compare body mass across species.

```{r rp1-u16, eval = FALSE}
library(dplyr)

penguins_clean <- penguins %>%
  filter(!is.na(body_mass_g), !is.na(species))

kruskal.test(body_mass_g ~ species, data = penguins_clean)
```
A small p-value indicates that there is a significant difference in body mass among the different penguin species.

### Part 3: Your Turn! Exploring the `flights` dataset

Now it's your turn to practice. We will use the `nycflights13` dataset, which contains information about all flights that departed from NYC in 2013.

#### 3.1 Load the data and start `aidea`

```{r rp1-u17, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("nycflights13") # if you don't have it
library(nycflights13)
data(flights)

aidea::assist(flights)
```


```{r rp1-u18, eval = FALSE}
data(penguins)
#|label: plot-penguins
str(penguins)
variable.names(penguins)
# Load required libraries
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)

# Create scatter plot showing relationship between flipper and bill lengths
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = flipper_length_mm)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = species, shape = species), size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "gray30", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Adelie" = "#ff6f00", 
                                 "Chinstrap" = "#c75dcb", 
                                 "Gentoo" = "#007c91")) +
  labs(title = "Relationship Between Bill Length and Flipper Length",
       subtitle = "Palmer Penguins Dataset",
       x = "Bill Length (mm)",
       y = "Flipper Length (mm)",
       color = "Species",
       shape = "Species") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray40"),
        legend.position = "bottom")

# Print correlation coefficient
cor_value <- cor(penguins$bill_length_mm, penguins$flipper_length_mm, 
                 use = "complete.obs")
cat("Correlation coefficient:", round(cor_value, 3))

```


#### 3.2 Exercises

Use the `aidea` assistant to answer the following questions. Try to generate both code and visualizations.

1.  What are the most common destinations or carriers in the dataset?
2.  How do delays vary by month, day of the week, or time of day?
3.  Which routes or airlines have the longest average delays? (Hint: a route is a combination of `origin` and `dest`).
4.  Are there patterns in flight cancellations? (Hint: cancelled flights have missing `dep_time`).
5.  How does `air_time` relate to `distance` for different flights?

### Conclusion

In this tutorial, you've learned how to use `aidea` to explore and analyze datasets in R. You've seen how it can help you with everything from basic data summaries to more complex statistical tests. Now you have a new tool in your data science toolbox!

### Color Palettes Inspired by Neotropical Poison Frogs
A collection of color palettes inspired by Neotropical poison frogs. With more than 200 brighly colored species, Neotropical poison frogs paint the rain forest in vivid hues that shout a clear message: “I’m toxic!”. Spice up your plots with poisonfrogs and give your dataviz a toxic twist! But wait, we also included some color palettes inspired by other pretty frog species, because… why not? 🐸

Get inspired with the collection of species behind the color palettes.



### Installation
You can install poisonfrogs from CRAN:

```{r rp2-u1, eval = FALSE}
#install.packages("poisonfrogs")
```

### Examples
Using poisonfrogs in base R plots

```{r rp2-u6, eval = FALSE}
library(poisonfrogs)
library(ggplot2)

prevalence <- ggplot(
  prevasv,
  aes(TotalAbundance, Prevalence, color = Prevalence)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = prevalenceThreshold,
             alpha = 0.5,
             linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_color_gradientn(
    colours = poison_palette(
      "Ramazonica",
      return = "vector",
      type = "continuous",
      direction = 1
    )
  ) +
  ggtitle(
    paste0("Prevalence filtering, using a threshold of ",
           prevalenceThreshold)
  ) +
  xlab("Total Abundance") +
  ylab("Prevalence") +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~ Phyla, nrow = 4)

# Save
tiff("prevalence.tiff", units = "in", width = 10, height = 6, res = 300)
print(prevalence)
dev.off()
```

### In R, you can also view and work with QIIME 2 representative sequences (rep-seqs.qza) in a couple of ways. The approach depends on whether you want to read the .qza directly or use the exported FASTA.

Option 1 — Export rep-seqs to FASTA, then read in R

Export from QIIME 2 (same as in Python):

```{r rp2-u9, eval = FALSE}
qiime tools export \
  --input-path rep-seqs.qza \
  --output-path repseq_export
```


This produces repseq_export/dna-sequences.fasta.

Read FASTA in R with Biostrings:

```{r rp2-u10, eval = FALSE}

# install if needed
if (!requireNamespace("Biostrings", quietly = TRUE)) {
    BiocManager::install("Biostrings")
}

library(Biostrings)

fasta_file <- "repseq_export/dna-sequences.fasta"
seqs <- readDNAStringSet(fasta_file)
# View first few sequences
seqs[1:5]

# Access sequence names
names(seqs)

# Access actual sequence as string
as.character(seqs[1])
```


You can now manipulate, filter, or analyze sequences in R just like any DNA object.

Option 2 — Use the .qza directly in R

QIIME 2 artifacts are .zip files internally. You can read them in R by unpacking and loading the data:

```{r rp2-u11, eval = FALSE}

# unzip the artifact
unzip("rep-seqs.qza", exdir = "repseq_qza_unpacked")

# The sequences are stored in `data/dna-sequences.fasta`
fasta_file <- "repseq_qza_unpacked/data/dna-sequences.fasta"

# Use Biostrings to read
library(Biostrings)
seqs <- readDNAStringSet(fasta_file)

```

This is essentially what QIIME 2 does under the hood.

Option 3 — Convert to phyloseq for downstream analysis

If you’re using phyloseq, you often want ASV sequences + ASV table + taxonomy:

```{r rp2-u12, eval = FALSE}

library(phyloseq)
library(Biostrings)

repseqs <- readDNAStringSet("repseq_export/dna-sequences.fasta")
# Assume you have asv_tab and taxonomy tables loaded
ps <- phyloseq(otu_table(asv_tab, taxa_are_rows=TRUE),
               tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy)),
               refseq(repseqs))
ps

```

This gives you a fully integrated phyloseq object with your sequences linked to ASVs and metadata.


## Source: `joined-scripts/reports/manuscript.qmd`


claude academy: https://www.anthropic.com/learn/build-with-claude



Welcome! You’re working with the psm dataset, which looks like a rich and detailed dataset with 207,500 rows and 24 columns. Here are some key points to help you get started:

Key Features of the psm Dataset
Size & Structure:

207,500 rows (observations)
24 columns (variables)
Most columns are character type (17), with 7 numeric columns.
Diversity:

Many columns represent categorical information (like Phyla, Genus, Species, etc.), with a wide range of unique values (e.g., 119 unique species, 81 genera).
Numeric columns include variables like Abundance, Season, dpt, Rain, SOM, TEX, and total_reads.
Data Quality:

No missing values in any column, which is great for analysis.
Distribution Highlights:

Abundance is mostly zero or low values, but with some higher outliers.
total_reads has a wide range, with a median around 17,080 and a maximum close to 50,000.
Rain and dpt (possibly days post-treatment?) also show a broad spread.
Example Questions to Get You Started
Here are some questions you might consider exploring:

What are the most common genera or species in the dataset?
How does Abundance vary by Season, TreatmentCode, or Management?
Are there relationships between environmental variables (like Rain, SOM, TEX) and microbial abundance?
How is total_reads distributed across samples or categories?
What are the top 5 most abundant OTUs?
If you’d like to dive into a specific aspect, just let me know! If you can provide a bit more context about the study or your goals, I can tailor the analysis and code examples to your needs.

What would you like to explore first?

summarize every variable in relation to the taxonomy abundance; draw correlation between the different taxa, and abundance, related ti the different variables; genralized model for each taxa in relation to the different variables; make statistical comparisions; make correlaion plots; if possible xgboost classification of the diffeent variables and taxa.

Great! You’ve outlined a comprehensive and ambitious analysis plan for the psm dataset. Since you’re interested in exploring relationships between taxonomy (e.g., Phyla, Genus, Species) and abundance, as well as modeling and classification, I’ll break down your request into manageable steps, with R code for each. This will help you proceed step by step and interpret results as you go.

Note: Each code block includes necessary library imports. Please run each block separately and return with results or questions for deeper exploration.

1. Summarize Every Variable in Relation to Taxonomy Abundance
Let’s start by summarizing Abundance for each taxonomic level (Phyla, Genus, Species):


library(dplyr)

### Summarize abundance by Phyla, Genus, and Species
psm %>%
  group_by(Phyla) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance), 
            median_abundance = median(Abundance), 
            n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abundance))

psm %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance), 
            median_abundance = median(Abundance), 
            n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abundance))

psm %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance), 
            median_abundance = median(Abundance), 
            n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abundance))
2. Correlation Between Taxa Abundance and Other Variables
Let’s look at correlations between numeric variables and abundance, and visualize them:


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)

### Select numeric columns for correlation
numeric_vars <- psm %>%
  select(Abundance, Season, dpt, Rain, SOM, TEX, total_reads)

### Correlation matrix plot
ggpairs(numeric_vars)
3. Generalized Model for Each Taxa in Relation to Different Variables
Let’s fit a simple linear model for each Genus, predicting Abundance from environmental variables:


library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(purrr)

### Example: Linear model for each Genus
models <- psm %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~lm(Abundance ~ Season + dpt + Rain + SOM + TEX + total_reads, data = .x)),
    tidied = map(model, tidy)
  ) %>%
  unnest(tidied)

### View model summaries for each Genus
models
4. Statistical Comparisons
For example, compare Abundance between two Management types:


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

### Boxplot and t-test for Abundance by Management
ggplot(psm, aes(x = Management, y = Abundance)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()

### t-test
t.test(Abundance ~ Management, data = psm)
5. Correlation Plots
Let’s make a correlation heatmap for numeric variables:


library(corrplot)

### Compute correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_vars, use = "complete.obs")

### Plot
corrplot::corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "color", addCoef.col = "black")
6. XGBoost Classification (Example: Predicting Phyla)
Let’s try a simple XGBoost model to classify Phyla based on numeric variables. This is a more advanced step and may require some data preparation.


library(xgboost)
library(dplyr)
library(caret)

### Prepare data: encode Phyla as factor, select numeric predictors
psm_xgb <- psm %>%
  mutate(Phyla = as.factor(Phyla)) %>%
  select(Phyla, Season, dpt, Rain, SOM, TEX, total_reads)

### Split into train/test
set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(psm_xgb$Phyla, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train <- psm_xgb[train_idx, ]
test <- psm_xgb[-train_idx, ]

### Prepare matrices for xgboost
train_matrix <- as.matrix(train %>% select(-Phyla))
test_matrix <- as.matrix(test %>% select(-Phyla))
train_label <- as.numeric(train$Phyla) - 1
test_label <- as.numeric(test$Phyla) - 1

### Train xgboost model
xgb_model <- xgboost(
  data = train_matrix,
  label = train_label,
  nrounds = 50,
  objective = "multi:softmax",
  num_class = length(unique(psm_xgb$Phyla)),
  verbose = 0
)

### Predict and evaluate
preds <- predict(xgb_model, test_matrix)
confusionMatrix(factor(preds), factor(test_label))

If you have a specific hypothesis or comparison in mind, let me know and I can help you refine the analysis!
If you need help interpreting any output or want to go deeper into any step, just ask!

#### Alpha Diversity Plots with Significance Letters

```{r rp4-alpha-plots-with-letters, fig.width=12, fig.height=15, eval = FALSE}
# Create plots for all specified variables if they exist in the dataset
attach(alpha_df)
plots_list <- list()

# Define a function to add significance letters to plots
add_significance_letters <- function(data, var_name, metric, dunn_results) {
  if(is.null(dunn_results) || nrow(dunn_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Get group letters for the specific metric
  group_letters <- calculate_group_letters(dunn_results, var_name, metric)

  if(is.null(group_letters) || nrow(group_letters) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Create a mapping of group to letter
  group_to_letter <- setNames(group_letters$letter, as.character(group_letters$group))

  # Add letters to the data frame
  data_with_letters <- data
  data_with_letters$letter_labels <- ""
  for(grp in names(group_to_letter)) {
    data_with_labels_idx <- data_with_letters[[var_name]] == grp
    data_with_letters$letter_labels[data_with_labels_idx] <- group_to_letter[grp]
  }

  return(data_with_letters)
}

# Define all alpha diversity metrics to plot
alpha_metrics_to_plot <- intersect(c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1", "InvSimpson", "ACE", "Evenness", "PD", "SR", "Shannon_Effective", "Simpson_Effective"), colnames(alpha_df))

# By TreatmentCode
if("TreatmentCode.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
  # Get Dunn's test results for TreatmentCode
  treatment_dunn <- all_dunn_results[["TreatmentCode.x"]]

  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
    plot_name <- paste0("TreatmentCode_", metric)

    # Create plot with or without letters
    if(!is.null(treatment_dunn)) {
      data_with_letters <- add_significance_letters(alpha_df, "TreatmentCode.x", metric, treatment_dunn)

      if(!is.null(data_with_letters)) {
        p <- ggplot(data_with_letters, aes_string(x = "TreatmentCode.x", y = metric, fill = "TreatmentCode.x")) +
          geom_boxplot() +
          scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
          geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
          geom_text(data = data_with_letters,
                    aes_string(x = "TreatmentCode.x", y = paste0("max(", metric, ") * 1.05"), label = "letter_labels"),
                    inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 0, size = 3) +
          labs(y = metric, x = "Treatment Code") +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom",
                legend.box = "horizontal",
                axis.text.x = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
      } else {
        p <- ggboxplot(alpha_df, x = "TreatmentCode.x", y = metric,
                       fill = "TreatmentCode.x") +
          scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
          geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
          labs(y = metric, x = "Treatment Code") +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom",
                legend.box = "horizontal",
                axis.text.x = element_blank(),
                axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
      }
    } else {
      p <- ggboxplot(alpha_df, x = "TreatmentCode.x", y = metric,
                     fill = "TreatmentCode.x") +
        scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.9) +
        geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
        labs(y = metric, x = "Treatment Code") +
        theme(legend.position = "bottom",
              legend.box = "horizontal",
              axis.text.x = element_blank(),
              axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
    }

    plots_list[[plot_name]] <- p
  }
}

# By EnvZone
if("EnvZone.x" %in% colnames(alpha_df)) {
  # Get Dunn's test results for EnvZone
  envzone_dunn <- all_dunn_results[["EnvZone"]]

  for(metric in alpha_metrics_to_plot) {
```

### Kruskal-Wallis tests by all specified variables
alpha_metrics <- c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson", "Chao1", "InvSimpson")

### Function to run Kruskal-Wallis tests for a variable
run_kruskal_tests <- function(data, var_name, metrics) {
  if(!var_name %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("Variable", var_name, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  results_list <- list()

  for(metric in metrics) {
    if(!metric %in% colnames(data)) next

    formula_str <- paste(metric, "~", var_name)
    test <- kruskal.test(as.formula(formula_str), data = data)

    result_df <- data.frame(
      Metric = metric,
      Chi_squared = round(test$statistic, 3),
      df = test$parameter,
      p_value = format.pval(test$p.value, digits = 3),
      Significance = ifelse(test$p.value < 0.001, "***",
                           ifelse(test$p.value < 0.01, "**",
                                 ifelse(test$p.value < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
    )

    results_list[[metric]] <- result_df
  }

  return(do.call(rbind, results_list))
}

### Function to run Dunn's post-hoc tests for a variable
run_dunn_tests <- function(data, var_name, metrics) {
  if(!var_name %in% colnames(data)) {
    cat("Variable", var_name, "not found in dataset.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  results_list <- list()

  for(metric in metrics) {
    if(!metric %in% colnames(data)) next

    # Perform Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction
    if(require(FSA, quietly = TRUE)) {
      formula_str <- as.formula(paste(metric, "~", var_name))
      
      tryCatch({
        dunn_test <- dunnTest(formula_str, data = data, method = "bonferroni")

        # Extract results
        dunn_results <- dunn_test$res
        if(!is.null(dunn_results)) {
          dunn_results$Metric <- metric
          
          # Parse Comparison column to get group1 and group2
          if("Comparison" %in% colnames(dunn_results)) {
            split_groups <- strsplit(as.character(dunn_results$Comparison), " - ")
            dunn_results$group1 <- sapply(split_groups, function(x) x[1])
            dunn_results$group2 <- sapply(split_groups, function(x) x[2])
          }
          
          # Add significance column
          dunn_results$signif <- ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.001, "***",
                               ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.01, "**",
                                     ifelse(dunn_results$P.adj < 0.05, "*", "ns")))
          
          # Reorder columns to put Metric first
          cols_to_keep <- c("Metric", "group1", "group2", "Z", "P.unadj", "P.adj", "signif")
          cols_to_keep <- intersect(cols_to_keep, colnames(dunn_results))
          dunn_results <- dunn_results[, cols_to_keep]
          results_list[[metric]] <- dunn_results
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("Error in Dunn's test for", metric, ":", e$message, "\n")
      })
    } else {
      cat("FSA package not available for Dunn's test.\n")
      return(NULL)
    }
  }

  return(do.call(rbind, results_list))
}

### Function to calculate group letters from Dunn's test results
calculate_group_letters <- function(dunn_results, var_name, metric) {
  if(is.null(dunn_results) || nrow(dunn_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Filter results for the specific metric
  metric_results <- dunn_results[dunn_results$Metric == metric, ]

  if(nrow(metric_results) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Create comparison names for multcompLetters
  # It expects "Group1-Group2"
  comparisons <- paste(metric_results$group1, metric_results$group2, sep = "-")
  p_values <- metric_results$P.adj
  names(p_values) <- comparisons
  
  # Calculate letters using multcompView
  tryCatch({
    mcl <- multcompView::multcompLetters(p_values, threshold = 0.05)
    
    # Create result dataframe
    group_letters <- data.frame(
      group = names(mcl$Letters),
      letter = mcl$Letters,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    return(group_letters)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error calculating letters for", metric, ":", e$message, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  })
}

  # Add individual variable results as separate sheets

### rphylopic — learn by doing

This short, step-by-step notebook is structured so you can learn rphylopic by completing a few small, focused tasks. Each step has a one-line goal, a compact explanation, a minimal code example to run, and a tiny exercise to try.

Useful references

- Cheatsheet (endpoints & options): https://palaeoverse.org/images/rphylopic-cheatsheet.pdf
- Browse and preview images interactively: https://rphylopic.palaeoverse.org/?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email


#### Step 1 — Install and load (goal: have rphylopic ready)

Why: the package provides helpers to search, fetch, plot, and save silhouettes.

```{r aux1-u1, eval = FALSE}
# install if needed
# install.packages("rphylopic")
# remotes::install_github("palaeoverse/rphylopic")
library(rphylopic)
```

Try: run the chunk above. If it loads without error you're ready for Step 2.


#### Step 2 — Find candidate images (goal: get 1–5 UUIDs)

Why: many taxa have several silhouettes — pull candidates first so you can inspect them.

```{r aux1-u2, eval = FALSE}
# get one uuid
uuid <- get_uuid(name = "Canis lupus", n = 1)
# get several candidates
uuid_candidates <- get_uuid(name = "Canis lupus", n = 5)
uuid
uuid_candidates
```

Exercise: change the `name` to a taxon you study and run again.


#### Step 3 — Preview and pick (goal: choose the silhouette you want)

Why: `get_uuid()` returns ids but you often need to see the images to choose the best one. `pick_phylopic()` shows candidates and returns an image object.

```{r aux1-u3, eval = FALSE}
# interactive preview; returns chosen image object
img <- pick_phylopic(name = "Canis lupus", n = 5)
img
```

If `img` exists in your session already, you can skip this and use the existing object (the active R session often retains `img` and `uuid`).

Try: pick a different candidate (change `n`) or try a different species.


#### Step 4 — Minimal base-R plotting (goal: place a silhouette on a plot)

Why: quick way to annotate plots, create figure panels, or add biological context.

```{r aux1-u4, eval = FALSE}
plot(1:2, 1:2, type = "n", xlab = "x", ylab = "y")
# use image object
add_phylopic_base(img = img, x = 1.5, y = 1.5, height = 0.5)
# or use uuid directly
add_phylopic_base(uuid = uuid, x = 1, y = 1, height = 0.25, color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8)
```

Exercise: add two different silhouettes at different coordinates and sizes.


#### Step 5 — ggplot2 integration (goal: use silhouettes with the grammar of graphics)

Why: use `add_phylopic()` for background images or `geom_phylopic()` to use a silhouette as a point glyph.

```{r aux1-u5, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
# fetch a simple image
uuid_iris <- get_uuid(name = "Iris", n = 1)
img_iris <- get_phylopic(uuid = uuid_iris)

# background silhouette behind points
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width)) +
  add_phylopic(x = 6.1, y = 3.2, img = img_iris, alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_point()

# silhouette as glyph
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width)) +
  geom_phylopic(img = img_iris, color = "purple", height = 0.18)
```

Try: vary `alpha` and `height` to see how silhouettes integrate with plot layers.


#### Step 6 — Attribution and licensing (goal: fetch credit metadata)

Why: always inspect and include image credit when publishing.

```{r aux1-u6, eval = FALSE}
# fetch attribution for a uuid
uuid2 <- get_uuid(name = "Nycticebus", n = 1)
attr <- get_attribution(uuid = uuid2)
attr
```

Exercise: copy `attr$artist` and `attr$license` into your figure caption. (Example caption: "Silhouette credit: <artist> / <license>.")


#### Step 7 — Save and reuse (goal: export silhouettes for pipeline use)

Why: saving avoids repeated downloads and makes figures reproducible.

```{r aux1-u7, eval = FALSE}
img_save <- pick_phylopic(name = "Phascolarctos cinereus", n = 1)
save_phylopic(img = img_save) # saves to working directory
```

Tip: save into a `figures/` folder and commit the file to your project so figures render offline.


#### Quick workflow checklist

1. get_uuid(name, n = N) — gather candidates
2. pick_phylopic(...) — preview & choose
3. get_phylopic(uuid) or use returned `img`
4. add_phylopic_base() or add_phylopic()/geom_phylopic() to plot
5. get_attribution(uuid) — record artist & license
6. save_phylopic(img) — store locally


#### Small projects you can try

- Build a small panel of four silhouettes (one per corner) to annotate a 2×2 figure layout.
- Create a scatterplot where each point uses a different species silhouette (loop `geom_phylopic`).
- Produce a figure with silhouettes faded into the background and labeled with their scientific names and attribution lines.
